on behalf of the alde group. – mr president, let us recall that free movement has been one of the fundamental pillars of the single european market, which aims to achieve increased competition and larger economies of scale and confers on the eu its main power of attraction. over time, the ability of people to move freely within the eu has become not only a basic component of the internal market but a fundamental right. by removing the barriers created by different national provisions and regulations, european citizens, as well as businesses, can thrive. likewise, the possibility for eu citizens to carry their pets with them, without being subjected to specific national regulations and standards, is important, as it can significantly reduce their travel efforts and costs. i am pleased that the commission proposal points in that direction. i welcome the general-regime passport, which will harmonise the animal health measures and controls that will facilitate the free movement of pet animals. at the same time, i agree that we need to guarantee a high level of protection for human and animal health. this transitional regime will allow more time for the right infrastructure and staff to be in place. so, under this argument, parliament will certainly vote tomorrow to prolong the transitional regime for some member states until the end of 2011, as these countries allegedly need to take specific health risks into account. however, this is not the first time that some member states have been allowed to apply more stringent health requirements than others. initially, the transitional period lasted until july 2008. then the transitional period was extended to 2010. now we have agreed to a new prolongation. thus, while i have some sympathy for the fears of the member states who consider that their pet population is more prone to certain diseases, and i understand that the proposed prolongation would be simultaneously completed with eu-funded vaccination programmes to eliminate sylvatic rabies in some member states, i believe that this should be the last extension of the special treatment enjoyed by these countries. we all know that asymmetrical measures and opt-outs will not bring the full benefits of the internal market in this area. so let us all agree that this transitional regime needs to be eliminated and that a level playing field has to be ensured as soon as possible. interestingly enough, the more contentious issue in this report has not been the content that has sparked heated debate among us on how to apply the new lisbon treaty provisions regarding the comitology procedure. this is the first codecision file where these provisions are to be put into practice. given parliament’s extended powers under the new treaty, it was crucial for us that this particular regulation did not set a precedent for future decisions. in this regard i welcome the written statement which was agreed between parliament and the council during the trialogue, stating that this file should not be treated as a precedent.
first of all, i would like to congratulate the rapporteur on her work and all those who made this compromise possible. i am pleased that the report allows member states to continue protective measures against the spread of rabies but also that it will lead to the free and safe movement of pet animals in the european area after 2011. i think that a good compromise has been reached, which provides for an effective response if member states justify their concerns about the spread of diseases and provides a guarantee that when the delegated power is used, the commission will consult a range of experts - commission experts, member states' experts, experts from non-governmental organisations or experts from parliaments. in a broader context, we have received written assurances that this report will not set a precedent for the future use of the delegated powers. in this way, parliament's concerns about setting a precedent for the new comitology procedure under the lisbon treaty will be taken into account.
the package travel directive covers transport, accommodation and other related services provided by package travel and sets out the rights of consumers and the responsibilities of distributors and suppliers of package travel services. the 1990 directive does not take account of new developments such as the purchase of package holidays and payments made via the internet. the increase in internet use and the emergence of low-cost operators has led 23% of european tourists and 20% of european households to purchase their package holidays personally via dedicated websites. the directive should therefore be revised to include dynamic package travel providers. the consumer must be fully informed of his rights and how they are guaranteed by each of the offers available, both for the package as a whole and for each component. i also think it is important that websites offering tourism services are certified. this will ensure that the identity of the tourist service provider is known and, consequently, that there is a clear assumption of responsibility for the information and services provided. the study published in january 2009 by the commission on package holidays organised at the request of the customer, the so-called 'dynamic packages', shows that the share of packages purchased by electronic means increased by 12% in 2009, although their value represents only 25% of the total value of the tourist services sold. 66% of online purchases are direct purchases via the websites of airlines, travel agencies or specialised websites that present last-minute travel deals. tourists prefer dynamic packages because they offer more flexibility, lower prices compared to traditional packages, better quality of service or because they cannot find traditional packages that meet their requirements. furthermore, payment for purchased dynamic bundles can only be made by electronic means of payment. however, about 70% of complaints received last year by the european consumer centres network were related to travel services and were due to incorrect and incomplete pre- and in-trip information, substandard services, flight cancellations or delays and even non-delivery of services purchased. so i think it is important and timely that this directive be revised. thank you, sir.
i don't think that the introduction of a financial transaction tax is helping anything. it doesn't help to get out of the financial crisis, it doesn't help to prevent another crisis, and it doesn't help to stabilize financial markets. this would only increase the cost of capital and credit and would be a brake on investment. before introducing a new tax, the european commission must carefully consider the advantages and disadvantages of the tax. if a decision is taken to introduce a financial transaction tax, the competitiveness of the european economy at world level may be affected. double taxation and obstacles to the free movement of capital must also be avoided. the costs of such a tax should not be borne by the citizens. for countries where speculative capital accumulations take place, leading to the creation of short-term external debt, it would be appropriate to consider the introduction of such a tax. it could prevent the accumulation of speculative capital. sweden introduced in 2009 an annual stability levy on banks and credit institutions of 0,036% of total certain liabilities. however, the implementation of such a tax is not justified in romania. in the context of the negotiations between the romanian government, the imf and the european commission, legislative amendments were agreed on the special administration procedure, which would allow the bnr to intervene quickly and efficiently in the case of a credit institution in difficulty. in this context, i would like to ask the european commission what mechanisms or formulas are envisaged to protect countries against the accumulation of speculative capital and whether it is also considering other measures to regulate and supervise the financial system. thank you, sir.

the reporter. − i would like to thank first of all those with whom i had the opportunity to work on the solvit report, the imco secretariat, all the shadow rapporteurs, and the other colleagues who have shown their interest in this dossier and who have made an important contribution to the final result. solvit is a network that provides informal solutions to problems that may arise from the improper implementation of internal market legislation. it is a very useful innovation for european consumers and businesses in the european union to reap the benefits of european legislation. we often have problems with the implementation of european internal market legislation, and solvit seems to me a viable alternative to the judicial path, as the courts are already overwhelmed with all kinds of different cases. we cannot ignore the fact that solvit is facing a steadily increasing number of cases and that in this respect it is, in some ways, a victim of its own success. in order for solvit to provide quality assistance to citizens and businesses in the european union, it is necessary to supplement the solvit centres that do not have the necessary staff. supplementation must be done in a rational and controlled way, taking into account the population of the country and the previous number of cases the center has dealt with in the past. this analysis must be done to supplement staff, exclusively where it is really needed. of course, adding solvit staff comes with costs. the report calls on member states to use all available means to finance the additional staff, including alternative financing arrangements. another focus of this report is the promotion of the solvit network, which i personally - and i think you all agree with me - consider to be of major importance. by using solvit, smes can save significant amounts of money to invest in other growth-generating areas that are more useful for their development than the legal assistance they would need to solve problems, and for individual consumers, solvit gives them the advantage of avoiding long and costly legal proceedings. however, to benefit from solvit, citizens and businesses must first know how effective the network is. that is why i think we should have an active involvement, both of the national authorities and of the european commission and of the members of this parliament, in promoting solvit. the means are many: from the media to information campaigns organised by the member states, to the creation of a single solvit portal. public services responsible for implementing european legislation in the field of the internal market could also appoint a solvit communication officer, which would again increase the efficiency of the network and help to promote it. as meps, we can take the initiative to promote solvit ourselves and help raise awareness among our colleagues at national parliamentary level. the exchange of good practice between member states in promoting solvit and solving problems in the operation of the network is another element that this report strongly encourages. this way, good ideas can be disseminated and applied at european level to the benefit of all. finally, we cannot ignore the fact that sometimes solvit is faced with numerous cases that are outside its competence or that are particularly complex, requiring solutions by other means. petitions to the european parliament's committee on petitions can be a solution for those cases that are too complex to be solved at solvit level. one of the proposals in this report is therefore that the solvit portal should link to the website of the european parliament's committee on petitions and to the specialised committees of the national parliaments. these are just some of the ideas on which the solvit report is based. i believe that these proposals have the potential to improve the functioning of the network, with a view to providing quality assistance to consumers and businesses. solvit has enormous potential, but we need to continuously analyse its performance to maximise its potential.
it is a fundamental right of european citizens in the single market that when they want to buy a product or service, regardless of which member state they are in, they should benefit from the same prices or fees and, where differences exist, be able to explain them. i think we need to look more at the problems in banking and financial services, because today in the single market there are big differences in the fees charged in these services. if you are in romania, for example, and you want to use a banking service provided by banks the same banks operating in romania, france, italy and austria , in romania you pay more and much higher fees. such a situation is not right and i believe that the hope of the citizens, not only in romania but also in other member states, that the european institutions will play a more active role in clarifying these differences is justified. again, this is about commissions, not bank interest. thank you, sir.
the reporter. − i thank commissioner barnier and his colleagues for their positive comments on my first report and on the solvit network itself. i believe that solvit is a practical solution for consumers and therefore i believe that it should be improved and promoted by us and by the member states, so that as many european citizens as possible know about solvit and can defend their rights by using solvit assistance. i think that the result we have achieved, both in the committee on the internal market and consumer protection and in the committee on petitions, is satisfactory. solvit is already a well-functioning network, but we need solutions to some of the difficulties faced by both solvit users and solvit staff. the report contains some of these solutions, but others have been discussed in this debate. in addition to the need for more staff in some solvit centres, for solvit to be effective, staff must be suitably qualified and trained in the internal market rules. it is equally important that solvit staff can benefit from legal assistance, both from civil servants and from the european commission, given the complexity of the cases that come to solvit's attention. sometimes the european commission responds late to legal assistance requests from solvit staff, which leads to some delays in the entire case resolution process. i thank commissioner barnier for his commitment to the european parliament to make the existence of the website http://www.solvit.eu possible as soon as possible.' i strongly believe, ladies and gentlemen, that this report is an important step towards improving the functioning of solvit and i therefore ask all the groups to vote in favour of this report. thank you, sir.

in writing. i support the efforts made in this report to achieve the extension of freedom of movement for long-stay visa holders to those of short-stay permits and visas. the current arrangements have created many inconveniences for third-country nationals who are legally resident in one of the member states and who wish to travel throughout the european union for various reasons. there are discrepancies between member states as regards the timing, methodology and criteria for issuing visas. in practice, it has been observed that visa applicants rejected by one member state 'try their luck' in other member states. this is because some countries are more demanding, while others are more permissive when it comes to issuing visas and residence permits. in order to avoid creating an influx of visa applications through certain states adopting a more liberal granting policy, i propose to standardise the controls and approval of visa applications between all member states. this will ensure a uniform approach to all applications, thus eliminating the risk of 'gateways' in the schengen area.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on mobilising the egf to support the 2 476 people made redundant in the automotive sector in germany. the unemployment periods will be used by the german authorities to raise the general level of skills, not only for vocational training and higher education, but also to enable migrant or low-skilled workers to acquire basic skills for reintegration into the labour market. at european level, in the machine-building industry, we are faced with such situations in sweden, where 2 258 workers were made redundant, in austria 744 redundancies were made in enterprises producing cars, trailers and semi-trailers, and in belgium the industry made over 2 500 redundancies. in europe, over 8,000 jobs will be lost due to the restructuring of the machine-building industry. financial assistance for displaced workers should be made available as quickly and efficiently as possible, but this is a short-term measure which does not solve the problem of job loss. the eu also needs a strong industrial policy in the machine-building industry to preserve existing jobs and even create new ones.
in writing. − in september 2009, lithuania submitted an application for assistance for the use of the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) relating to redundancies in 128 enterprises in the building sector. i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the mobilisation of the egf for building construction in lithuania. i believe that the eco-efficient economy and the construction of energy-efficient buildings can contribute to the economic recovery of the eu. it is estimated that these sectors can create around 2 million jobs at european level by 2020. in 2006, the construction sector had some 2.9 million enterprises generating €510 billion and employing 14.1 million people across the eu-27. as a result of the economic and financial crisis, in lithuania at the beginning of 2009 the volume of construction activity decreased by 42,81% and 48,04% respectively compared to the first part of 2008. this has a negative impact on lithuania, as it has one of the highest unemployment rates in the eu. the construction sector has been particularly affected, losing almost 10% of lithuanian jobs in 2008 alone.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report to help bring the additional protocol to the lisbon agreement into force. this agreement creates a mechanism to ensure cooperation between the contracting parties in the event of pollution accidents and obliges them to establish and implement their own emergency structures and plans. this agreement is part of a network of regional maritime agreements that the eu has concluded with certain individual member states and neighbouring third countries. the network is made up of the helsinki convention, the bonn agreement, the barcelona convention and, in this case, the lisbon agreement, each covering different parts of the sea around eu countries and aiming at the individual or collective intervention of the contracting parties in cases of pollution or threat of pollution of the seas or coasts, to protect the environment and the health of citizens.
in writing. − the european union's internal market has expanded substantially in recent years and now has almost 500 million consumers in 27 countries. a harmonisation of consumer protection principles and rules throughout the european union and an improvement in their enforcement mechanisms is an achievable objective, without the expectation that the supply of products and services in all 27 countries will reach the same quality in the short or medium term. the current difficult economic situation in europe is manifested in a reduction in incomes and an increase in unemployment, which translates, at community level, into a real need for better management of the daily basket. the attitude of the european consumer, who is directly affected by the economic downturn, is particularly evident in the goods and services he buys and wants to have in good quality so that he can make the most of them. consumer protection measures are therefore becoming increasingly important. strengthening market surveillance structures in all member states to ensure that products placed on the market meet the highest safety standards is a solution to the current state of affairs.

in writing. − the internal market offers citizens and businesses many opportunities. the internal market generally works well, but sometimes mistakes can be made. solvit is a problem-solving network in which eu member states work together to solve problems arising from the misapplication of internal market legislation by public authorities without resorting to legal proceedings. in each member state of the european union (as well as in norway, iceland and lichtenstein) there is a solvit centre. we voted for this report to give solvit a boost in dealing with complaints from both citizens and businesses.

acting president of the council. - mr president, i am going to answer the questions put by mrs flašíková beňová and mrs flautre on a matter which directly affects human rights, which affects all of us and which affects a large part of the population. because the roma population, as is well known, is the first ethnic minority to live in the european union, and not exactly at the same level as the average citizen of the union. to be specific in relation to the questions you have asked me, there is one that deals with the application of the structural funds in this area and i must tell you that the conclusions which the spanish presidency intends to adopt in the council include these ten basic principles, among which is the revision or modification of the current operational programmes of the structural funds, as well as the future regulations from 2014. we insist that the structural funds be used to the full to promote the integration of the roma population and, in particular, we propose that comprehensive actions be launched in both rural and urban areas, starting with the recent amendment of article 7 of the erdf. the aim is to promote roma communities in an integrated way by improving their housing and living conditions. the second question concerns the action of local authorities. we believe that in order to make the structural funds accessible to the roma population, it is necessary that local authorities and roma organisations, including the roma population itself, are actively involved in all stages of the process, i.e. planning, management, monitoring and evaluation of european funds. the council will also propose in its conclusions that the european commission provide technical support and guidance to member states and local authorities, and that horizontal coordination between states and vertical coordination between the european, national, regional and local levels be facilitated. a third question is whether the presidency trio has a strategic proposal, a strategic agenda, in this respect. i have to tell you that the programme of the trio of presidencies explicitly mentions the social and economic integration of the roma. it is a phrase which is in the programme adopted unanimously by the general affairs council and which therefore corresponds to the strategy for the next year and a half, which is the period covered by the programme of the trio of presidencies. we understand that short-term and long-term measures must be taken. in the short term we must give priority to the instruments i have mentioned above and also adopt a work plan to deal immediately with problems such as pupils attending special schools, in some cases predominantly, or only, for roma - with which there is therefore an obvious disagreement - or problems relating to housing - of which we have spoken before - as well as in the field of health and access to employment, to correct inequalities. and in the long term we also want to see a horizontal approach, mainstreaming, of roma issues in all european union policies, and this must be done within the framework of the so-called open method of coordination and in areas such as fundamental rights, the fight against discrimination, regional development, education, access to public jobs and public services. and finally, as regards non-discrimination, it is well known that the spanish presidency is trying to promote, during its six-month term, and the presidency trio too, the adoption of a directive which has been unable to be adopted for some time in the european union, without reaching its final conclusions, which is the comprehensive directive on combating discrimination and equal treatment, which is essential precisely for those groups who suffer particularly from discrimination and, therefore, specifically, the roma community.
vice-president of the commission. − mr president, i would like to thank mr swoboda and his colleagues for tabling this oral question on the european roma summit. it allows the commission to express its commitment to ensuring the protection of fundamental rights, on the one hand, and full social and economic integration into our societies on the other. we have just heard the council making a real plea about the way the member states have to go ahead by putting this in the mainstream of their policies. as you know, this debate is taking place just some weeks before the second roma summit, which will be hosted in córdoba by the spanish presidency on 8 and 9 april. the commission welcomes and actively supports this initiative. i think this initiative will be a welcome moment to take stock of developments at national, european and international level since 2008. it will then help us to contribute to a common perspective for the future. two years ago the first summit was held. how far have we got? you can see a glass as being half full or half empty. of course there have been significant improvements but there are also significant gaps. your question rightly highlights the central role of the european union’s instruments and policies and the importance of strengthening cooperation between all the key actors – member states, institutions at european level, international organisations and civil society. the commission is committed to enforcing a directive which prohibits discrimination on the grounds of race and ethnic origin, and roma discrimination is fully covered by this directive. we now have legislation at european level and the framework decision on racism and xenophobia, which will be a key tool to tackle the racism that roma people suffer from. by november of this year, all member states should put into place criminal penalties for racist and xenophobic crimes, as laid down in the framework decision. as i have already announced, i am committed to monitoring the implementation of this framework decision as closely as possible. the commission is fully aware that this is not enough and that strong legislation needs to be complemented by information and awareness-raising about rights and obligations. to this end, the commission is addressing roma issues in the context of the eu campaign ‘for diversity. against discrimination’ and in specific training for legal practitioners. quite rightly, the structural funds, the rural development funds and the instruments for pre-accession were underlined as being important levers for change because they allow member states to implement ambitious programmes which are targeted to the roma. it is evident that these programmes must be very down to earth and pragmatic, based on evidence and must approach the living conditions of the roma in all their complexity. this is not an issue that can be solved by a simple slogan. it needs a lot of concrete work. that is why the commission is encouraging member states to use the full potential of these funds to support roma inclusion. to this end, we have launched a series of high-level bilateral visits to member states with significant roma populations. they should lead the concrete commitments with agreed targets. the first event took place in october 2009 in hungary with the full cooperation of the government. others will be organised in the future. another concrete example of the commission’s commitment to using the structural funds for tackling roma exclusion is the amendment that has been proposed to article 7(2) of the regulation on the european regional development fund. a very large majority in this house voted for the report by your colleague, mr van nistelrooij, at the beginning of last month: a measure which opens new policy and funding opportunities for housing for the benefit of marginalised communities where we can target the roma specifically, although not exclusively. finally, thanks to the european parliament, there are the pilot projects on roma inclusion, with a budget of eur 5 million over two years. this pilot project addresses early childhood education, self-employment through micro credits and public awareness. the evaluation of this pilot project will be carried out jointly by the undp and the world bank. i am very much looking forward to this evaluation because the evaluation will bring us the information about what we have done well and where the deficiencies are so that we can build on this in order to go ahead with a very targeted action afterwards. the european platform for roma inclusion was launched as a joint initiative of the commission and the czech presidency in april 2009. its objective is to bring together relevant actors at european, national and international level, as well as actors from civil society, and make existing policies altogether much more coherent. this platform has led to the elaboration of the common basic principles for roma inclusion, which is annexed to the council conclusions on roma inclusion adopted in june of last year. these conclusions call upon the commission to take the 10 common basic principles for roma inclusion into account when designing and implementing policies. further meetings of the platform are expected to take place under the spanish presidency and the belgian presidency so it is not a one-off action but it is followed up. i very much welcome the strong commitment of the trio of presidencies on this objective because we need to play into each other’s hands so that progress can be made. the commission will continue to contribute to the trio’s actions through its policies and instruments, in close partnership of course with member states and civil society. ahead of the roma summit, i would like to inform this house that my colleague commissioner andor and i will publish a communication on the social inclusion of the roma people, looking at the challenges ahead and outlining the eu’s contribution to meeting this challenge. this communication will then be the basis of the discussion in córdoba.
on behalf of the alde group. – mr president, in view of the second roma summit i would like to share with you a couple of ideas, in the hope that they will take effect as soon as possible. firstly, i strongly believe we need a broad and coherent strategy on roma inclusion and we also need an action plan with clear benchmarks and appropriate budgeting. in my view, it should be a strategy not only for the eu member states, but also for other countries where roma communities live and which are either in the enlargement process or in the neighbourhood policy, thus allowing the eu to use the most appropriate tools available to it on roma policies. secondly, i am convinced that we must apply the lessons learned from the gender equality policy, namely mainstreaming. ‘roma mainstreaming’ should become the working approach of all eu institutions. thirdly, when it comes to the expertise on roma we should consider some affirmative actions, especially hiring roma experts in the council, the commission and parliament. it is on this note that i have prepared letters to president van rompuy and president barroso recommending them to lead by example and hire roma advisors.
as one of the largest and most vulnerable minorities in europe, roma need to be an even more active topic on the european agenda. unemployment, poverty, abuse, discrimination and, not least, poor access to education are common problems faced by the roma minority, which ultimately lead to social exclusion. i believe that an integrated programme at european level is needed, which corresponds to their culture and values, given their free movement. children make up 46% of the roma population, due to the compound effect of high birth rates and, unfortunately, low life expectancy. a real opportunity for them would be access to education. although access to and the right to education are guaranteed by european standards, most children from poor roma communities do not attend school at all or drop out. a concrete step would be to include these children and young people in the full compulsory education system, thus preventing early school leaving. in the 2009-2010 school year, the romanian ministry of education allocated 7 483 special places in high schools across the country, with only 2 460 pupils enrolled, of whom 2 246 were admitted. but the effort must be on both sides. to improve their living standards, the roma minority must act responsibly. lack of education excludes active participation in the social, economic or political life of the country in which the roma live. the european union supports the integration of roma into society through various funding programmes, such as the european social fund, the european regional development fund, the progress and 'youth in action' programmes. thank you, sir.
the economic and social development of the roma minority group is one of the most sensitive and controversial issues facing the countries of central and eastern europe. we do not have exact estimates of the actual number of roma in the eu, but what we do know is that the roma minority is the largest and poorest transnational ethnic minority. the european union needs a coherent long-term approach, because national policies are not enough to change the situation of roma. the responsibility for improving the living conditions of the roma population lies with each state, but the success of this process lies largely in addressing the phenomenon in its entirety through coordinated action. the lack of perspective of the younger generation is, in my opinion, one of the biggest problems we face. the roma population is a young population, with a significant proportion under the age of 20. in the knowledge-based and innovative society that europe wants to develop, if we do not take immediate action, the gap between young roma and the rest of the population will widen. children and young people are included in few current policies and strategies, although the large number of children and young people in the roma population allows them to play the role of the generation of change. the process of sustainable development must start with a generation of children who have access to education, health care and all the opportunities enjoyed by children in the majority population. i would therefore like to point out that the commission's proposal for the eu 2020 strategy does not contain any objectives on how to solve the problems of the roma community. if we do not take concrete action, if we do not make major changes in our approach, millions of young roma will continue to face social exclusion and marginalisation throughout their lives. the lack of hope will make these communities unsafe for their residents and for the rest of the population. we need to give the roma community a real chance to change their perspective. at the heart of the european project is solidarity as a fundamental value, which is why we must move from the political will to take action to the concrete implementation of it.
i would like to express my hope from the outset that the roma summit in cordoba will be the decisive moment for the adoption of a common strategy for roma inclusion. the living conditions of this community remain poor and discrimination against them is deepening, despite the fact that the amounts allocated in recent years for projects dedicated to improving the situation are close to half a billion euros. i think it's time we move from good intentions to action. unfortunately, the european commission has not yet shown the will to coordinate actions to improve the living standards and social integration of roma, and to combat racist actions against them. i think it is necessary to make the roma problem a specific, well-defined task for the commissioner for social affairs, and it would be very useful to include roma specialists among the commission's experts in charge of this issue. i also believe that we need a social as well as a cultural approach, so as not to deepen the existing inequalities in both literacy and employment. in this context, i ask the commission to encourage programmes for access to the labour market for migrant roma, cooperation between local authorities and roma communities and to consider closer collaboration with non-governmental organisations.
indeed, the first european union roma summit marked the recognition of the individual failure of european states to ensure roma rights and integration and was a first step towards a common and long-term strategy at union level. unfortunately, there is a massive gap between the plans and studies and their implementation in order to visibly improve the lives of the roma community, which remains the most vulnerable ethnic group in europe, facing the highest levels of poverty and social exclusion. and the prospects are not good, considering that about half of the roma population is made up of minors, due to high birth rates and low life expectancy. i believe that the first step in a coherent inclusion strategy must be to ensure non-discriminatory access to education for the younger generation of roma, who alone can play the decisive role of change agent, for integration into the labour market and for breaking the vicious circle of social exclusion.
the roma constitute a crossborder ethno-cultural community of over 10 million people across europe. the social problem of the roma requires concerted, long-term action involving the european union and the member states. important initiatives have been taken in this area, but i think we need to go further. we need to adopt a genuine european roma strategy with well-targeted actions and regular impact assessments. i come from a country with a large roma community and i welcome the fact that today we recognise the roma problem as a problem of europe as a whole. in romania, a strategy for improving the situation of roma has been applied since the pre-accession period. they are given special places at public universities free of charge, which contributes substantially to the increase in the level of education and culture among this community. national and local public authorities are working to promote roma social inclusion and integration into the labour market, to combat extreme poverty and to improve access to health services. but it needs strong european financial support to achieve the desired results.
in writing. statistics show that unfortunately roma are the most hated and discriminated ethnic minority in europe. we have seen the difficulties that several member states, including myself, have concerning the social inclusion of the roma. this clearly shows that this is a broader european issue that we must handle together. better access to education and employment, is crucial so that we avoid the tendency of roma to choose other more easier but harmful ways of making money. we need to fully apply the anti-discrimination legislation to roma people and to take further initiatives to integrate them in our society. so far we haven't had any coherent strategy. i wish that this second european rome summit brings about a real eu strategy for rome. structural and pre-accession funds should be more efficiently used to finance such initiatives. i would also like to stress that this strategy should be a tool of coordination and an impetus for the member states. the initiatives have to be taken at local level and benefit from the expertise of local ngos and roma themselves who know what the main difficulties are, so that this strategy really meets roma people's needs.
in writing. – the roma continue to be one of the most disadvantaged minorities in all of europe, subject to widespread discrimination in all spheres of life. in the last decade, the european union and its member states have devoted attention and resources to improving the situation of the roma. working in cooperation with the roma rights movement, some member states have begun to implement policies aimed at ensuring equal access to quality education for roma children. continuing efforts in this area should remain the highest priority in the coming years. policies need to be comprehensive in order to achieve a maximum systemic impact in closing the gap between roma and non-roma in all areas: education, employment, housing and health. the european union and member states should continue to evaluate their roma-related policies to date and seek ways to eliminate any paternalistic approaches to the roma issue, which treat the roma as dependent, passive recipients of policy benefits. a traineeship scheme should also be set up for young roma to build up their professional expertise through programmes in commission departments and appropriate government institutions.
in writing. we are halfway through the decade devoted to roma inclusion ((2005-2015), and we find that much is said about the roma minority, various programmes and platforms are created, but results are limited. problems related to education, employment, regional development, etc., are persistent and are becoming more acute in some member states. the second roma summit in cordoba this year is intended to reinvigorate the european perspective and find new directions for action. i agree with the need to redefine the principles, but i think we should rather build a transversal, horizontal strategy that addresses the problems of this minority in an integrated way and not exclusively. the most important thing is that the pre-accession funds and structural funds are used correctly and produce the results we want, both for us, the policy-makers, and for civil society and, in particular, the roma minority.
in writing. the first roma summit had at least one positive consequence: the conclusion at community level that roma need education as a first step towards social integration. in this context, i also welcome the second meeting of the european platform for roma inclusion, dedicated exclusively to the education of this ethnic group in europe. in their process of educational reform, it is necessary to involve not only state institutions but also non-governmental organizations whose primary objective should no longer be the identification of acts of discrimination, but the education of ethnicity. reducing illiteracy, completing education and the need for vocational qualification and retraining are opportunities for access to the labour market and for social inclusion. it is clear that we urgently need a positive development in this minority, and this is the responsibility of both the authorities and the roma community itself. the second roma summit should motivate the european commission sufficiently to come up with legislative proposals with a view to achieving visible results. the european commission should also review the social fund and propose an increase in funding for projects aimed at improving the socioeconomic situation of the largest minority in the european union.
in writing. although member states have invested considerable eu and national resources in putting permanently unemployed roma back to work, there is no coherent solution at eu level: member states are faced with the situation in very different ways and to very different degrees. i believe it is important that we can develop a coherent and effective strategy for the roma issue, which is still unresolved and is a common problem for the european union as a legal entity and for the member states. the main topic of the european roma summit scheduled for 8 april in cordoba should be the formulation of the principles of a strategy at european level, so that the roma problem can no longer be "moved", but rather solved by each member state itself, on the basis of a common european strategy. i believe that education is the key to this. i believe that a comprehensive package of programmes is needed to encourage and motivate young roma intellectuals to return to the community and to work within and for the community. this can be greatly helped by the development of a close partnership between the various roma interest organisations, the responsible public institutions, civil society and the cooperating eu institutions. the role of preferential microcredit or government interest reimbursement methods should be enhanced. in the concept of agricultural aid, it is important to consider the objective of enabling roma communities to achieve the conditions that ensure their livelihood. the situation is worse than you might think: long-term unemployment rates have skyrocketed among them, and more and more are being marginalized.

in writing. - the overwhelming adoption of the report shows the care we need to take for small and medium-sized enterprises. currently, 5.4 million microenterprises are subject to the obligation to prepare annual reports, although their scope is limited to a particular local area or region. as there are no cross-border or even national activities, the reporting obligation only creates unnecessary administrative burdens, thus burdening the expenses of these companies (approximately eur 1 170). the report therefore recommends that member states exempt from annual reporting obligations companies that meet two of the following criteria to be considered micro-enterprises: total assets of less than eur 500 000, net turnover of less than eur 1 million and/or an average of 10 employees during the financial year. of course, micro-enterprises will continue to keep accounting records in accordance with the national law of each member state. in the current crisis situation in europe, the private environment of small and medium-sized enterprises (including micro-enterprises) must be encouraged, and seen in this unfortunate context also as an area for absorbing the workforce laid off by the state or private-corporate sector.

in writing. − the eu 2020 strategy must respond to the problems generated by the economic and financial crisis through measures that directly target the hotspots of member states' economies. if the lisbon strategy has not been a complete success because it has set too many targets, a recovery strategy must focus on a few clear and quantifiable objectives, for example: providing solutions to effectively tackle unemployment - especially among young people, promoting and supporting small and medium-sized enterprises - which create the most jobs and innovations, and increasing the share of the eu budget and national budgets allocated to research and development to 3%. we must realise that the room for manoeuvre for social policies in europe will be reduced in the future because of an ageing population, and that productivity growth can only come from greater investment in technology and education. if we want a more competitive labour market, we will have to restructure social security systems and support more flexible working arrangements. at the same time, such a strategy should support the development of production methods that respect the environment and human health.
in writing. − that strategy 2020 is neither green enough nor social enough is a reality we have all seen. that the objectives are vague and the economic crisis is not being addressed in proportion to its severity is also a pertinent observation. the resolution adopted by the ep plenary therefore has the role of making important additions to the european vision for the next 10 years. although our role as members of parliament is limited by the letter of the treaty, our contribution can be substantial. we must, however, wait for the member states to show political will and reflect on our position constructively. objectives such as 'a social market economy' and 'a budget reflecting smart, inclusive and sustainable growth' are key to overcoming the effects of the economic crisis. investing in education, encouraging student mobility and developing new skills to meet labour market demands are areas for action where we need to build realistic action plans.

in writing. - i have read both the report of judge richard goldstone and the conclusions of ambassador dora gold, which debunk many of the arguments of the report of the un commission headed by judge goldstone. in comparing them, i noted the subjectivity of the goldstone report and therefore did not support the resolution on the application of the recommendations of the goldstone report on israel and palestine. the analysis of the facts must be made in a transparent and impartial manner to both sides of the conflict. the goldstone report fails to mention the cause that triggered the israeli operation in gaza: the almost 12,000 rocket and mortar attacks on israeli civilians. after the withdrawal of israeli forces from gaza, the number of rocket attacks increased by 500%. while there were 281 and 179 rocket attacks on israeli territory in 2004 and 2005, after the withdrawal from gaza (in september 2005), the number of attacks increased to 946 in 2006, 783 in 2007 and 1 730 in 2008. no member country of the european union voted in favour of adopting the goldstone report at the united nations human rights council. respect for international law must be a priority for all parties involved.
in writing. the current motion for a resolution, which follows the g20 discussions at the pittsburgh summit and the call of international bodies such as the imf, may be a solution both to avoid further financial catastrophes and to recover the sums that the treasuries have made available to banks to save them from collapse. it is welcome that such legislation has been pioneered in france and belgium (the uk is also considering introducing similar legislation), and we look forward to seeing its effects. according to french estimates, a 0.005% tax will take over 20 billion euros out of the pockets of french banks. however, will the banking community react by limiting the number of speculative transactions - considered harmful - or will it take advantage of the mobility of capital and continue to conduct such transactions through bank branches in countries where this type of tax does not exist? so i think that the success of such a taxation requires a global approach, including bringing it before international bodies like the un. even so, it is hard to believe that joint global action can be achieved (see offshore legislation).

author. − mr president, after 13 years without an execution in south korea, it is deeply sad that the constitutional court there ruled in favour of the death penalty a few weeks ago. the ruling states that the death penalty is a legal punishment that can deter crime for the public good. that is a commonly heard argument and merely a response to emotive situations in a given country at a certain time. it in fact means that the death penalty is being viewed as a preventive force in the hope that, when a criminal knows there is capital punishment, he or she will think twice about his or her acts. we all know that many studies have refuted that idea. even more important is the fact that an execution is irreversible; there is no way back. roman law at the time of justinian stated that it was better for a guilty person to go unpunished than for an innocent person to be deprived of their life. that was 15 centuries ago. since the south korean constitutional court itself recognised that the death penalty could be subject to errors and abuse, our concerns brought forward today might strengthen the democratic institutions of the republic of korea in the idea that this method of punishment should be abolished for good. since the republic of south korea acceded to the international covenant on civil and political rights in 1990, and is a signatory to most of the major human rights treaties, moving backwards would be very harmful to its international reputation.
in writing. – ‘every person shall have the right to life. if not, the killer unwittingly achieves a final and perverse moral victory by making the state a killer too, thus reducing social abhorrence at the conscious extinction of human beings’ (amnesty international, 1998). morality, deterrence and fairness are key in the debate on the death penalty. the ‘crime control’ approach seeks repression of criminal conduct, while the ‘human rights/due process’ model emphasises individual rights. the former considers the death penalty moral because the defendant took a life (retribution), a deterrent because those who might kill refrain from doing so fearing for their life, while fairness is unimportant or unproven. the latter model claims that death penalty is immoral because the state should not take a life, is not a deterrent – as shown by statistics – and is unfairly administered, sometimes people on death row being innocent and their trials involving irregularities. i believe in the human rights model, as reflected by the international community in hard and soft law, and by the increasing number of countries abolishing the death penalty. i urge the republic of korea to show a clear political will abolishing the death penalty, and, until then, to immediately adopt a moratorium on its application.
in writing. the eu guidelines on the death penalty date from 1998. also in that year, an unofficial moratorium on the death penalty began in south korea. in the meantime, the south korean parliament has discussed three proposals to outlaw the death penalty. last month, the constitutional court of this country by a narrow majority reaffirmed the constitutionality of the death penalty. i deplore this decision and hope that parliament will introduce a resolution to ban the death penalty. south korea's passage into the abolitionist ranks would send a strong signal to the entire asian continent.
the council of the european union welcomed the commission communication on europe 20-20. it is true, it is a very necessary document, but that is precisely why we must look at its contents very carefully. i think it lacks financial consistency. the council is required to ask the commission to clarify budgetary resources and their allocation to the key components of the budget. my view is that the budget cannot be drawn up before the reform of the common agricultural policy and the reform of cohesion policy. one of the major areas of development and stability in the union, namely infrastructure, both transport and energy, is completely lacking. developing transport and energy infrastructure in the european union and aligning it with neighbouring countries can be a powerful driver for sustainable growth and stable jobs, and can provide the european union with much-needed security in both energy and transport. i therefore call on the council to ask the commission to introduce these key areas in the eu 2020 strategy in the interest of european citizens.
in writing. one of the important items on the european council agenda concerns the eu 2020 strategy for jobs and growth. we need european policy coordination to respond to the challenges and needs of the moment, and to set clear long-term objectives. the sustainable development of the european economy must be a priority. the commission's new strategy for the next 10 years has five lines of action: creating new jobs, fighting poverty, reducing school drop-outs, investing in research and development and reducing greenhouse gas emissions. the latest eu member states need the union's resources and support to achieve these ambitious goals. romania supports the 20-20-20 target of reducing carbon emissions by 20%, increasing the share of energy from renewable resources by 20% and increasing energy efficiency by 20%. a more ambitious 30-30-30 target that envisages reaching a 30% threshold in all three areas would be far too costly for my country. this would be an unrealistic target for many european countries.
in writing. in this period of economic and social crisis, coupled with the climate crisis, the eu has set out a new strategy for the next 10 years. the eu 2020 strategy must contribute to creating a more inclusive europe with an integrated and environmentally friendly economy. developing research and innovation must become a priority to combat the effects of climate change, to create green, smart jobs. the objectives set must therefore be binding in order to ensure sustainable growth, the development of a more inclusive labour market and decent living conditions for all citizens.
in writing. the spring european council has as its main theme the eu2020 strategy. earlier this year, the unemployment rate reached 10 percent, and in countries like spain and latvia, it was almost 20 percent. 67% of europeans consider job loss to be their main concern. the main concern of european leaders must be to preserve existing jobs and create new ones that will enable european citizens to live a decent life. this can only be achieved through substantial investment in economic and social development, transport and energy infrastructure, agriculture, research, education and health. this is why the european council must pay particular attention to the union's industrial policy. according to european statistics, industrial production fell by 2% in the euro area and by 0.2% in the eu27 in january 2010 compared to december 2009. at community level, industry generates 26.4% of gdp, but there are member states where industrial production contributes only 14% of gdp. the union must remain globally competitive and this requires that jobs and industrial production be kept within the union and not relocated to third countries.

the possibility of a european citizens' initiative can help to generate public debate on european issues, leading to a genuine european public. representatives of civil society can channel in social issues that the parties present in the ep are unable or unwilling to raise. i would like to raise one of the issues that arise. i consider it important that the commission, in parallel with the prior notification of the proposed initiative, before the start of the collection of signatures or after a certain number of signatures have been collected, should give its opinion on the admissibility of the initiative in question on the basis of community law and its own competence. after a million signatures have been collected, a refusal on formal grounds or for lack of a legal basis could cast a very unfavourable light not only on the commission but also on the union as a whole.

first of all, congratulations to the rapporteur on his approach to the quality of agricultural products. the market demands are diverse and increasingly numerous. in the european union, the most important issues are food hygiene and safety, health and nutritional value, and certain societal requirements. consumers are also increasingly aware of agriculture's contribution to sustainability, climate change, food security, biodiversity, animal welfare and water scarcity. in the face of these new commercial challenges, the european farmer's main asset is quality. the european union has the quality advantage, and this is due to a very high level of safety, ensured by the legislation in force, along the entire food chain to which farmers and producers have contributed. there are, however, a few aspects that can enhance the quality. i believe that the european union has a duty to promote quality products, but also to act in favour of their protection at international level. in this context, i believe that stricter controls should be applied to organic products from third countries, so as to ensure fair competition between european and third country organic products.
a quality policy for agricultural products can be a solution for many farmers. for many households, focusing on quality rather than quantity can bring long-term benefits and therefore the european union needs coherent policies in this area that, at the same time, ensure that european farmers are able to compete on the international market. in these circumstances, the scotta report is welcome, as is the package announced by commissioner ciolos. at the same time, to achieve our quality objectives, we will need something else, a future strong common agricultural policy with a strong budget. a policy on the quality of agricultural products and a reduction in the budget for european agriculture are two incompatible concepts. we also need sufficient tools for farmers to develop their quality policy and, last but not least, equal opportunities for farmers in the western and eastern member states.

member of the commission. − mr president, i welcome this opportunity on world tuberculosis day to underline the commission’s commitment to addressing the challenges caused by this disease. we had believed that our successes in past decades had eliminated the threats related to this serious public health concern. however, for too long, we have mistakenly lowered the guard against tuberculosis. in 2008 the european centre for disease prevention and control reported around 83 000 cases and close to 6 000 deaths due to tuberculosis in the european union and efta countries. this amounts to about 16 deaths a day. this is simply unacceptable and requires action by all concerned sectors and stakeholders. it is unacceptable because tuberculosis is a preventable and curable disease that should not lead to such dramatic consequences. tuberculosis is a cross-sector issue and it is linked to many of the public health challenges we face in the european union, including the spread of antimicrobial resistance, the lack of new effective tools to diagnose and treat tuberculosis, the steep rise of co-infections such as with hiv, and the inequalities, with tuberculosis disproportionally affecting the most vulnerable groups. the commission has launched a number of initiatives over the past years to strengthen capacities to tackle tuberculosis. in 2000 tuberculosis was included in the list of priority diseases under eu-wide surveillance. in this context, the commission supported several projects that have helped coordinate the surveillance of tuberculosis in the 53 countries of the who european region. this has improved our shared knowledge and monitoring of the epidemiological situation. in addition, through its research framework programmes, the commission supports the development of new treatments, vaccines, drugs and diagnostic tools against tuberculosis. since 2002 more than eur 124 million has been allocated to these efforts. but, as tuberculosis is not constrained by borders, we have to support countries beyond the european union. the commission supports developing countries in their tuberculosis control programmes through the european programme for action to confront hiv/aids, malaria and tuberculosis through external action (2007-2011). the main channel for financing this support is the global fund to fight aids, tuberculosis and malaria, to which the commission has contributed eur 870 million since 2002, with an annual contribution that amounts to eur 100 million since 2008. in addition, it supports clinical trials and capacity building in sub-saharan africa through the european and developing countries clinical trials partnership (edctp). finally, the setting-up of the european centre for disease prevention and control has enabled us to raise our efforts against tuberculosis to a new level. in march 2007, following a request from the commission, the centre developed an action plan to fight tuberculosis in the eu. this addresses the key cross-sectoral challenges we are facing today in tuberculosis prevention and control and strengthening epidemiological surveillance: ensuring prompt and quality tb care for all, developing new tools for diagnosis and treatment, decreasing the burden of tuberculosis and hiv co-infection, and addressing the threat of multi-drug resistance. however the commission cannot succeed in this challenge alone. the contribution from civil society to reach out to the most vulnerable, and the member states’ commitment are key towards achieving our objective to support the global fight against this disease.
on behalf of the epp group. "the cause of death in the age of antibiotics", a group of researchers called tuberculosis, a term that many of us thought had disappeared from the vocabulary, but which still kills many people. tuberculosis is the seventh leading cause of death in the world. unfortunately, the present period is marked by an increase in the number of cases of tuberculosis that are resistant to standard drug treatments. worldwide, there were 9.4 million new tb cases and 1.8 million deaths in 2008. every second, someone somewhere in the world is infected with the tuberculosis bacillus. we need to hear these figures spoken as clearly as possible in a major forum of the european union, so that we can all better understand that this disease is still eating away at our societies, still killing large numbers of european citizens. i come from a country that unfortunately ranks first in the european union in the sad rankings of tuberculosis. although there has been a slight downward trend in recent years and an increase in the rate of cure for chemoresistant tuberculosis, the absolute figures are still worrying and the reality they reflect is dramatic. we need a coherent, integrated and well-planned fight to bring this scourge under control. we need to continue, at eu level, the work that has been done so far to ensure that we raise the level of disease detection, the level of access to appropriate treatment, the quality of treatment monitoring, the quality of healthcare provided to patients in all member states. we need all governments to recognise the importance of this fight and to work as closely as possible with the social partners, so that fewer and fewer europeans suffer from this disease that we thought was exiled in past centuries. and most of all, we need to fight this fight together, as a family, overcoming our differences, helping each other to overcome this difficulty. after all, we are the european union and our strength lies in our unity.
member of the commission. − mr president, i would like first of all to congratulate the rapporteur for this very comprehensive report. as rightly emphasised in this report, developing countries have been affected by the crisis much harder than initially expected. in fact, they have been hit through several transmission channels, such as volatile commodity prices, declining export revenues and tourism earnings, as well as falling capital flows and remittances. one common feature is the increase in financing needs of many countries. many developing countries were often obliged to cut social expenditure (notably in nutrition, health and education), entailing severe social and political consequences and threatening not only the achievement of the mdgs by 2015, but also undermining past progress observed in recent years. despite some first signs of global recovery, developing countries, particularly in sub-saharan africa, will certainly lag behind. the eu has shown leadership and unity through a joint eu response to the crisis framed within the global response, namely within the united nations, the g20 and g8. we have acted quickly and efficiently to translate pledges into concrete commitments to help developing countries cope with the crisis. last spring, the eu adopted a set of comprehensive, timely, targeted and coordinated measures to cushion the human impact of the crisis, boost economic growth in developing countries and protect the most vulnerable. the eu response comprises not only the community response but also the eu member states’ response (their respective bilateral responses as well as their contributions to the resources of the international financial institutions as called upon by the g20). moreover, close collaboration with the world bank and the imf has enabled us to ensure the consistency of our respective analyses and the complementarity of our assistance. as highlighted in the report, the commission has set up and is currently implementing a very concrete and short-term ad hoc mechanism, named the vulnerability flex, to support the most vulnerable countries with poor resilience capacity, with a view to enabling them to maintain priority spending, notably in the social sectors. other measures include reallocations following ad hoc country reviews and the advanced mid-term review of the 10th european development fund, which is currently ongoing, support under the traditional flex instrument, frontloading of aid where feasible, etc. official development assistance (oda) has played, and will continue to play, a critical role in supporting our partners’ efforts in coping with the crisis. in this context, the commission welcomes your support in urging member states to stay committed to achieving by 2015 the 0.7% oda/gni target. other donors should take similar ambitious targets for oda increases, and we must call upon the entire donor community to live up to their commitments in terms of aid volumes and effectiveness. on 21 april, the commission will publish its yearly spring development package of proposals to member states. this year, the focus will be on the actions that remain necessary to achieve the mdgs. the package will adopt a comprehensive approach and define an action plan for accelerated progress towards the mdgs. it will also provide an opportunity to make an ambitious eu contribution to the forthcoming un high-level mdg review in september. in doing so, the eu will remain credible about its commitments and continue to play a leading role in international development.
the economic and financial crisis has also hit moldova, a developing country, hard. the country's economy contracted by 9% last year according to imf estimates, and the unemployment rate was over 6%. direct investment must be stimulated. i should mention that moldova has hired nine high-ranking european advisers for one year to assist the main ministries in chisinau. given that we speak the same language, our neighbours across the prut can benefit from romania's expertise in absolutely all areas. it is necessary to reduce the cost of money transfers that migrants make from the countries where they work. the commitment of the g8 leaders to reduce them from 10% to 5% over the next five years is a first step in this direction. i would like to welcome today the award of record financial support to moldova of $2.6 billion for the period 2011-2013. the agreement was reached today by prime minister vlad filat in brussels at the donors' conference.
in writing. developing countries have ended up as the main victims of the financial crisis, despite initial predictions that developed countries would be the hardest hit. the theory that developing countries are insufficiently connected to the world economy to be seriously affected by the financial market crisis has been refuted by reality. we are seeing the deepening of the crisis in many developing countries, with unprecedented unemployment rates, exponential increases in public debt and budget deficits. and that's while developed countries, which didn't feel the crisis very strongly or had effective tools at their disposal to mitigate its impact, moved on to economic growth, albeit timidly. the economic crisis is already directly affecting the population and unemployment is increasing in developing countries. the economic recovery efforts of countries still feeling the effects of the crisis could affect entire social groups, but the recovery measures can only be painful. eu funding programmes are the most comprehensive and complex financial assistance in the world and affected member states must benefit as much as possible from the money allocated to situations of restriction of economic activity with social effects.
the major cause of the crisis is the mafia. i'm going to give you a few examples from my country, romania, and please believe me that as a writer and historian, who runs a daily newspaper and a weekly magazine, i know exactly what i'm talking about. since 1990, some 6 000 enterprises worth €700 billion have been fraudulently privatised. unfortunately, of this money, only 7 billion euros have been collected so far, so 1%. in many cases, it was not even privatization, but the transfer of values from the property of the romanian state to the property of other states, that is, nationalization. this is no longer a market economy, but a jungle economy. the situation is repeated in several balkan countries where the local mafia has joined forces with the transnational mafia in an organized crime cartel. just as it was 100 years ago, the balkan peninsula is sitting on a powder keg. the flame of social protest can spread rapidly from greece to the other countries in the region. if in the 20th century we talked about exporting revolution, in the 21st century we can talk about exporting bankruptcy. hunger is the most powerful electoral agent in history. we need to shift the focus from fighting corruption, which is an abstraction, to fighting the corrupt. the mood of the population is getting worse and worse and if we fail to stop the looting of our countries, then the generous project of the european union will collapse like a sand castle. there is a salvation, however: at such a historic crossroads, radical solutions are needed. the mafia doesn't have to be under control, the mafia has to be underground.
it is not surprising that the core of the ecb's annual report is made up of exceptional measures that the ecb was forced to adopt in crisis conditions. in this context, i consider it appropriate that the european central bank should constantly increase its liquidity provision to euro area banks, but we must not forget that the member states outside the euro area have also been severely affected by the crisis and that there is a need for intervention by the central bank through liquidity-enhancing measures in this area as well. the increase in budget deficits, public debt and the unemployment rate among young people under 25 is also being recorded in most eu member states. the stability and growth pact is experiencing an identity crisis, losing credibility and effectively applying its principles is becoming impossible. i believe that there is a need for less automation and uniformity in the pact, for an approach that takes account of the circumstances of each member state, where the emphasis is much more on the long-term sustainability of public finances and less on the public deficit. the main purpose of the pact was preventive; it sought multilateral monitoring of budgetary developments through an early warning system. i therefore believe that, in the spirit of my colleague scicluna's report, it is absolutely necessary to set up a european systemic risk committee to fulfil the objective of early warning against systemic risks or imbalances that threaten the financial markets. this financial crisis, and its recent sharpening in general, should prompt a rapid clarification of the mechanisms for mutual support at union level, as well as a strengthening of the instruments for coordination between member states in support of common economic governance. one of the major lessons of the crisis is the need for increased fiscal responsibility and, by implication, for economic oversight to maintain budgetary balance.
during the crisis, it was seen that fluctuations in interest rates and exchange rates hit a single currency, which acted as a real shield for the euro area. the single currency has not been a solution to all internal and external imbalances that have arisen, but the advantages offered by access to the european central bank's liquidity for national financial institutions and the elimination of the risk of exchange rate fluctuations have increased interest in it among non-euro area member states. the effort made by these countries, by improving their own economies and fiscal policies to adopt the single currency, should be appreciated and i call on the commission and the european central bank to encourage more the enlargement of the euro area in the shortest possible time, in order to be more protected from the effects of the economic and financial crisis.

mr president, when the creator of the concept of 'gross domestic product', simon kuznets, acknowledged that the well-being of a nation can only be measured with difficulty by the size of national income alone, i do not think he imagined that three quarters of a century would pass before five nobel laureates would work on a set of proposals for a more accurate assessment of economic performance and social product than that provided by gdp. this macroeconomic indicator neglects product quality, does not measure sustainable economic growth, and excludes, among other things, subsistence and suburban economies, domestic work, and volunteering. the outcome of this committee's work, summarised in the stiglitz report, proposes improving the national statistical system, better determining the quality of life and including sustainable development in the calculation of the index of economic and social progress. in this context, i believe that we need to have a coordinated system for measuring the quality of life, the sustainability of economic growth and, last but not least, social disparities throughout the european union. it would be a sign that we've learned something from the lesson of the recession that's affecting us so much.
madam president, the third postal directive, which will completely liberalize this market, is due to be implemented at the end of this year. the economic and financial crisis has repercussions known, including on the postal market. the effects of the crisis have doubled in the member states where the postal market has been fully liberalised following the application of the directive. here, layoffs, declines in the incomes of the remaining staff are above average. there have also been decreases in transactions, increases in postal rates, and the deprivation of citizens in hard-to-reach localities and regions of access to communications and universal service. i consider that an assessment of the social consequences of the application of this directive is necessary. it is our duty to prevent social dumping and i ask the european institutions concerned to consider the possibility of applying a moratorium of at least two years to the deadlines for implementing this directive, differentiated in each of the other member states.
