on behalf of the ppe group. – mr president, i join my colleagues in deploring the execution of 18 people in libya on 30 may 2010 and in calling for the abolition of capital punishment. libya uses the death penalty as a tool for curbing free expression and association in the country. documentation of such cases is made difficult by the government. however, human rights watch interviewed one prisoner who said that the authorities had commuted his death sentence at the last moment to life in prison. according to mr al-sharif, the people’s court convicted him and two other men of organising a political group which opposed the principles of the al-fateh revolution. the supreme court confirmed the death sentences but the supreme council for judicial authority spared the prisoners’ lives at the last moment in february 2002 after they had spent one hour blindfolded and bound to a wooden stake awaiting execution. according to mr al-sharif, one of the three men committed suicide in december 2004. reportedly, more than 200 people are currently on death row in libya. i call on the commission and the council to raise these issues as a priority in their dialogue with libya.
the death penalty is the most cruel and inhumane punishment possible, and libya is among the 12 countries that have already applied the death penalty in 2010, even though it is frowned upon by the un and most of the world's states. i believe that the european union has a duty to take on more firmly its mission of advocating for the abolition of the death penalty and, at the same time, it is our duty to intensify our pressure for the commutation of these sentences and for the respect of the rights of foreign nationals against whom the death penalty is used disproportionately, because they face the difficulty of having a translator, of contacting the diplomatic representatives of their governments, as well as of obtaining commutation of the sentence due to lack of financial means and of the family, who negotiate financial compensation, as is customary, for the forgiveness of the victim's family. in these circumstances, i believe that a strong signal must be sent to the libyan authorities to respect international standards of legal fairness and also to allow the un refugee agency to resume its work for the benefit of refugees and asylum seekers.
for us europeans, the death penalty is something absurd, because, as we know, it has been eliminated from our political culture, and what is happening in libya now is scandalous. it is all the more scandalous when we have to understand that this punishment is applied very often to people from outside the libyan area and the information about the recent execution of 18 people tells us that they are egyptians, nigerians, chadians. why is it so much worse for these people? because, unfortunately, their basic rights are not respected in the process and i am referring here to access to translators and also to consular assistance, which must be imposed in accordance with international standards. i would also like to say that we must discuss this next week, when we will have guests from libya as part of the maghreb delegation, and i think we must say these things emphatically in the context of our dialogue with that country.

in writing. the european council of 17 june 2010 adopted five main objectives for growth and employment: an employment rate of 75% for the population aged 20-64; improved conditions for research and development and the use of 3% of gdp for this sector; a 20% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions compared to 1990; a 20% increase in energy efficiency; 20% of energy consumed to come from renewable sources; a reduction in school dropouts and higher education graduation rates; and poverty reduction. some of these objectives were set by the lisbon strategy in 2000, but the results achieved so far are still far from expectations. in addition, the economic and financial crisis has led to a dramatic increase in unemployment, jeopardising the sustainability of pension systems already dependent on demographic change, thus putting the elderly and young population at risk of poverty. i believe that the digital agenda, the climate change agenda, investment in transport and energy infrastructure and agricultural development should be the main elements of the eu2020 strategy, to be supported by cohesion policy, the common agricultural policy and the future financial perspective.
the two regulations on the rights of passengers travelling by bus and coach, and those travelling by sea and inland waterways, complement the legal framework defining and protecting passenger rights. in the airline industry, such regulations already exist, but even under these conditions many passengers are unaware of their rights and do not complain when they are not respected. that is why it is absolutely necessary that this type of regulation exists for all types of transport. the regulations we are discussing today lay down liability for death or injury to passengers, the rights of persons with reduced mobility, compensation and assistance in the event of cancellation or delay, and contain clear provisions on the lodging of complaints and possible remedies. we welcome the agreement reached on shipping, but we consider that defining and respecting the rights of disabled people travelling by bus and coach is a must for the inclusion of all citizens in society.

the adoption of the directive on the framework for the deployment of intelligent transport systems in road transport and for interfaces with other modes of transport is an important step towards increasing safety in the transport sector. i would like to thank the whole team of rapporteurs for extending the scope of the directive to road transport by including interfaces with other modes of transport. intelligent transport systems will thus be able to be used for passengers, vehicles and infrastructure and their interaction in the field of road transport, including urban transport and interfaces with other modes of transport. the european parliament has called for a minimum level of applications and services for intelligent transport systems and for strict provisions on the protection of personal data since the first reading. the directive provides for four priority areas in which the commission is to define common specifications and standards for the implementation and use of intelligent transport systems. the commission has committed to the speedy adoption of specifications, within a well-established timetable, as follows: 2014 for the provision of information services on multimodal travel at european level; 2013 for the provision of real-time traffic information services at european level; 2012 for the provision of road safety-related minimum universal traffic information free of charge; 2012 for the harmonised provision of an interoperable eu-wide ecall system; 2012 and 2013 for the provision of information and reservation services respectively on safe parking spaces for trucks. the adoption of this directive was delayed as a result of the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon and the provisions on comitology. the specifications referred to above will therefore be adopted by the commission by means of delegated acts. i believe that we are only at the beginning of the road towards the implementation of intelligent transport systems and we hope that both the commission and the member states will allocate the necessary financial resources to the implementation of these systems.
the establishment of a single framework for the coordinated use of intelligent transport systems is an important step in the modernisation of the transport sector and obliges member states to ensure the implementation and coordination of its in an interoperable manner. as rapporteur on the european rail freight corridors, i believe that interoperable its systems are absolutely necessary on the railway, especially in terms of traffic management. for this reason, there is a need for mutual recognition of national approvals and specifications for equipment and software, and for compliance with the rtms deployment schedule. the fact that member states have the possibility to adapt to the new requirements by upgrading their existing systems is a positive thing and avoids the creation of geographical discontinuities.
the directive on reporting formalities for ships entering and leaving the ports of the member states provides for simplification of customs formalities, wider use of electronic data exchange and the introduction of e-maritime systems, the creation of a single administrative desk and simplified rules for dangerous goods. the implementation of this directive requires a good level of cooperation between the different competent authorities. the commission shall report to parliament by 31 december 2011 at the latest on the extension of the scope of the simplifications introduced by this directive to inland waterway transport. to this end, the commission will assess the compatibility of the river information system with safeseanet, the electronic data exchange platform used for the implementation of this directive. also, to ensure more effective communication, the report recommends by amendment 9 the use of rule 14 of the solas convention, which provides for the use of english as the working language.

in writing. the economic downturn has caused a massive increase in youth unemployment, one of europe's most pressing problems. today, more than 5.5 million young people under 25 are unemployed, representing 21.4 percent - twice the overall unemployment rate. previous crises have shown that young people are the hardest hit because they are the last to be hired and, in many cases, the first to be fired. many young people, particularly in southern europe, have short-term contracts, which means they are easily dismissed in times of crisis. the european commission must increase funding for the european social fund, allocate at least 10% of this fund to projects for young people and simplify access to this fund. i believe that the most important issues that can be addressed at eu level to help young people are: the european charter for the quality of traineeships, which will ensure that where practical experience is incorporated into education systems, certain conditions are met, and the introduction of a european youth guarantee, which will ensure that every young person in the eu is offered a job after a maximum of 4 months of unemployment.

in writing. − the paris convention on international exhibitions regulates the frequency, quality and procedures of international exhibitions falling within its scope. since the paris convention covers matters falling within the scope of the customs legislation of the european union and the european union cannot itself accede to the paris convention, as only a sovereign state can be a party to it, a member state wishing to accede to the convention needs the authorisation of the european union. we voted for this report so that the three member states which have not yet joined can join the paris convention.
in writing. − the european union is a signatory to the barcelona convention for the protection of the mediterranean sea against pollution and has an obligation to promote integrated coastal zone management, taking into account the protection of areas of ecological interest and the rational use of natural resources. the text of this protocol contains provisions relating to economic activities, construction, tourism, fisheries, aquaculture and maritime activities in the coastal areas of the mediterranean. through its mechanisms, the protocol contributes to improving coordination of actions for the management of coastal areas between national, regional and local authorities. i voted in favour of this report because it includes objectives and principles for good coastal management and promotes the sustainable use of natural resources through the use of monitoring tools.
in writing. − the coastal areas of the mediterranean sea continue to be subject to severe environmental pressures and a marked degradation of coastal resources. in the mediterranean area, urban expansion is intense, leading to a gradual loss of natural areas and biodiversity, as well as increased competition for water resources. the problems of coastal erosion and low-lying coastal flooding are exacerbated by urban encroachment in near-shore and flood-prone areas. factors likely to aggravate the pressures include projected population growth concentrated in urban coastal areas, a (nearly) doubling of tourist flows and even greater transport development. nearly 50% of the coastline could become built-up area by 2025, up from 40% in 2000. moreover, the mediterranean basin is one of the most vulnerable areas to the impact of climate change. the protocol provides a framework for stimulating a more concerted and integrated approach, which is needed to address these problems more effectively and achieve a more sustainable development of the coastal areas of the mediterranean sea. that is why i voted for this report.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the council decision on the conclusion of the agreement between the european union and iceland and norway on the stepping up of cross-border cooperation, with a view to tackling terrorism and cross-border crime. this decision lays out the necessary administrative and technical provisions for the automated exchange of dna data, fingerprint data and vehicle registration data. with the freedoms granted by the schengen area, it is also necessary to extend the tools available to combat cross-border crime and terrorism to those schengen members not within the eu. i support this agreement, as it will strengthen the fight against terrorist and criminal threats within the schengen area. it should be recalled that the security of the schengen area will be further strengthened through the full implementation of the sis ii system. the commission should exert all efforts to end the continuing delays with sis ii.

in writing. − the european community has learned a lesson from the greek experience and the commission's initiative to regulate and empower eurostat will prevent similar situations from occurring in the future. i therefore believe that the commission's proposals, as amended by parliament, must be put into practice as soon as possible in order to be able to take immediate action in the event of suspicions of false statistical reporting by any member state. the european union cannot afford to gamble with its credibility or position in the financial markets, because it is perceived as a whole and the blame becomes shared, even though it belongs to one state. the idea of making eurostat an audit institution was rejected five years ago. there is no point in thinking about the 'what if' system, but it is relevant that at this moment the proposal has every chance of being put into practice. accurate and reliable statistical data are vital for the proper functioning of economic and monetary union. moreover, the rethinking of eurostat's tasks can only result in an increase in the level of trust between the member states of the european union and even in the credibility of each of them.
in writing. − the quality of statistical data is particularly important during this period, given the need to respond rapidly to any potential economic alarm signals. the precedent being known, no further arguments are needed. statistical data are also a useful tool in all sectors where the european union has competence, being indispensable for decision-making in the short, medium and long term. the better the quality of these statistics, the better the decisions made will be able to meet the challenges facing the member states and the european union as a whole.
in writing. − the european union and its member states are facing a major financial, economic and social crisis and must make a major effort to ensure that europe has as many jobs and as high a level of employment as possible. to overcome this crisis, the union must step up its efforts and invest in skills, vocational training and sustainable job creation. the objective of the eu 2020 strategy should be to effectively launch a comprehensive european employment initiative, for example by strengthening activation systems, in particular for low-skilled people, through personalised counselling, intensive skills/re-skilling and upskilling of workers, apprentices, job subsidies and grants for self-employment and business start-ups. these measures may be financed through the european social fund payments committee. rapid intervention is required when jobs are effectively being eliminated, not least to reduce the risk of people being excluded from the labour market. the measures are necessary given that the unemployment rate in the eu-27 increased in 2009 from 8% to 9,6%.

in writing. − decarbonizing transport is a significant policy objective that needs to be pursued more intensively in the future, as the adverse health and environmental effects of transport are a major challenge, especially in efforts to combat climate change. for such decarbonisation to contribute to a significant reduction in exhaust gas and noise emissions and to reduce traffic jams, two conditions must be met: the internalisation of external costs must cover all transport modes, and the revenues generated must be used to increase the sustainability of the infrastructure. the effects of the financial and economic crisis on the transport sector should not be overlooked, as the sector has reacted very sensitively to the crisis. i believe that this crisis should be seen as an opportunity to provide specific support to the transport sector in the future by encouraging investment. they should not only be quick aid, but also contribute to improving environmental and safety performance, creating new green jobs, by developing both national and european policy instruments. the commission and the member states should continue to exchange good practices (e.g. in the framework of the covenant of mayors, the civitas initiative, etc.) which give communities the chance to learn from the experience of other european citizens.
in writing. - i voted for the grosch report on a sustainable future for transport because i believe its recommendations should be reflected in the forthcoming white paper on the development of trans-european transport. the transport sector is a vital sector, both for the eu's economic development and competitiveness and for the eu's economic and social cohesion. unfortunately, however, the financial resources allocated to this sector are insufficient. the ten-t budget for 2007-13 is only €8.013 billion, and the sums allocated to transport through cohesion policy represent only 11% of the total budget allocated to this policy. i call for the eu to allocate additional financial resources to the development of the trans-european transport system and its integration with the transport systems of the union's neighbouring countries. that's why i voted against amendment 6. this amendment was intended to replace the creation of a transport fund with more resources than those already included in the eu budget with a mechanism for coordinating the use of the different existing sources of transport funding. it is clear that the eu needs to ensure better coordination of existing sources of finance for the transport sector, but it is also imperative to create new instruments for financing transport infrastructure development work.

in writing. − almost a quarter of young people aged under 25 in the european union are currently unemployed. in figures, this means that almost 6 million young people are now unemployed, and this reality is also reflected in the impoverishment of national budgets, which consume money for the maintenance of these young people, without collecting taxes and duties from them. the development, at european level and at the level of each member state, of incentive programmes to employ this enormous human resource with its enthusiasm intact and fresh from school can only bring about optimal results, from an economic point of view, for everyone. this is the first time in 30 years that europe has seen such dramatic figures for youth employment. as some studies have shown, young unemployed people are likely to repeat this behaviour throughout their lives, and this can only result in putting an unnecessary burden on national and european budgets in the long term.

in writing. − the challenges in achieving a 'europe for the young' are to actively mobilise investment, create new jobs and provide vocational training opportunities. member states should encourage employers to offer young people stable and long-term jobs and pay that reflects their level of effort and their professional and intellectual abilities, to protect them against contracts containing clauses that place them in a precarious position in relation to the employer, to ensure a gender balance in terms of employment conditions between young women and men at the beginning of their careers and, not least, to ensure access to social protection mechanisms for young men and women.
in writing. − the european union is facing a major financial, economic and social crisis, and to overcome it, efforts to invest in skills, vocational training and sustainable job creation must be stepped up. in this context, atypical forms of contract have increased significantly, with young workers aged 19-29 or over 50, women and low-skilled workers being the most affected. in terms of quality of work, these workers face low job security, lack of a set career plan, fewer opportunities for training and career development and greater difficulties in reconciling work and family life. it is therefore necessary to extend the protection of workers in these atypical forms of contract, to take measures against undeclared work and to facilitate the transition between different employment situations and unemployment. any form of employment must be accompanied by a set of rights including: equal treatment, protection of the health and safety of workers, access to training, collective bargaining and freedom of association and representation.
in writing. − increasing resource efficiency in europe is one of the priority objectives of the eu 2020 strategy. for example, biogas is a valuable resource for the production of electricity and transport fuel, as well as for supplying the gas grid. the most efficient way to produce biogas is by recovering organic waste, which benefits industry, the economy and the environment. at the same time, recycling of bio-waste can also help to reduce the use of chemical fertilizers in agriculture, especially phosphorus-based ones, and to improve the hydrological retention capacity of the soil to maintain high productivity. this link between the transition to a recycling society, the development of a low-carbon economy and the potential for job creation in the field is important in the current economic, environmental and social context.
in writing. − a strategic objective of waste management policy is to transform the eu into a recycling society. the enormous amount of waste produced annually in the eu (estimated at between 76.5 and 102 million tonnes of bio-waste, and in romania at around 8 million tonnes) cannot be wasted. biological waste plays an important role in combating climate change (in 2004, the waste sector emitted a total of 109 million tonnes of greenhouse gases), offering valuable potential for protecting soil and promoting renewable energy production. this means that sustainable development can be promoted through resource efficiency: the correct and uniform eu-wide management of bio-waste, the promotion of technological innovation and the creation of green jobs (e.g. the recycling industry of 10 000 tonnes of waste creates up to 250 jobs). therefore, a mandatory separate collection system, the recycling of bio-waste, a specific bio-waste directive, the encouragement of research and innovation and increased awareness of waste prevention measures among citizens are necessary to help the economy and the environment and to achieve the objectives of the eu 2020 strategy.

rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on legal affairs. - i would like to mention that i am speaking as a shadow rapporteur for the opinion. the current financial crisis has highlighted a lack of effectiveness in managing crisis situations that have arisen in cross-border financial entities in the eu. there have been different approaches at national level, but in general the authorities have either used public funds to rescue the banks or have isolated the banks' assets on national territory, applying national resolution tools only at the level of their own branches. these actions have amplified the risks related to loss of confidence, distortion of competition, legal uncertainty and the high level of the cost incurred for the rescue of the banks, which is borne by the taxpayers. in conclusion, we need measures at european level to eliminate the crisis management of a crossborder banking group through national systems, which can be extremely different and tend to protect existing branches within their own territory rather than resolve the problem of the group as a whole.
the current economic crisis has shown us that we need a system to prevent crises and limit their negative effects. the de larosière report, published in february 2009, analysed financial supervision in the european union, proposing the creation of a sui generis body to be responsible for macroeconomic supervision at the level of the european union and to respond to current weaknesses. since 2000, the european parliament has also asked the commission to come up with proposals aimed at ensuring the stability of the european union's financial markets. in practice, the european union is at a critical juncture where it must prove its usefulness to its citizens, who are looking to it for solutions to the current economic crisis and for effective mechanisms to prevent future economic crises. there has been talk of a democratic deficit in the european union, of a low participation rate of european citizens in european parliament elections, of their non-identification with european policies, and that is why i believe that the treaty of lisbon can indeed be an important step towards addressing these shortcomings, but it is only the basis. the next step is to build a strong foundation that generates confidence in the european economic and political system through stability and the benefits it brings. we need an effective supervisory system that creates the conditions for stable financing of the economy, for ensuring sustainable economic growth and jobs. the unity of the european single market must also be monitored if it is to be avoided from fragmentation. that is why i believe that the european systemic risk board and the financial supervisory authorities should be set up.
i would also like to draw attention to the activity of foreign banks in the new member states outside the euro area. this activity must be given the utmost importance in the framework of financial system supervision, both at the european union and national level, in order to prevent irrational and risky behaviour. i support this because foreign banks in some of the new member states have created extreme risk by taking short-term external credit and extending medium and long-term credit to firms and citizens in these countries. this was a major cause for which the countries concerned urgently appealed to the conditional support of the international monetary fund.
this crisis has shown that we need a better mechanism for cross-border regulation and supervision of financial markets. the main objective of the whole legislative package is to maintain financial stability in the union, to identify risks in the system in advance and to protect investors. it is very important, however, not to over-regulate the market, which could mean more bureaucracy and even corruption. i believe that the three european supervisory authorities, as well as the european systemic risk board, will contribute to strengthening supervision at eu level. it is therefore important that parliament, the council and the commission reach a compromise on the proposals for better regulation and supervision as soon as possible.
on 9 may, the finance ministers of the member states decided to set up a european financial stabilisation mechanism. it is part of a package of legislative measures designed to protect the euro and to restore the financial situation in the european union. i believe that the new mechanism will have to respond in a prompt and coordinated manner if a state cannot finance its public debt by its own efforts. it will thus be able to contribute to the sustainability of public finances in the beneficiary member state. the union has already responded through the european financial stabilisation mechanism to a crisis situation for which it was not sufficiently prepared. finally, i would like to ask you, commissioner barnier, given the temporary nature of this mechanism, which has been in place for three years, and taking into account the need for the union to respond promptly in crisis situations, when do you envisage making this mechanism permanent and what would be the sources of funding for it?
on behalf of the s&d group. i would like, first of all, to thank the rapporteur for her work and also for her cooperation on many of the issues important to our group. the main concern for the s&d group has always been food from cloned animals. research on the effects of food from cloned animals on humans is limited and has not been conducted to conclude that such food is safe for consumption. ethical concerns about the use of cloning, lack of knowledge about the effects of consumption of such food products on consumers, and animal welfare concerns lead us to conclude that the use of cloning for food production is not justified. the report also addresses the issue of food containing nanomaterials as well as food produced using nanotechnology. the effects of nanomaterials on the human body are unknown. we must do everything we can to ensure the safety of our consumption. we will therefore support the development of specific risk assessment methods by the european food safety authority before such foods are authorised for sale. we need to take a cautious approach to food technology if we do not fully understand its impact on the human body and the environment. it is also important to inform consumers about what they are eating, which is why i support labelling requirements. while the main objective of this regulation should be to ensure that food is safe for the human body, animal welfare is also an important concern. i am happy to support amendments which will ensure improvements in animal welfare, such as the development of alternative testing methods and the exchange of data between applicants for novel foods, where this will prevent the repetition of animal testing. the parliament's position on the issues at hand was very clear at first reading and the report was adopted by a large majority. given that the council has shown very little willingness to compromise on the issue of food from cloned animals, it is important that parliament takes a firm stand at this time. we represent the people and we must not forget that.
food products produced using nanotechnology undoubtedly need to undergo specific risk assessments before they are approved, labelled and placed on the european market, as do food derived from cloned animals and their progeny. these regulations are aimed at ensuring food safety and human health. i agree that the new food names, though dry, are exciting enough to make you dream of all kinds of beautifully colored, juicy, and deliciously tasty fruits you've never seen before. sadly, though, the reality is much grayer. the desire that foodstuffs produced by nanotechnology should only be allowed after nanospecific testing is legitimate. the fact that scientific discoveries in this field have been making rapid progress in recent years and that their practical applications may in the future provide real life-saving solutions to eradicating hunger or counteracting the effects of economic crisis does not give us the right to throw away our safety and health and that of future generations. food from cloned animals is often talked about with astonishing ease, as if it had been around for hundreds of years and everyday life could not be conceived without it. do i need to remind you that the technologies used to produce such foods are, in many ways, still experimental? finally, i just want to ask you: are you willing to put these foods on your children's table?
the purpose of this regulation is to ensure a high level of food safety and protection of the consumer, the environment and animal welfare, based on the precautionary principle. there are currently significant doubts about the safety of meat from cloned animals. they have suffered from premature aging or other diseases, and it is still not clear to scientists what causes the differences between the breeds of animals produced by traditional techniques and those produced by cloning. cloned animals suffer. most of the cloned organisms didn't survive or died prematurely. the success rate is a viable organism at 75 cloning attempts. not least, cloning raises safety concerns. at present, this technique is too dangerous to be used for direct human benefit. it's a serious ethical issue. given the serious health risks and moral consequences of using these techniques, i believe that there should be no ambiguity in this regard. for ethical reasons, for animal welfare reasons and because cloning is not justified in the food supply, i also believe that the ban on cloning should be emphasised in this regulation.
the industrial emissions directive aims to reduce emissions from over 52 000 industrial installations across the union in a variety of industries. installations covered by this directive must be authorised. the permits shall include emission limit values to be complied with and operating conditions established on the basis of best available techniques. in order to obtain these permits, companies in the industries concerned should also submit an investment plan guaranteeing the modernisation of industrial installations with a view to reducing polluting emissions. i believe that this directive should be linked to the industrial policy of the european union. the directive should provide sufficient flexibility for european industry to be modernised so as to preserve industrial production and jobs in the european union, while reducing polluting emissions. finally, i ask the commission to consult parliament and the member states at an early stage in the development of decisions to set emission limit values associated with best techniques and not only after they have been adopted by the commission.
i think the compromise text resulting from the trialogue is a good one. the differences between member states in the implementation and enforcement of legislation are eliminated. a number of derogations and flexibilities have been included for large combustion plants that cannot comply by the date of entry into force of the directive. it will be possible to establish minimum requirements, i.e. minimum emission limit values, for each industrial sector, to be uniformly respected by all economic operators in the european union. derogations from the accepted emission values established on the basis of best available techniques may be granted. these derogations concern cases where the costs of the investment exceed the environmental benefits. the compromise text is part of a systematic approach to improving the performance of industrial installations, both in terms of environmental protection and economic benefits. of all of these... member of the commission. − madam president, it is my pleasure to be here with you today for an exchange of views on iceland and the next steps in the accession process. the unanimous decision of the process. as a first step, the commission prepared a draft negotiating framework, rightly admitted by my predecessor, which is currently under discussion in the council. the belgian presidency foresees fisheries, agriculture and the environment – should start very early in the process. throughout the whole process, the commission aims to support iceland’s efforts to meet the accession criteria, monitored. as you can see, all preparations are well on track to allow for an early start to the negotiations. iceland’s membership of the eea, its association with the schengen agreement, and the country’s high democratic standards will be valuable assets in this process. however, we cannot turn a blind eye to the fact that the road to accession will also hold a number of challenges. we are in writing. − this regulation lays down harmonised rules for the placing on the market of novel foods in the community in order to ensure a high level of protection of human life and health, animal health and welfare, the environment and consumer interests, while ensuring the transparency and efficient functioning of the internal market and stimulating innovation in the agri-food industry. i voted for this report so that meat and dairy products from cloned animals or their descendants could be banned in europe and also so that food produced using nanotechnology could be subject to risk assessments and be labelled accordingly.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report, which reconfirms the position of the european parliament on the key issue of foods from cloned animals. there are many ethical concerns regarding the use of this technology, particularly with regard to animal welfare. in addition, we do not fully understand the risks or the reduction of genetic diversity in animals which would result from producing large amounts of clones. there is simply no justification or need to use cloned animals for food production. it is unethical and unnecessary. i will continue to work with the rapporteur and the other shadows to promote parliament’s common view that foods from cloned animals should not be allowed on the eu market. following parliament’s vote, we now have the strong mandate we need to negotiate with the council.
in writing. − we voted this report to adopt the revised legislation on industrial air pollution, with stricter limits for nitrous oxide, sulphur dioxide and dust particles, which are harmful to both health and the environment. i believe that there should be a uniform integrated authorisation system for all installations in the eu, operating under the same emission standards (best available bat techniques) and monitored and controlled on the basis of mandatory minimum requirements. this integrated approach is beneficial both for the protection of the environment and public health and for the sustainable development of european society. it creates new green jobs, ensures the supply of products, electricity and heat to citizens, without distorting competition within the eu.
in writing. − the european parliament's decision to ban illegal timber and to control its exact trajectory will reduce illegal logging and give consumers the opportunity to make informed choices about the products they use. eu legislation banning illegally sourced wood is a major legislative innovation at international level, from forests around the world that are devastated by illegal logging, to the eu market where timber and wood products are sold. the figures we have at this moment show that at least 20% of the timber and timber products that reach the european market come from illegal sources. each of the 27 member states must actively engage in the implementation of the new rules on wood sourcing control and apply sanctions to those who trade illegally harvested wood. it is clear now, more than ever, as europe and romania face catastrophic flooding with human and material losses, that deforestation has partly caused this situation. none of the member states should hesitate to apply criminal sanctions to those who trade illegally harvested wood.
in writing. − illegal logging is a significant contributor to deforestation, with the volume of industrial timber from illegal sources estimated at between 350 and 650 million m3 per year, representing 20% of global industrial timber production. deforestation, which occurs at a rate of about 13 million hectares a year, accounts for about 20% of global carbon emissions and is a significant contributor to the destruction of biodiversity. illegal logging also poses serious human rights problems, since in many countries forests are culturally and socially important to forest-dependent and indigenous peoples. i voted for this report because the proposed legislation promises to ban illegally harvested timber and punish unscrupulous traders.
in writing. − deforestation is responsible for up to 20% of carbon emissions worldwide. it causes excessive damage to ecosystems and threatens the invaluable eco-services they provide. large amounts of deforestation are carried out illegally, without any efforts to replant trees or otherwise manage the process to limit its negative impacts. illegal timber coming from third countries also competes unfairly with the eu forestry industry which, more often than not, is producing timber legally and in a sustainable manner. i therefore welcome this report and parliament’s successful negotiations with the council – it is an important piece of legislation which will help to address many environmental challenges, from biodiversity protection to climate change.
in writing. - the vote to postpone the sánchez presedo report is the european parliament's wake-up call to the council of ministers calling for stricter regulation of the european financial system. the initial proposal put forward by the council was not considered satisfactory by parliament and negotiations did not lead to an acceptable compromise. by postponing the report, we want to give the council time to come up with a proposal that better meets the needs of financial system oversight and that allows for the stabilisation of european economies, growth and the prevention of future crises.
in writing. − the ec has proposed a new architecture for the eu financial regulation, with a view to improving the quality and consistency of supervision, increasing the effectiveness of legislation and enforcement, and better identifying risks that the financial system may face. it was decided to set up a european system of financial supervisors, composed of a network of national financial supervisors, to work with three european supervisory authorities: the european banking authority, the european insurance and occupational pensions authority and the european securities and markets authority. the establishment of the european insurance and occupational pensions authority should be accompanied by the development of a single set of rules to ensure consistent harmonisation, uniform application, and to help the internal market to function effectively without unnecessarily complicating legislation and its implementation. member states, in cooperation with the european insurance and occupational pensions authority, should ensure consistent harmonisation, uniform application of this directive by applying common technical standards on authorisation, notification, information and publication procedures and by regular exchanges of information and experience and closer cooperation, thereby preventing distortions of competition and creating the conditions necessary to ensure the smooth functioning of the cross-border affiliation.
in writing. − the new rules on bank bonuses adopted by the european parliament would put an end to incentive policies in this system, even under conditions of excessive risk. the measures are welcome two years after the financial crisis began, as the bonus culture has had serious negative consequences on the global economy, with every european taxpayer now having to pay. the banking system may be quick to accuse the union of interfering in its own policies, but in fact it is only protecting the taxpayer, whereas the banking system has often looked after its own interests, ignoring those of consumers. changing the philosophy of bonus-giving in the banking system, judging by the long-term rather than short-term profits of banks, will make europe partly immune to economic slide. in addition, each banking institution must behave responsibly and accept that there must be an appropriate ratio between fixed remuneration and the amount of bonuses. it is good that parliament has also decided that there must be a fair balance between bonuses and pension policy. it is normal for a banker to receive a pension commensurate with the results that the financial institution he has led has achieved.
in writing. − as regards capital movements, the effects of globalisation have significantly influenced financial markets. thus, in addition to their role in controlling inflation, central banks have had to introduce a new objective into their agenda, namely the stabilisation of financial markets. the crisis has highlighted important oversight gaps. unfortunately, the accumulation of excessive risks in this sector could not be prevented and, at the same time, there were numerous weaknesses in macro-prudential supervision. i voted in favour of the report because i believe that the european union urgently needs a new financial architecture that includes integrated micro-prudential supervision. this will enable us to identify and prevent future risks that could threaten financial stability at european level.
in writing. − during this crisis, it has become clear that the european union has not been able to manage crises caused by crossborder financial institutions in an efficient and effective manner. the commission notes that the bank of greece has not provided any evidence that the bank of greece has been able to achieve its objective of maintaining a stable and stable financial situation. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that there is a need to create a european crisis management framework with common legislative rules applicable to all banking institutions operating in the eu. i also believe that these rules should promote the stability of the financial system and strengthen the internal market for financial services and its competitiveness.
in writing. − i consider iceland's accession to the european union to be beneficial for both sides: iceland will enjoy greater economic stability and the european union will play a more active role in the arctic region. however, there are several shortcomings that iceland needs to address by the time of accession. one of them is the reform of financial supervision. iceland is part of the european economic area and applies the community acquis in the field of the single market, but full compliance with it is needed in the areas of conformity assessment, accreditation and market surveillance. another issue that needs to be addressed is the independence of the judiciary. i voted for the resolution, expressing my hope that iceland will succeed in meeting these conditions, which i consider essential for the proper functioning of the union as a whole.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution as iceland's accession would allow the union to play a more active role in the arctic region and would contribute to multilateral governance in the arctic. i hope that the negotiations will proceed in a constructive manner and that they will give iceland the opportunity to move closer to the european model. as regards eu accession, national public opinion has changed considerably since the summer of 2009 and opposition to accession has never been so high, i believe that in the near future the authorities should organise a broad information campaign on the implications of this process so that icelanders can make an informed decision in the forthcoming referendum on accession.
mr president, we need a proactive foreign policy, guided by our european common goals and based on our common values. this policy should recognise the indivisibility of security in the globalised world, this being a source of solidarity of interest, both within and outside the european union. such a policy, aimed at increasing the european union’s capacity for providing security to its citizens and improving its capacity to shape the global environment, not only to react to changes, requires an adequate institutional instrument – an efficient european external action service. we should not forget that this service is not a decision-making body. it is a community instrument that will have to implement foreign policy and external action decisions and, before that, support and facilitate the decision-making process under the authority of the high-representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy/vice-president of the commission and in coordination with other relevant institutional actors. parliament’s main concerns were clearly expressed, ensuring political oversight and accountability of the service, including in its budgetary dimension. this in turn requires transparency in the functioning of the service and clarity through the presentation of a consolidated budget of the european union external action. in this way, the parliament can check whether the means match the policy and ensure the policy’s effectiveness. this report and the agreement it stands for meet the above-mentioned european parliament demands. moreover, a process of fine tuning and revision is provided for, so as to tackle in due time the unforeseen problems and deficiencies that may arise. mr president, the creation of the european external action service is a big step forward in the right direction. moreover, it will be a major change of pattern. if, as a rule, bureaucracy slows down courageous initiatives, this time we expect to accelerate one, namely foreign policy integration within the eu. my remarks address the apparent gap between our current efforts to provide the service with a solid legal and administrative base and the reality of manning it because, while we are fiercely debating important principles like geographic balance and corrective measures, job interviews are taking place in parallel. according to opinions explained by those interviewed from the new member states, the process seems to entail little hope for them – which, if true, would be both sad and unfair. therefore, i think that those in charge should be convinced that in the end, one way or another, the principles agreed upon in this house will have to be complied with –the sooner the better.
we are entering a decisive stage in the creation of the european external action service. it is desirable that all the legislative elements necessary for the launch of the service are adopted as soon as possible. this will enable the service to be operational by the end of the year and to have all three sources provided for in the treaty in its structure. what is not clear, however, at this stage, is how the geographical balance of the staff of the european external action service will be achieved. the new member states, and in particular member states such as romania, which joined in the last stage of the 5th wave of enlargement, have a negligible presence in the structures that currently manage external relations. i want to know how the high representative intends to correct this situation. i personally do not think there is a very clear view of the real disparities that are being announced in terms of geographical balance, including at management level.
mr president, the european parliament should have a strong and united position on the long-lasting crisis in albania. i am deeply concerned about the institutional and political crisis that albania has already faced for a year now, as well as about the attitude of the governing majority which is impeding all compromise with the opposition and leaving the country in a permanent state of instability. i urge the majority to negotiate closely with the opposition and to welcome the permanent support of the two main political groups in the parliament in order to reach a political solution – a positive one for the country –to ensure that albania has a stable outcome from this crisis and to guarantee that in all future elections the democratic will of the albanian citizens will be fully respected, while ensuring full and uninterrupted parliamentary activity. in the end, prime minister berisha, instead of trying to pronounce my name correctly in the albanian parliament, you must realise that european integration is at stake. the free-visa regime might be only the first step but the copenhagen criteria are the prerequisite.

important football match in south africa tonight. i recall that when i was in south africa a few years ago i was taken for a drive outside of johannesburg up into the country. the person driving me was talking about the problems of hiv and aids in south africa – an issue which has been taken up by many people and not least by someone i have had the privilege of working with, annie lennox, the singer. as we drove through the countryside the driver said, ‘pick a village, pick any village that you like in the next hour’. we drove along and i said i saw many villages but i would choose that one. i pointed to a village, we drove into the village and he drove me to the graveyard. he said that in africa the tradition is that you do not lay the headstone for one year after the death of a person, so any crosses that you see, small crosses, represent people who have died within the last year. i went to this graveyard and there were hundreds of them. he said to me very simply: those are the victims of aids. honourable members, what i saw was the tragedy of an unnecessary devastation and i pay tribute to the honourable members who have put forward this resolution and promise to do my best to support its implementation.
in writing. the number of people living with hiv continues to rise, with estimates showing that 33.4 million people worldwide are infected with hiv/aids, of whom no less than 2.7 million were infected in 2008. i believe that both the european commission and the council must step up their efforts to address hiv/aids as a global public health priority, placing human rights at the heart of prevention and treatment of this disease and of care and assistance to those affected. these two institutions should encourage countries most affected by hiv and aids to develop coordinated national hiv policy frameworks to ensure effective hiv prevention and care. the european commission, member states and the international community must urgently adopt legislation to ensure access to effective and affordable hiv medicines, diagnostics and technologies for the prevention, treatment and palliative care of hiv infection.

in writing. adapting the cap to new socioeconomic realities is a necessity, and to do so we need to answer some key questions. i completely agree with the need for food security. but how independent do we want to be, and how much are we willing to pay extra for it? so far, the cap has kept food prices high, which in other countries cost less. the eu cannot promote free trade and protect its agricultural market. solutions must be found so that the eu imposes its own quality standards on the world, so that the discrepancy between the prices of agricultural products in different countries is reduced. but i am most concerned about the effect of the cap reforms on farmers. the decoupling has done nothing but direct payments to the big landowners; they are not necessarily the farmers! the decoupling is necessary to avoid overproduction, but i ask the commission to propose fairer criteria so that farmers are the real beneficiaries of the cap. we need incentives for farmers, and especially to encourage young people to go to rural areas, and that will not happen by maintaining the current system of direct payments which is absurd.
in writing. at the beginning of european integration, the common agricultural policy not only ensured food security for the population but also provided the basis for the modernisation of european agriculture and the development of other policies. however, the european union (eu) recently added 12 new members. this means that the eu's pre-2004 agricultural population of 6 million has increased by a further 7 million, and its agricultural area has increased by 40% from 130 million hectares to 185 million hectares. when the new member states joined, they expected that their producers would eventually benefit from the cap subsidies to the same extent as those of the old member states. however, this requires that the resources allocated to the agricultural policy are not reduced in the period after 2013. the eu must take account of the different situations and needs of the member states, as european agriculture can only serve the interests of the member states, producers and all citizens if it does not lead to an unfair distribution of resources due to modernisation differences.

on behalf of the ppe group. – madam president, human trafficking in north korea remains a serious problem. reportedly 80% of north koreans in china end up as trafficking victims. women are particularly vulnerable to prostitution, rape, arranged marriages and bride traffickers. many victims of trafficking are unable to speak chinese and are held as virtual prisoners. the legal status of north koreans and the chinese government’s policy of detaining the refugees and sending them back to north korea increase the refugees’ vulnerability to trafficking for purposes of forced labour and sexual exploitation. they have no protection from the authorities in either china or north korea, and there is little recognition of their plight from the international community. china must change its law to protect the victims of trafficking instead of returning them to north korea. finally, if people are killed, tortured and illegally imprisoned, it is a matter of urgency every day.
the human rights situation in north korea is particularly dire. the government of this country bans all forms of political opposition, democratic elections, freedom of the press, and freedom of religion. we cannot remain indifferent to the suffering of the people of north korea, as they lack access to basic food or humanitarian assistance. i am particularly concerned about the plight of women and children in north korea, as over a third of them suffer from malnutrition. according to reports, over 150,000 north koreans continue to be held in six labor camps. they have no health care and very little food, and the november 2009 monetary reform failed and caused the poverty level of the population to rise. i believe that the european union should support the establishment of a un commission of inquiry to investigate human rights violations in north korea.
human rights violations in north korea are so numerous that it is impossible to compile a complete list. perhaps the most serious of these is the starvation of the population and the differential distribution of food between those close to the regime, the power, and those who are not. according to amnesty international, last year some 9 million north koreans, more than a third of the population, suffered from hunger. the situation of collective punishment is also extremely worrying, sometimes up to three generations of people being sent to prison systems dominated by brutality, torture, forced labour and, as mr tannock said, public executions. most of those sent to these camps are never released, and if they have children, they may spend their entire lives in captivity. in conclusion, although the north korean government has agreed to participate in the un human rights council's universal periodic review, it is serious that it has not yet accepted any of the recommendations it has received in this framework.

in writing. the human rights and humanitarian situation in north korea remain sensitive issues of concern to the european union as an international actor promoting human rights on a global scale. on the other hand, the united nations, in its resolution of 25 march 2010, expressed concern at the serious violation of civil, political, economic, social and cultural rights in the democratic people's republic of korea. the decision by the government of north korea to refuse to cooperate with the un through mechanisms to promote human rights, including through the mandate of the special rapporteur on the humanitarian situation in north korea, is regrettable. the union has a duty to urge north korea to respect human rights. the eu must also act independently to help the people of north korea, both by continuing humanitarian aid programmes and maintaining communication channels within north korea, and by granting asylum to north korean refugees arriving in member states. the appointment of a european union special representative for north korea would allow for closer monitoring of the human rights situation in the country and better coordination of member states' responses to the issue.
the bilateral safeguard clause in the free trade agreement between the european union and the republic of korea constitutes a necessary safeguard in case korean imports threaten to cause serious injury to union industry and european jobs. the principle of customs duty drawback, whereby korean companies are allowed to reimburse customs duties for important components, is a particularly sensitive one, which could benefit the latter and significantly affect european competitiveness. the free trade agreement between the european union and korea remains a positive one, as long as it respects the principle of fair competition. in this context, the commission will need to closely monitor the development of exports between south korea and the european union, in particular in sectors considered vulnerable, and act swiftly to remedy any irregularities. the monitoring system must also be strengthened to enable the representatives of the industries concerned, trade unions and social partners, and the european parliament as the direct representative of the citizens of the union, to raise the alarm and to request an investigation. the role of the european parliament in the control system and concerns about customs duty refunds are issues on which the parliament, the council and the european commission will need to find a compromise quickly. in this context, the vote on the report in this parliamentary session is positive and shows parliament's readiness to adopt this regulation as soon as possible.
a particular problem facing farmers is the unfair distribution of profits in the food chain, which affects the existence of adequate income for farmers. there are a large number of semi-subsistence farms producing mainly for their own consumption but very little for the market. inefficiency, high self-consumption of their production, and self-employed agricultural workers are the main characteristics of this type of agriculture. under these conditions, there are farms which will not be able to benefit effectively from the support provided by the common agricultural policy. as agriculture is one of the sectors most affected by the economic crisis, the european commission must provide and ensure measures to encourage farmers to produce sustainably and ethically, and to compensate for the investments made, thus striking a balance for the better functioning of the food supply chain in europe.
in the run-up to the recovery from the economic and financial crisis, the optimal functioning of the food supply chain is of particular importance. with citizens' purchasing power declining, urgent improvements are needed to avoid a spiral of consumer food prices. i believe that the asymmetric reaction of food prices to commodity price fluctuations is mainly related to the number of intermediaries operating along the supply chain. i support the adoption of instruments that promote and support short supply chains and markets where farmers can unload their goods. this will create a direct link between the consumer and the farmer, with the latter getting a larger share of the value of the final price, while the general public enjoys better prices.
in writing. the report prepared by mr bové certainly touches on one of the most sensitive issues of the day. the economic crisis has particularly affected farmers' incomes and measures are needed to bring farms and peasant households back on track. but measures are also needed to modernise them - because only by modernising them can we ensure their competitiveness and a reasonable level of income. i therefore allow myself to express a personal view: i believe that the report should have also dealt with the issue of rural development, which is one of the fundamental solutions to the problems of european agriculture, especially in the new member states.

in writing. the main concern of citizens at the moment is to overcome the economic crisis and its negative effects. that is why i strongly support the construction of a european economic governance capable of helping to overcome the crisis. the eu institutions must have effective means of acting. i therefore support the creation of the permanent structures needed for crisis management, as proposed by the european commission. the eu institutions must also monitor compliance with the stability and growth pact, including fiscal discipline. the budgetary and economic decisions of a state have a direct impact on the economic situation of all eu member states (a fact proven in practice, including by the greek crisis, and recognised by the treaty of lisbon). in the future, timely economic analyses by european commission experts would be extremely useful for crisis prevention and resolution. the establishment of the 'european semester' will give member states the chance to benefit from timely professional assessments and analyses of their budgets and macroeconomic performance, and the dialogue between the european commission and member state governments is therefore very useful. i would stress that the structuring of economic governance at european level must help states in difficulty. every crisis is a test of the application of the principles of solidarity and responsibility, a test of the coherence and efficiency of the european union.
in writing. the eu has a social market economy. the eu's economic and social development depends equally on an open, competitive market and on the number and quality of jobs that can provide decent living. the economic and financial crisis has had a dramatic impact on jobs in the eu. the unemployment rate has risen alarmingly over the last two years, from 6.8% (may 2008) to 10% (july 2010). that is why the main concern of european citizens is to keep their jobs. job creation requires substantial investment in areas that can increase the eu's competitiveness. i believe that the union should invest as a priority in the modernisation and development of energy and transport infrastructure, in agriculture, education and health, in economic and social cohesion and in an eco-efficient and competitive industrial policy that ensures sustainable development. however, these priorities should be reflected in both the eu and national budgets. in addition, to increase the eu's competitiveness and create jobs, the eu should set itself the objective of increasing energy efficiency and reducing energy dependence on traditional energy suppliers.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the free movement of workers within the union, because i consider that free movement is a fundamental principle of the eu and of the internal market. i call on the commission and the eu council to use the opportunity of the adoption of this regulation and to ask the member states to remove the existing barriers for romanian and bulgarian workers. barriers to the free movement of workers from member states which acceded to the union after 1 may 2004 constitute restrictions on the rights of citizens of those countries and may lead to illegal employment and social dumping. raising these barriers will protect both migrant and indigenous workers equally. achieving this objective ensures that the eu's fundamental principles are upheld and respected, and i hope that both the commission and the member states will show the necessary political will.

in writing. − the republic of moldova is one of the european states most severely affected by the economic crisis. in addition, the authorities in chisinau have been facing political uncertainty for more than a year, which can only accentuate the effects of the economic crisis on the population and on the government finances. the grant of some eur 90 million to moldova, exclusively and supervised for balance of payments and state budget financing, will help moldova to achieve the imf's macroeconomic targets and, in the medium and long term, will enhance the state's credibility on international financial markets. it is welcome that parliament and the commission will impose control mechanisms to ensure that the union grant reaches its destination. moldova is in a difficult political moment and the temptation of populist political gestures may arise in view of the upcoming snap elections. the assurances of prime minister filat and his determination to honour his commitments, which would only produce positive effects on the moldovan economy, are welcome. moldova needs a sign of goodwill from the international community because it's going through a difficult time. it is in the interest of the european union to extend its hand to have an economically and politically stable state on its eastern border.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament's draft legislative resolution on the granting of macrofinancial assistance to the republic of moldova. as shadow rapporteur for my political group, i called for the financial aid of up to eur 90 million to be granted as soon as possible. the republic of moldova, a member of the eastern partnership, has been severely affected by the financial and economic crisis. at the same time, it has undertaken important policy reforms, which need to be strengthened and accompanied by the implementation of european standards. i therefore see the granting of this financial support as a way of encouraging the momentum of the reform process.
in writing. − the economy of the republic of moldova has been severely affected by the international financial crisis, which has manifested itself in a deterioration of the budgetary position and an increase in external financing needs. in view of the deteriorating economic situation, the republic of moldova has requested macro-financial assistance from the european union. i voted in favour of this assistance because i believe that the european union must be involved, together with the international monetary fund, the world bank and other international institutions, in alleviating the delicate situation in which the republic of moldova finds itself. this aid will be a real support for the government in chisinau in terms of financing the balance of payments deficit and other budgetary needs. at the same time, bilateral relations between the republic of moldova and the european union will be strengthened, and the union will show its solidarity with a signatory state of the eastern partnership.

in writing. − all the more so now, when member states are facing a serious economic and social crisis, we need measures to create new jobs. in this context, the role of eu cohesion policy is crucial in developing the job-creating potential of a sustainable economy by reducing regional disparities and creating a society with full employment. we need to encourage regions to use the structural funds to finance national, local and regional projects and the european social fund to create better educational and employment opportunities. the european social fund is the solution for member states that want to invest in skills development, employment and training, retraining, career guidance for the unemployed, with the aim of creating more and better jobs. to support the communities and regions of the member states, we have asked the european commission to fund a pilot project to train and facilitate the exchange of best practice models for those directly involved in the management and implementation of european funds at local and regional level.

in writing. − i voted for the report on the job creation potential of a new sustainable economy because i believe that member states need to move towards a competitive, efficient and low-carbon economy. i therefore call on the union to develop a sustainable industrial policy and to involve the industrial sector in eco-innovation, in order to reduce the dependence of economic growth on the consumption of resources and energy and to reduce polluting emissions. i believe that to create jobs in the 'eco-efficient' economy, we need to invest in energy efficiency and the use of renewable energy and green technologies in buildings, transport and agriculture. call for a european employment strategy to achieve a sustainable economy as part of the eu 2020 strategy and draw attention to the role of regional authorities. i also call for the development of effective funding systems and tax incentives to support smes to ensure green innovation and production processes. finally, i believe that employment policy plays an important role in combating poverty and social exclusion and i urge member states to use the egf to promote new skills needed for 'eco-efficient' economic development.

in writing. − i voted for this report because it contains concrete proposals for a better functioning of the food chain and for ensuring fair incomes for farmers. improving the functioning of food chains should include differentiating and reviewing hygiene rules; decentralising and simplifying certification and control systems; promoting direct producer-consumer relations and short food supply chains; involving producers and consumers in the development of quality and fair trade criteria and environmental sustainability criteria for public procurement practices in the food sector (food services) as a means of increasing food quality and local economic development, while reducing food transport distance and dependence on agrochemicals; reducing losses along the food chain, most of which are linked to 30% of imports from member states; reviewing the european food chain, which should help 43 million people to develop closer links between local food producers and european food consumers; and closing the gap between the european food supply chain and the food supply chain, which should help 43 million people to achieve a better quality of life.

in writing. − the european globalisation adjustment fund is designed to support workers made redundant as a result of the changes taking place in the world economy. moreover, since 2009, the fund has also been intervening in support of those affected by the economic crisis, with a view to reducing the unemployment rate. i personally think it is appropriate to make the fund a permanent instrument of support for jobseekers and to complement the social policies of the member states. this would shift the focus to unlocking the potential of each worker, as a counterbalance to measures to support enterprises. it should also be noted that the globalisation adjustment fund is currently still facing difficulties with respect to mobilisation procedures and execution periods. given that the main problems facing the unemployed are vocational retraining and temporary assistance, measures to simplify the fund are absolutely necessary in order to speed up and make the mobilisation of aid more efficient.
in writing. − the assistance provided by the egf must be dynamic and able to adapt to the constantly changing and often unforeseen situations arising in the market. the purpose of this fund is to provide specific and targeted assistance to facilitate the reintegration into employment of workers who have lost their jobs as a result of serious economic disruptions in the labour market. calls on the member states to involve the social partners and to promote dialogue with the social partners and entrepreneurs from the very beginning of the preparation of egf contribution applications. i also call on the member states to use this fund to promote new skills in greening existing jobs and creating new green jobs and to promote lifelong learning, to enable workers to develop their personal careers and to contribute to improving the union's competitiveness in the context of globalisation. they also support the functioning of this fund after 2013 as an independent fund with its own budget. the commission and the member states need to work closely together to effectively monitor support for multinational companies and to make a strong commitment to creating jobs with rights, with a view to discouraging social dumping.
in writing. − recent eu statistics show that in the last year, due to the economic and financial crisis, the number of unemployed in the eu27 increased by 1.1 million. as a result, the number of calls for mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund increased from 18 to 46 between may 2009 and april 2010. also, although the number of applicant member states has increased from 8 to 18, 9 member states have not yet made use of the european globalisation adjustment fund. in view of all this, i voted in favour of the european parliament's motion for a resolution on the financing and operation of the european globalisation adjustment fund, as the effects of the economic crisis on jobs are likely to persist. this is why it is important to ask the commission to carry out the mid-term evaluation of the use of the european globalisation adjustment fund in advance and to revise the relevant regulation so as to reduce substantially the duration of the procedure for mobilising the fund. i would also like to draw the commission's attention to the redundancies in the public sector, which do not benefit from the existence of a similar instrument, although these redundancies are a direct consequence of the reduction in public budgets as a result of the current economic and financial crisis.
