in writing. − technological developments in recent years have forced professionals in many fields to adapt both in terms of skills and competences and in terms of the work they do. mass communication is one of the areas seriously affected by technological innovation. so the boundary between the journalist and his audience is no longer as sharply delineated, the roles have become interchangeable. the draft report on journalism and new media is therefore welcome. it also underlines the european parliament's desire to contribute to the creation of a continent-wide public sphere, to encourage a spirit of participation. i personally strongly believe that we need to encourage journalists to report regularly on the eu institutions and, at the same time, to regularly assess how the new media support the creation of this european public sphere. the european union should also be able to provide the necessary financial support to the countries of the region, in particular through the european regional development fund. at the same time, there is a need for a greater emphasis in the school curriculum on training courses for this new type of journalism. and as a recognition from the european parliament, i support the inclusion of new media in the journalism prize sections that we give out every year.
president of the council. - mr president, madam commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the values and principles of the european union are clearly set out in the treaties and in the charter of fundamental rights, which the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon has made binding. respect for the rule of law and respect for human rights, including the rights of persons belonging to minorities, are highlighted. the council therefore affirms its commitment to these values. the council has repeatedly expressed its support for measures to promote the integration of the roma. in fact, our heads of state or government, meeting in the european council, also recognised the very special situation of the roma in the union and called on the member states and the union to do everything possible to improve their inclusion. it is ten years since the council adopted a comprehensive directive prohibiting discrimination on grounds of race or ethnic origin in a number of areas. these include conditions of access to employment, vocational training, social protection including social security and health care, education, provision of goods and services including housing. all ethnic groups, and therefore of course the roma, are protected by this directive. the directive also contains a positive action clause, which authorizes member states to maintain or adopt specific measures to prevent or compensate for disadvantages linked to race or ethnic origin. some of you were present at the second european roma summit in cordoba in april. the council welcomed this important event, which brought together the main stakeholders. following the summit in june, the council unanimously adopted conclusions on 'advancing roma integration'. ministers unanimously recognised that a significant proportion of roma live in extreme poverty, discrimination and exclusion, resulting in low levels of education, inadequate housing conditions, poor access to employment and poor health. roma women and girls face particular difficulties, including the risk of multiple discrimination. in many cases, these conditions have deteriorated sharply in recent years and there has been a rise in the rejection of roma and the violent attacks to which they are sometimes subjected. we must take into account that while it is primarily the responsibility of all member states to promote the social and economic integration of the roma, cooperation at european union level also brings significant added value. the council therefore invited the commission and the member states to advance the social and economic integration of the roma, in the context of the decisions taken and the recommendations made by the union institutions, by ensuring the most effective use of existing policies and instruments. responsibility in this area is shared: all actors have a responsibility to work towards the integration of the roma, insofar as their respective competences are concerned, and the council plays its part. the council also stressed the importance of ensuring the active participation of civil society, local authorities and the roma themselves. i would also like to recall the concrete measures recently taken jointly by the european parliament and the council to facilitate the social inclusion of the least favoured citizens. we have recently reached agreement at first reading to amend the provisions governing the european regional development fund, which now allow support for housing improvements in the most severely marginalised communities in europe, which include many roma. the two institutions agreed - and this is crucial - that these interventions should always be part of an integrated approach. this approach includes in particular actions in the fields of education, health, social affairs, employment, security and measures to combat segregation. finally, i would remind you that the european social fund also makes it possible to finance actions against discrimination in general. the union must provide a safe environment in which differences are respected and the most vulnerable protected. this is the stockholm programme, which the european council adopted in december 2009. measures to combat discrimination and xenophobia must be vigorously implemented. the roma community is expressly mentioned in the stockholm programme, which calls for member states to join forces to ensure the full integration of vulnerable groups. like all citizens of the union, roma must enjoy freedom of movement and the right to protection and must not be discriminated against. as our societies grapple with the economic crisis, let us be careful not to scapegoat our fellow citizens who suffer most from exclusion. this requires a clear and honest understanding of the causes, consequences and costs of social exclusion. what can a population do without education, housing, health care, or worse, employment? in order to promote roma integration, we need to define an integrated approach that is in line with the legislation, european values and in which the stakeholders are actively involved. the situation of the roma is included in the trio presidency work programme adopted by the council in december 2009 and the belgian presidency has planned to address the issue of roma integration on several occasions. firstly, at the conference on child poverty, which took place on 2 september last; the european council will be meeting in brussels on 14 and 16 november, and will be discussing the future of the european union. the conference on the homeless scheduled for 9-10 december; the commission will also be present at the meeting of the integrated platform for roma inclusion, scheduled for 7-17 september. finally, as announced at the general affairs council on 26 july, the issue of roma integration will continue to be followed by the council of the european union.
vice-president of the commission. − mr president, let me start by thanking my co-commissioners, lászló andor and cecilia malmström, because there has been very close cooperation between our teams on the roma issue in recent last weeks. this allowed the commission to reach a clear and balanced position on the matter over the summer, and this has received the full backing of the college of commissioners today. i would also like to thank president barroso, with whom i have been working closely on this matter over the summer, in parallel with the evolving situation in france. it was in full agreement with the president that on 25 august i took a public position on the situation of the roma in france and on the need to uphold european law and the rights and the principles laid down in the charter of fundamental rights. the line taken by the commission – which, as politicians, you know perfectly well must always be aware of the dangers of being instrumentalised by national party political debates – has been consistent over the past weeks. firstly, member states are in charge of public order and of the safety of their citizens on their national territory. this means that, in spite of the important right of free movement, member states have to take measures against eu citizens who break the law. there can be no impunity under the umbrella of european free movement principles. under certain conditions, member states can even send eu citizens who have broken the law back home, provided that they observe the principles of proportionality and the procedural safeguards which are written into the eu free movement directive of 2004. secondly, in our european union, no citizen must become the target of repressive action just for belonging to an ethnic minority or to a certain nationality. this is clearly set out in the eu charter of fundamental rights, which prohibits discrimination on the basis of nationality or ethnic origin and which specifically prohibits collective expulsions. so there must be no collective punishment in europe and no stigmatisation of any ethnic group. every human being has their own rights and also their own obligations. thirdly, the social and economic integration of the roma – and you all know that, with 10 to 12 million members, this is the biggest ethnic minority in europe – is a challenge for all 27 member states, both for the countries of origin and for roma host countries. under the subsidiarity rule, it is the responsibility of member states to ensure access to housing, education, health and employment but, at the same time, the eu institutions – for more than a decade now – have developed strategies and policies to support national efforts financially, notably via the european social fund, the pre-accession instrument, and the european regional development fund, which has recently been modified so that housing for roma can be covered by the fund. it is very important to stress that, for the commission, the social and economic integration of the roma is not an issue just for the month of august. it is an issue for every day and for every year. commissioner andor and i presented earlier this year, on 7 april, a strategic roma communication – the first ever in the european union. on the basis of that, we had a ministerial meeting in córdoba, together with the roma associations. as president barroso said this morning, there were only three ministers present at that meeting. the main legal and political issues raised by the measures taken by france this summer have been well summarised in a detailed note which commissioner andor, commissioner malmström and i presented to the college of commissioners last week and which was endorsed today. allow me to update you on where we stand today. first of all, thanks to a very intense dialogue between the commission and the french authorities over the past weeks, i see an important development. i viewed it as crucial that it was made clear in france that there was no intention to target actions against the roma community, because such targeted action would have been incompatible with the fundamental values and rights on which the european union is founded. that is why it was so important that minister éric besson came to a meeting in brussels with cecilia malmström and myself last week. he assured us publicly that the french authorities would treat all citizens in the same way, that there was no targeted action against the roma or any other group, and that the french authorities would do their best to act scrupulously in line with eu law. i see this assurance given by a french minister as a very positive development. in the meantime, the commission’s services – dg justice and the legal service – have continued to check at a technical level with the french authorities since last friday to see if what has been said reflects the legal reality on the ground. the commission services have identified a number of issues where the french authorities will need to give supplementary information, and where they will need active assistance by the commission services to ensure that their action now and in the future is fully in line with eu law. since 2008, the commission has insisted to france that the eu free movement directive must be fully implemented, including the procedural and substantive safeguards in that directive which had not been fully implemented in french legislation. even though these safeguards are partly a reality in france because of the case law which the courts use – and you have seen lately that the courts have decided on the basis of the eu directive although this eu directive has not been implemented in french law – we have been very clear with the french authorities in saying that legislative implementation will enhance legal certainty in free movement situations similar to the ones experienced this summer. that is why, after the meeting of the college today, i sent a letter to the french authorities insisting on those aspects. it goes without saying that other member states which are in a similar situation will also get similar assistance. an important lesson to draw from the developments of this summer is that roma integration is a challenge that must be kept on the political agenda of all member states. that is why, with cecilia malmström and lászló andor, i have agreed on five actions, which the college of commissioners has just approved. firstly, in order ensure the conformity of all member state measures taken regarding the roma with eu law on free movement, non-discrimination and the charter of fundamental rights, we will monitor and assess the progress made on these questions. secondly, we will establish a roma task force at senior level which will analyse the follow-up given by member states to the commission’s strategic roma communication of 7 april. this will in particular streamline, assess and benchmark the use and effectiveness of eu funding for roma integration in all member states and identify underpinning deficiencies in the use of those funds. we are we doing this simply because we want to know and to have proof of instances where these funds are (a) not being used and (b) if they are being used, are not being properly implemented. the first findings of this task force will be submitted to the college before the end of the year, and i will keep parliament and the council informed on these findings. thirdly, i am calling on the presidency to hold a jumbo jha, security and social affairs council as soon as possible in order to identify a more targeted use of national and complementary eu funding to promote social and economic integration of the roma. that council meeting should be followed by yearly meetings at ministerial level because we have had cold experience of member states not taking responsibility for changing things on their territory for themselves. we have to bring them together, officially and publicly, and we have to push them in the right direction. fourthly, i will call on future presidencies of the council to address the priorities identified in the roadmap agreed last june by the european platform on roma inclusion. in that context, dialogue with representatives of the roma community should be intensified. the next platform will take place under the hungarian presidency. fifthly, we will call also on the member states to look into the issue of human trafficking, to which roma are particularly vulnerable, with the assistance of the commission and, if necessary, with europol and eurojust where appropriate. i will now pass the floor to lászló andor to speak on the important subject of the use of the european social fund for roma integration.
member of the commission. − mr president, as vice-president reding has just pointed out, the european union is based on fundamental rights and values, and the commission is fully committed to commission and the member states in a wide range of areas of relevance to roma integration. the commission is committed to improving the effectiveness of instruments and policies in terms of both content and process, and stresses the importance of closer cooperation between eu, national and international players and roma communities. the communication also reaffirms the commission’s commitment to encouraging and assisting the member states to make full use of the potential of the structural funds to support the social and economic integration of the roma. eu structural funds offer a very integration of the roma. in hungary, this set in motion a dialogue between the national authorities and the roma under the auspices of the commission. a second series of high-level events involving in writing. i am convinced that radical measures cannot solve the problems faced by roma. we need accountability in action and the involvement of all european states in this process, however difficult this effort may seem. roma are european citizens and must enjoy all the fundamental rights guaranteed by european law - the right to establish their domicile and freedom of movement. failure to comply with them in france sets a risky precedent and may have long-term negative effects. i believe that we have an obligation to avoid incriminating and especially criminalizing a particular segment of immigrants, especially since the voluntarily repatriated roma had no criminal record. i also believe that the solution does not lie in the expulsion of roma citizens from one region of europe to another, or, worse, in collective expulsions. we need a united european action on the integration of this minority, a european strategy for the roma. the priority areas of this strategy should be education, health and facilitating access to the labour market. it is essential that we find together concrete solutions for the social inclusion of roma and that we do not allow roma to feel marginalised.
in writing. i would like to emphasise that the expulsions of roma citizens by the french authorities are not necessarily contrary to the treaty. the question must be examined on a case-by-case basis, since european citizens do not have an unconditional right to freedom of movement, but exercise that right in accordance with the provisions of directive 2004/38 which clearly lays down the conditions of residence. moreover, eu citizens can be expelled for reasons of security, public order and public health. the question of the illegality of these measures arises only if roma lawfully staying in the country have been expelled. on the other hand, roma, like other european citizens, have rights as well as obligations. the solution is to develop a coherent and effective european strategy for the social inclusion of roma to enable them to fulfil their citizenship obligations. eliminating discrimination by changing perceptions of roma is another vital element. neither france nor other member states should leave the entire responsibility for resolving the roma situation on romania's shoulders. the media spin in france and the exploitation of expulsions for electoral purposes is completely unconstructive. in this delicate matter we must show solidarity and responsibility, and our ability to do so is a test of the values that the union has affirmed over time.

in connection with efforts to promote active, healthy and dignified ageing, and a commission communication is scheduled for 2011. yesterday, the commission adopted the proposal for designating 2012 the european year for active ageing. the year will serve as a framework for raising awareness, identifying and disseminating good practice and, more importantly, encouraging policy-makers and stakeholders at all levels to facilitate active ageing. the aim is to invite these players to commit themselves to specific actions and goals in 2011, the run-up year, so that tangible achievements can be presented during the european year in 2012. i want now to talk about people more concretely. you have rightly pointed out that, in most member states, the bulk of support and care for dependent persons is provided by family and friends, and this will continue to apply over the next few decades. in all countries, women are far more likely to be carers than men. inadequate recognition of the role of informal carers and inadequate support for their contribution can lead to risks of social exclusion. to help remedy this situation, the member states, together with the eu institutions, could consider moves to assess and certify caring skills, including those acquired while caring for dependent relatives, and in household management, which are activities mainly performed by women. progress will depend on efforts by many stakeholders. the commission warmly welcomes the work on care issues carried out by parliament’s interest groups on ageing and on carers and by civil society organisations such as age and eurocarers. the commission is not planning to set up an active ageing observatory, but mutual learning covering active ageing is one of the aims of the european year of active ageing, for which a dedicated web site will be set up. i also want to mention the contributions of the grundtvig programme for adult education, the public health programme and the 2011 european year of volunteering. mrs lynne, you rightly underlined the importance of ethical issues such as those involved in ‘do not resuscitate’ orders. while the commission acknowledges the importance of this issue – and i fully share the moral substance of your question – we sometimes have to express ourselves in legalistic terms, and if we do that in this case, we must say that such matters are exclusively a member state competence and that we do not have the capacity, from the viewpoint of the charter of fundamental rights, to interfere with that member state competence. the commission has taken a number of initiatives – including the major conference it held on 17 march 2008 – to increase knowledge of the elder abuse issue and to promote debate at eu level on how to prevent it. in 2009, the commission implemented a pilot project which led to the selection of two projects. one project investigates how elder abuse can be monitored through public health and long-term care systems. the second seeks to map existing policy approaches and policy frameworks in the european union. both projects started in december 2009 and the findings will be presented in autumn next year. the commission also continues to co-finance a number of actions under the daphne programme and the public health programme. the commission is actively supporting work under way within the social protection committee on a voluntary quality framework for social services. that framework needs to be flexible enough to apply in all the member states at national, regional and local level and to a variety of social services. one big sector where the framework could apply is long-term care. but delivering long-term care is not an easy task on a daily basis, and it is the sad truth that people with heavy care responsibilities often have to give up, or reduce, their hours of paid work because of these commitments. in turn this affects their attractiveness on the labour market, their current income and their future pension rights. our longstanding work with the member states on reconciling family and working life has revealed the importance of adjusting the working conditions of persons who provide informal care. establishing social services that allow for respite care and care leave, and granting specific rights to informal carers in social security schemes, in particular as regards pension entitlement, would also help to encourage and enable more people to provide informal care. as you suggest, poverty, access to care and longevity may be interlinked. we looked at such links in a recent communication on health inequalities. the evidence clearly confirms that differences in income, working and living conditions are reflected in the average health status at all ages. however, we are only at the beginning in terms of policies that effectively break or modify the links between the social hierarchy and the hierarchy of health statuses. what we are calling for is therefore more awareness and research, and more innovative policy development. in addition, we need to promote a health-in-all-policies approach, which is a vital component of any successful strategy.

in writing. − the european union's concern for the welfare of animals in general and of those used for scientific purposes in particular is commendable, and in the light of the massive enlargement of the european community and technological progress, it was necessary to adopt a new directive to try to unify animal treatment practices. the protection of animals and the good treatment of them is a community value enshrined in a unanimously agreed protocol. the 1985 ec directive sought to eliminate discrepancies between the laws and regulations of the member states concerning the protection of animals used for experimental and other scientific purposes. since the adoption of that directive, however, the discrepancies between member states have increased, especially as the union has received new members since then. the resolution adopted by parliament is intended to reduce the differences in the degree of protection of animals used for scientific purposes in the member states, since we are all aware that this is necessary for the protection of human and animal health and the environment. the resolution is a step towards the unanimous goal of completely replacing animal experiments for scientific purposes as soon as this becomes possible with the coming discoveries.

in writing. the commission's november 2008 report shows that the overall impact of mobility flows since the eu's 2007 enlargement has been positive. at the moment, member states which maintain restrictions on the internal labour market should review their attitude. although, according to the transitional agreements to the accession treaty signed by romania and bulgaria, restrictions on the right to work do not constitute discrimination, it is not normal and moral, in the area of freedom, security and justice, to maintain such restrictions for so long after accession. it is time for the commission to take action to persuade those member states which still maintain restrictions to abandon them. how can we explain to european citizens of romanian and bulgarian nationality that here, we, their chosen ones, can offer equal rights to work to all legal immigrants and we can do nothing for them. the commission and the member states must act in the spirit of european unionism and implement the free movement of its citizens.
we have recently received the alarming news that products from cloned animals in north america have entered the european food chain. the european parliament has repeatedly expressed its view that these foods should be banned, for a number of ethical and environmental reasons, and we will continue to have a strong and united position on this during the negotiations on the new food regulations. evidence provided by the european food safety authority and the european group on ethics indicates the existence of serious health problems affecting both cloned animals and their surrogate mothers. at the same time, from an environmental point of view, the impact of increased meat consumption could be devastating, and large numbers of cloned animals would affect natural biodiversity, increasing the vulnerability of animals to epidemics and thus threatening food security. we've already heard the arguments about trade and the rules of the world trade organization. we are told that we cannot ban these foods from entering the european union without breaking our obligations under the wto. but the european union decided to stop products from entering the market when there were doubts about the benefits to consumers, or concerns that consumers were being misled. we will consider all legal options to implement such a ban. moreover, looking at the bigger picture, we should insist that the wto rules also take into account such ethical and environmental considerations. there are serious arguments against food from cloned animals. there is, however, no clear evidence of the benefits they provide. it is time for the commission to propose a concrete solution to this problem, which also takes account of the vision of our forum, which is representative of the european citizens. we cannot allow experiments that jeopardize the health of citizens or the environment.
in writing. the ethical, medical or economic arguments against the consumption of food derived from cloned animals have already been discussed in the european parliament, and the arguments have not lost their validity. there is another argument, at least as important: european citizens do not want 'cloned' products on their plates. they're against the idea of feeding their children food that originated in a genetic experiment lab. a 2008 eurobarometer survey on the subject shows that a majority of europeans oppose cloning animals, especially for food. 84% believe that we do not have enough experience with long-term health and food safety to use cloned animals in food. 75% believe that cloning food for consumption is ethically unacceptable. the percentages are not small, and they send a very clear message. people do not want to consume products obtained by cloning, they do not trust and do not agree with these methods. we must complete and improve community legislation so that there is no longer any possibility of forcing or circumventing the principles or decisions in which we believe.
the liberalisation of postal services is planned for 2011, with the possibility for member states that joined the union after 2004 and those with a special topography to postpone the opening up of the postal services market to competition until 2013. however, in the field of postal services, it is essential that member states ensure that postal items are collected, sorted, transported and delivered to all european citizens, regardless of their location, once a day, at least 5 days a week, at the same price throughout the territory of a member state, in accordance with the universal service obligation. i draw attention to the need for member states, even in this period of crisis, to continue to maintain well-functioning postal networks with a sufficient number of access points, including in rural or sparsely populated areas. the directive on the completion of the internal market for community postal services requires member states to define their own arrangements for financing the universal service, while allowing them sufficient flexibility. the quality of postal services, the provision of decent working conditions for postal workers and the existence of guarantees regarding jobs, training and income of employees depend on this funding. i think it is absolutely essential that the commission should present us with a study by the end of this year on the impact of the liberalization of postal services in the countries which have opened up competition in this field completely. finally, i would draw attention to the need to diversify the activities of postal operators by providing information society services.

the rapporteur. − this is the first readmission agreement since the entry into force of the lisbon treaty to be subject to the assent of the european parliament. on 18 september 2000, the council authorised the european commission to negotiate readmission agreements between the european community and pakistan. after several rounds of negotiations, the agreement was signed in brussels on 26 october 2009 by the european community and pakistan, after almost 10 years. the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon has made the union the legal successor of the european community, which means that the european parliament must also give its consent to the proposed agreement as from the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon. the committee on foreign affairs gave a favourable opinion and the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs voted in favour of the recommendation. the purpose of this agreement is to improve cooperation between the administrative authorities of the requesting and requested states in order to speed up the readmission procedure. in this respect, the agreement lays down the obligation to take back its own nationals and third-country nationals and stateless persons on the basis of full reciprocity and the technical provisions necessary for the readmission procedure. the aim of the agreement is to serve as an important tool in the fight against illegal immigration to the european union and to increase the security of citizens in the union. pakistan is a significant country of origin or transit for migrants who do not, or no longer, fulfil the conditions in force for entry to, presence in, or residence on the territory of any eu member state. the agreement with pakistan is also important from a regional perspective, as it will support the union's efforts to enhance cooperation with other countries in the region. the agreement contains a non-disclosure clause with respect to international law and data protection regulations. the return of natural persons remains the sole responsibility of the competent authority of the member state or pakistan. accordingly, they must comply with the requirements of international law. the agreement provides for the establishment of a joint readmission committee, which may adopt its rules of procedure. given that the joint readmission committee is the only european institution to participate in it, the european parliament asks the commission to provide it with regular information on the activities of the joint readmission committee. the agreement shall enter into force on the first day of the second month following the date on which the parties have notified each other of the completion of the confirmation procedures. i would like to thank the commission for its statement and for the critical remarks made by my colleagues, and i hope that on the basis of what i have said the house will vote in favour of this convention.
in this debate i would like to refer to the case of one of the third countries, namely the republic of moldova. in 2007, the european parliament ratified the agreement between the republic of moldova and the european community on readmission. this policy has, however, some shortcomings. its impact on the republic of moldova has been under-evaluated and the procedures for negotiating and implementing the agreement have not been sufficiently transparent. during the communist rule from 2001 to 2009, over 600 000 people migrated from the republic of moldova to the eu. one of the causes was the lack of respect for human rights. an example of this is the high number of convictions of moldova at the echr. to tackle these problems, the eu must ensure appropriate trade policies and increased development assistance. in this respect, i believe that the eu's initiative to provide financial assistance to moldova should be continued.

however, i would be happy to come back and discuss these issues with you at some other time. as regards pakistan, as some speakers mentioned, we have been discussing this readmission agreement with them for many years. i think you all agree that it is much better to have a european agreement with pakistan instead of several more or less obscure bilateral agreements. as a european agreement it can be monitored, it can be subject to control, it is much more transparent, we can discuss it here in plenary, we have greater leverage on issues such as fundamental rights and human rights, and we the rapporteur. - mr. president, i hope you won't be too hard on me, i only used three minutes and 20 seconds of my first four minutes. we are deeply moved by what happened in pakistan during the floods, and we are concerned to this day about all the human rights violations that are happening in pakistan and even in the world, but we are even more concerned about the human rights violations in countries that have signed the geneva protocol on the status of refugees. and we are even more concerned that colleagues are defending - and rightly so - the people of pakistan, speaking out against human rights violations, who may not recognize national minorities in their own eu country. i repeat what i said in the debate, that while human rights are important, this convention is not primarily about human rights. it's not just about that, it's about the fact that we are being asked to provide security by eu citizens, security by member states, and let me give you an example of what happened in the uk in may 2010, when two pakistani university students, abid nasser and ahmad faraz khan, were arrested on suspicion of terrorism, and the british court decided that sending the two students back would put their lives at risk and therefore they could stay in the uk. so when we talk about returns, we can of course rightly hold pakistan accountable for human rights violations, but first and foremost we can trust the judges and courts of our member states and make sure that the human rights of the person are not violated. pakistan falls far short of the requirements, but let's not forget that it has had a minority ministry since 2004, and it may be because of your critical comments that it has ratified two international conventions this year, the international covenant on civil and political rights and the 1984 convention against torture and other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. i have to say that perhaps that is why it was changed, because you were critical of this convention and ratified it, but perhaps i can also say that if you vote no tomorrow, you will be voting no confidence in the courts of your own member states. so i urge everyone to give pakistan a chance to move forward on this path after nearly ten years of negotiations, of agreement, and hopefully to sign the geneva convention that is still missing.
in writing. i would like to stress first of all the symbolic importance of this first readmission agreement concluded by the european union as an entity. in addition, pakistan is an important partner of the union, especially in the fight against terrorism, and there is a general consensus that the union needs to improve its strategy and become more involved with the country. i believe that a clear and well-established framework for cooperation on readmission with pakistan is necessary. in the absence of this agreement, we run the risk of member states returning illegal immigrants to this country outside any european legal framework and on an ad hoc basis. in that case, the union would have no say and, in particular, no possibility of requesting guarantees as regards respect for fundamental rights. it should be noted that the union will be represented in the joint readmission committee established under article 16 of the agreement, which will allow it to monitor the respect of fundamental rights in the context of readmission. in addition, the non-infringement clause in article 15 addresses concerns about human rights in pakistan.
turkey is the european union's seventh trading partner and the only candidate country to benefit from a customs union with the eu. turkey and the european union therefore enjoy a privileged relationship in which trade and economic exchanges play an important role. in this context, the two partners need to work together to align their trade policies, in particular as regards the conclusion of free trade agreements with third countries. the customs union must also be strengthened by including agricultural products, services and public procurement in the agreement and by resolving the issue of visas for turkish traders wishing to enter the territory of the european union. at a time when the effects of the economic crisis are still being felt, closer economic and trade cooperation between the two regional powers is becoming necessary. the european union must send a clearer signal to turkey in order to be able to convey to it the fundamental european values.
mr president, eu trade and economic relations with turkey are a matter of political significance, too. however, in spite of recognising this fact, the eu finds it increasingly difficult to avoid the impression that it is playing a game of ‘who blinks first’ with turkey. not willing to pay the price of interrupting the admission negotiations, it expects the turks to do so, exhausted by their length and complexity. the good news is that, according to the latest data, the turks are increasingly dissatisfied with the eu, and in spite of the latter’s leading position as turkey’s major economic partner, other partners like russia, china, united arab emirates, the us and iran are catching up fast. therefore, success in our commercial relations with turkey should not obscure the need to finally make up our minds on whether or not to accept turkey into the eu, given the impact of that decision on the international position of the eu.
i would like to start by welcoming the positive result of the constitutional referendum on 12 september. it demonstrates the attachment of the turkish people to the democratic regime, the only one acceptable in europe. the content of this report reaffirms the need for the harmonisation of trade policies between turkey and the eu. implementing effective measures to remove remaining technical barriers within the customs union would support turkey's european path. this country has demonstrated remarkable recovery potential in the economic crisis. although global demand has declined, the volume of foreign trade has doubled, and economic growth is expected to be 7% in the coming years. i would like to stress that relations between romania and turkey have evolved significantly in recent years. the two countries are the most important trading partners in the balkans, with annual trade exceeding $7 billion. in addition, turkey's participation is vital in the implementation of union-wide energy infrastructure development projects such as nabucco.
in writing. – i strongly support the report on trade and economic relations with turkey. furthering the eu and turkey’s interconnectedness through strengthened trade and economic ties will be of great benefit to both sides. the severity of the youth unemployment crisis in turkey has been highlighted; the removal of unnecessary barriers to trade and burdensome procedures will lead to increased trade volumes which will in turn positively impact on employment levels. efforts taken to complete the customs union should be supported, and especially its deepening to include agricultural products. such a development would be a sign of turkish commitment to completing necessary reforms. the resolution also calls for steps that would infuse an element of welcome dynamism into eu-turkey relations.
i would also like to congratulate mrs de lange on her work in setting up and running this dossier. the maintenance of natural ecosystems, the regulation of climate, water and air, soil fertility and the production of food, fuel, fibre, medicines, all depend on biodiversity. the european commission, but especially the member states, must actively engage in the conservation of the natural capital necessary for the sustainable development of communities, in terms of ensuring renewable resources, landscape and recreational value, protection and ensuring the ecological balances necessary to maintain a healthy environment. the good news would be an increase in the amounts allocated to the environmental financial instrument. even if it is still a small part of the union budget. additional investment platforms are needed and we need to find ways to encourage biodiversity-positive investments and, conversely, discourage investments that affect biodiversity, both in the public and private sectors. good practices need to be established in terms of effectiveness and added value of projects. i also share the rapporteur's view that the commission should consider all factors relevant to the sustainability of projects and introduce systematic monitoring of projects.
a very important report, congratulations to the lady reporter. i am referring to the key instrument in the union for the protection of biodiversity and ecosystems, which is the natura 2000 network, which covers 18% of the union's land area, and in romania, for example, 17.84%. according to the commission's financial estimates, the annual cost of managing the natura 2000 network is €6.1 billion, for example, for romania €342 million. given that we have to achieve this, we have to protect biodiversity, i believe that the commission should supplement the funds allocated to biodiversity protection in the new multiannual financial framework, starting in 2014, as well as a mid-term evaluation of the current budgetary framework, especially as the target of halting biodiversity loss by 2010 has not been reached.

in writing. eco-conditionality is part of the common agricultural policy and has many implications for soil conservation; it is also a control and sanctioning mechanism that leads to a reduction in direct support in the event of non-compliance with the standards set in the field of environment, public health, animal and plant health, and animal welfare. eco-conditionality refers to the requirement to maintain land in good agricultural and environmental condition. i believe that cross compliance should apply to direct income support payments as well as to most environmental payments applied in rural development and that member states should set this at national or regional level, in accordance with a common framework existing at european level.
i would like to point out a very acute problem currently in romania, but which exists, i am convinced, in some form in all the member states of the union. this is a serious situation that affects small businesses and cancels out their chances of developing and recovering from the economic crisis. the national council for small and medium-sized enterprises estimates that 8 out of 10 firms that have received european funding abandon projects for lack of co-financing. this is the case for all programmes with european funding and i believe that, in these circumstances, the union, on the one hand, and the member states, on the other, have a duty to identify and implement new measures to support small businesses, especially given that 70% of the workforce in the union is employed in them.
we will soon begin the mid-term review of the 2007-2013 multiannual financial framework, which must be the result of interinstitutional cooperation and must offer concrete solutions to mitigate the effects of the economic and financial crisis. the entry into force of the lisbon treaty and the eu 2020 strategy also provide a new perspective on the mid-term review of the current financial perspective. i ask the commission to be flexible and prompt when, under the erdf regulation, a member state requests the revision of operational programmes or the national strategic reference framework. the current economic crisis could lead to some changes in budgetary priorities, precisely to ensure adequate funding for priority areas. in this context, i call for the promotion of solidarity and efficiency in the field of energy resources, transport and agriculture infrastructure, broadband infrastructure in rural areas, priority areas that can ensure job creation.
social europe is at a turning point, with the echo of austerity measures manifesting itself in various strikes. we have the strike of the employees of education, transport, justice, administration and industry in france, we have the strike of the employees of transport in greece, or we have the strike of the unionists in romania. these social grievances will certainly intensify in the coming months. that is why i believe that our priority must be economic growth, but in close correlation with the creation of new jobs and the protection of existing ones. the responsibility for overcoming the crisis is shared. solidarity must be at the heart of european economic and social policies. increased support should therefore be given to member states that are experiencing difficulties in implementing economic recovery measures in order to avoid a deepening of the gap between member states' economies and to mitigate the painful social impact.
the issue i am addressing is one that concerns respect for the rule of law and professionalism in the administration in romania. at the beginning of 2009, there were changes of prefects and sub-prefects. the decisions appointing them provided that they were to hold those posts on a temporary basis until the competition for the permanent posts had been organised. at the end of september 2009, the executive organised these competitions, the results of which were announced at the beginning of october. the government was supposed to issue final appointment orders for the admissions, but it did not. in this context, i would like to draw the attention of the european parliament to the abuse by the romanian government and ask the romanian government to respect the principles of the rule of law and to promote professionalism in the administration.
there is no doubt that the eu 2020 goals put education and skills development at the forefront. in the current programming period, achieving economic, social and territorial cohesion is the main objective that creates the framework for developing education and skills to harness local resources. each region can be enhanced by ensuring the regional dimension in education and training. there are professions that are still practiced only in certain areas and that are on the verge of disappearing, just because they no longer have a chance to be in national vocational training programmes. the same is true of local resources that are only known in oral history. i argue that regions should be financially supported through appropriate programmes and encouraged in developing the regional component in vocational education and training. that is where european funds can come in, because otherwise many jobs will be lost.

member of the commission. − mr president, firstly i would like to thank the rapporteur, mr arias echeverría, and parliament as a whole for this wide-ranging appraisal of the european e-commerce market. this report serves as a timely reminder that the e-commerce market is not yet a reality for many businesses and consumers. a fragmented market for e-commerce is also a worrying symptom of the missing links within the wider internal market. most consumers have first-hand experience of the internal market when shopping online. it brings them into contact with sellers from all over europe. many sellers, especially smes, are keen to develop new markets thanks to the opportunities opened up by the internet. addressing the obstacles that citizens face in the online world can go a long way towards turning the promise of an integrated internal market into a reality. so what can we do to fill the gaps in the internal market and make e-commerce work better? the commission will reflect carefully on its response to the report. many of the points raised are addressed in various policy domains, including the digital agenda. in short, the report sketches out two avenues that we should explore. first, we need to make life easier and simpler for both consumers and businesses. we can do this by harmonising rules, for example on consumer contracts, and we can streamline procedures to make them less costly for businesses conducting cross-border transactions, for example, concerning waste management fees, copyright levies, vat reporting obligations and invoicing. in this context the commission welcomes the report’s support for a consumers’ rights directive, which is currently being considered in the committee on the internal market and consumer protection. we will make consumers’ lives easier by enforcing eu legislation, in particular in relation to the services directive, which prohibits geographical discrimination against consumers. improving delivery and payments issues will also be a key factor if we want to develop e-commerce. we can also make it easier for citizens and companies to interact with national administrations by setting up one-stop-shops. the commission has set up a dedicated group of commissioners for the digital agenda to ensure a joined-up approach to policy-making on digital issues. it is also committed to fostering self-regulatory solutions by looking at the possibility of setting up an eu trust mark for e-commerce to complement a code of online rights. second, we need to better enforce rules and monitor the internal market: rights that are not enforced in practice are worthless. alternative dispute resolution, as mentioned in the report, can provide low-cost, simple and quick redress for consumers shopping on the internet. we will explore how best to improve adr in the eu and come forward with a proposal for an eu-wide online dispute resolution system for e-commerce transactions by 2012. we also intend to ensure that consumers in mass-claim situations across the eu are able to obtain compensation. proposals for adr and collective redress are also planned for the end of 2011. knowing that public authorities are working together to keep a close watch on the internal market is a foundation for creating confidence. as part of the consumer protection committee, national authorities regularly cooperate to stamp out unlawful practices on the internet. the commission also monitors the e-commerce market through its yearly consumer markets scoreboard. earlier this month we launched an in-depth study of e-commerce. at the beginning of 2011, a communication will be dedicated to the evaluation of the application of the e-commerce directive and will reflect on its better enforcement. finally, i should like once again to thank everyone who has been involved with this very useful and inspiring report. let me also apologise on behalf of mr dalli, who is unable to be here for personal reasons.

in writing. security of supply will depend in the future on the evolution of the fuel mix, the development of production in the union and in third countries supplying it, investment in storage facilities and diversification of supply routes and sources within and outside the union. i am pleased that the proposal for a regulation has been amended by the european parliament to include an article on the nabucco gas pipeline project. this confirms that the european union institutions will continue to attach particular importance to the nabucco gas pipeline project in terms of its political and financial aspects. in concrete terms, this regulation guarantees the european household gas supply during the crisis, in order to avoid situations such as that of january 2009, when several member states were completely deprived of gas supplies. the european commission will have to coordinate these possible emergencies and ensure that each member state is protected.
madam president, i should today like to repeat once again something i have always said: relations between the eu and china are extremely important for both sides and for the whole world. this is even truer today, with china continuing its rapid growth and the eu still struggling with the crisis. the eu needs china and china needs the eu. until now, no real strategic agreement has been reached by the eu with beijing. my hope is that the forthcoming summit will finally be the right opportunity for us to speak with a single voice and to establish a strategic approach to our relations with china. commissioner, with the agenda now so close and so important, the following issues are essential within the strategic partnership for this autumn and next spring. first, in the g-20, europe and china need to build up a strong and effective partnership. second, there is cancun, with the lessons drawn from the eu failure on climate change in copenhagen. third, there is the issue of international aid and development, – not only for africa – with a view to working together to make the millennium development goals a reality, rather than just a holy promise.
we all know that the european union is not alone in recognising the opportunities that a smart and green economy offers for increased competitiveness and prosperity. china is one of the countries that has set similar priorities and is investing heavily in emerging industries, green technologies, information and communication technology and smart grids. in addition to close cooperation in these sectors of the economy, i believe that another priority area to be examined is trade. one of the driving forces behind growth, employment and investment in both the eu and china. we need to take action in bilateral cooperation to ensure that barriers to trade and investment flows are reduced and that trade is promoted based on well-defined rules. we should also strengthen the economic and political relations we have established with china, one of our main strategic partners.
madam president, it is now a fact of life that china, already the second economic and exporting power in the world, is moving towards the status of a superpower, forcing the us to pay it increasing attention. consequently, europe will soon have to compete with china for the favours of the us, while its power of attraction is fading away. under the circumstances, the eu’s own relations with china are given even more weight, not only commercially and economically, but politically, and perhaps even militarily too. however, in order for that to happen, we need to overcome the apparent division of labour between the institutions of the eu, often entrusted to play the ‘bad cop’ role in relations with china, and the individual member countries competing for the role of ‘good cop’ in their relations with this rising superpower.

in writing. − gas emits the least co2 of all fossil fuels, making it a key player in europe's transition to a low-carbon energy system. currently, a quarter of europe's primary energy consumption is gas, with almost 60% of the volume of gas consumed being imported. while the eu's 2020 targets for renewables, energy efficiency and greenhouse gas emissions reductions could help stabilise gas demand growth, the decline in domestic production could nevertheless lead to a situation where the eu's dependence on gas imports stays at the same level or even increases. the gas crisis between russia and ukraine in january 2009, which led to a 30% reduction in gas imports into the eu for a period of two weeks, clearly demonstrated that, in the current situation of increasing import dependence and supply and transit risks, the review of the existing gas security directive and the completion of the creation of a fully liberalised internal energy market are needed, and that there is a strong need to adopt measures to strengthen the security of gas supply in the eu.

member of the commission. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the commission has already made a number of proposals. we welcome your interest in developing an intelligent energy infrastructure keyword smart grids . we have limited practical experience with smart grids so far and the results of our studies must therefore be interpreted with caution. a study funded by the commission concluded two years ago that smart grids could reduce primary energy consumption in the eu energy market by almost 9% over ten years. based on our average electricity prices, this would result in savings of almost 7.5 billion euros per year. we also see advantages in the field of technology and safety for the market and for consumers. smart grids allow for better tracking of electricity flows through intelligent monitoring and can thus reduce grid losses and increase the security and reliability of the grid. on the other hand, consumers can also better control and manage their energy consumption. these benefits are not zero-rated. this requires massive investment from both the public and private sectors. some member states have taken the first steps towards setting up the networks. sweden, for example, italy, with almost 100% of their customers already equipped with smart metering systems. we have pilot projects in france, germany, the netherlands, spain and the united kingdom. the commission is promoting the widespread adoption of smart metering and the development of smart metering networks beyond the scope of the new directive. we set up a smart grids working group in november last year. we have to look at the industry, the regulators and the consumer organizations to see if it is appropriate, we have to look at incentives and requirements, we have to look at where there is a need for regulation and we have to look at whether further standards of technology make sense. we shall be presenting the results of the working party to parliament next year. the communication on regional initiatives mentioned by the honourable member has several objectives and is not only focused on smart grids. the purpose of the forthcoming commission communication on this subject is to consult the regulatory authorities of the member states and other stakeholders on the commission's views on electricity and natural gas with regional interconnection. this means that we want to balance objectives, tasks, regions covered and the management of regional initiatives accordingly. the role of the agency for the cooperation of energy regulators (acer), which will be operational in the spring of next year, should also be highlighted. all in all, we want to achieve europe's energy objectives not only on a europe-wide basis but also in regional cooperation. we are expressly supporting this with our measures.

member of the commission. - madam president, i have to say that i am very sorry. i would like to thank you on behalf of my colleague, mrs connie hedegaard, who has already made her position very clear in public on this matter, for the question which comes at the right time. connie hedegaard is unable to be here today because she is in new york in the context of the ongoing climate negotiations. the icao assembly will be held, as you know, from 28 september to 8 october, and climate protection is, in principle, at the top of the agenda. the icao council, which met last week to prepare a resolution on air transport and climate protection, was unfortunately unsuccessful. the eu's unilateral commitment to reduce co2 emissions by 20% below 1990 levels also includes emissions from aviation. these have not been subject to any other international reduction targets, and that is about to change. air emissions have almost doubled since 1990 and are expected to continue to rise. for 2020, we expect them to be 70% higher than in 2005. by 2050, it is estimated that the number of jobs will have increased by between 400% and 500% compared to 2005. the european union's action to tackle the climate impact of aviation has been a focus since the european parliament and the council decided in 2008 to integrate aviation emissions into the eu emissions trading system from 2012. this concerns all flights to and from the eu. airline operators around the world have already begun preparations for this. they all have to contribute to climate protection in the european emissions trading system, unless the home countries have comparable systems to reduce emissions from international aviation. the eu's position for the forthcoming icao negotiations was confirmed by the council at the beginning of september, with the adoption by icao of a 10% greenhouse gas reduction target for international aviation by 2020 compared to 2005 and the establishment of a common framework to support market-based actions to reduce aviation emissions by icao. the eu is prepared to exclude flights from third countries from the ets on a bilateral basis if that country implements appropriate climate protection measures for transport. you know that we disagree with the united states and other icao members on the issue of air traffic emissions. the us demand for a mutual agreement, i.e. for mutual recognition of climate change measures, is directly opposed to the implementation of european measures. but we will not allow our partners to undermine eu legislation, especially as we believe that this measure, which will account for one third of global aviation emissions, is a key contribution to the fight against climate change. we cannot accept that those who want to do more to combat climate change need the permission of those who want to do less. there is no veto over the climate protection legislation of other states. but it is also impossible for serious climate action to create a competitive disadvantage. if we were to apply eu rules only to european airlines, it would be discriminatory on grounds of nationality, it would undermine the fight against climate change and it would be economically pointless. mutual agreement is the magic word for continued inaction in the fight against aviation emissions and climate change. the european union must and will remain firm in the forthcoming negotiations. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the european parliament is able to exercise its right of initiative. on the contrary, we need a common approach and a global reduction target to reduce aviation emissions in a sustainable and long-term way.
the world economy is increasingly dependent on air travel. statistics compiled by the european environment agency showed that in 2005, 20% of total carbon dioxide emissions were generated by air transport. research into new engines and fuels will obviously reduce these emissions. according to a recent study, today the standard fuel efficiency of an a380 jet engine is 3 litres of fuel per 100 kilometres per passenger, which means that it is perfectly comparable to that of a modern diesel car. in order to open up the market for air transport services, the union shall negotiate framework agreements with third countries on certain aspects of air services. an example of this is the agreement recently signed between the european union and canada. i believe that these agreements should explicitly contain provisions on the reduction of aviation's impact on the environment. article 25a (1) of directive 101/2008 provides that, where a third country adopts measures to reduce the climate change impact of flights departing from that country and landing in the community, the commission will examine the options available to ensure optimal interaction between the community scheme and the measures available in that country. i ask the commission to provide examples of such successful interactions. article 25a (2) of directive 101/2008 also states that member states and the community shall continue to work towards agreement on comprehensive measures to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from aviation. with a view to such an agreement, the commission should consider whether amendments to the existing directive are necessary. commissioner, is the commission considering such changes?
the inclusion of aviation in the eu its is an important step forward in the fight against climate change, because this change is occurring at a global level and the legislation in force needs to act at this level. application of the directive in its current form from 2012 onwards will facilitate this. requiring third countries to icao to participate in the scheme on a voluntary basis only slows down progress in this area. meeting this demand will not only reduce the competitiveness of european airlines but also hinder the fight against climate change. the commission will also continue to monitor the implementation of the union's policy on aviation security and will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's policy on civil aviation security. i ask the commission and the council to involve the european parliament in the negotiations with third countries to obtain the mandatory inclusion of companies from these countries in the emissions trading scheme. this does not diminish the progress made in creating the single european sky, which will reduce air routes and further facilitate fuel savings.
the council dealt mainly with the union's external relations. but let us not forget that the economic situation is the problem facing the european citizens today. it is good that an agreement has been reached on the european semester, but unless the european commission has an implementation mechanism including sanctions, this agreement is useless. sanctions must exist, but they must not allow citizens to be punished twice: once by inefficient governance and a second time by reducing european union support. the proposed measures must help to prevent deficiencies, not allowing a situation to be reached which already produces negative effects. on the roma issue, all european citizens are obliged to respect the law. all member states are obliged to comply with european law. anyone who does not, whether a citizen or a member state, must bear the consequences. in this case, however, i believe that punishing citizens - or member states - does not solve the fundamental problem. the roma situation can only be solved by a european policy. i am convinced that all member states, whether of origin or transit, can produce a list of different measures to support roma integration. i believe that a european policy means a single list of measures and programmes to be applied identically and simultaneously in all the member states. and i also believe that implementing this idea doesn't require more responsibility or more money - just political will.

in writing. − pharmacovigilance is the process and science of monitoring the safety of medicines, including the collection and management of data on the safety of medicines, the evaluation of these data to detect the presence of a safety concern, the actions to be taken to correct it, including reporting on the issue, and the evaluation of the procedure used and the results obtained. under current eu legislation, medicines can be authorised in two ways: (a) through a centralised procedure whereby a pharmaceutical company submits an application to the emea (european medicines agency), as provided for in eu regulation no 726/2004, or (b) through a mutual recognition system whereby a country carries out an evaluation of the new medicine and establishes coordination with other member states through mutual recognition. i support the report because consumers and healthcare professionals should have full access to the central european eudravigilance database to prevent the recurrence of adverse drug reactions, which could be prevented by facilitating access to validated information. this is an effective way of addressing disparities between member states in the provision of information on adverse reactions to medicinal products. public access to eudravigilance is necessary to restore citizens' confidence in the ability of health authorities to protect public health.

for the third year in a row, the european parliament adopted a resolution on human rights violations in the democratic republic of congo. it's a sign of major concern in this regard, but, we have to admit, also of inefficiency. we've been condemning rape as a weapon of war since 2008, and here's the un estimating that the average reported rape in the first quarter of this year was 14 a day. in late july and early august, the grim record was set of over 500 gang rapes in just five days. the fact that the un troops in the world's most expensive peacekeeping force only learned about these barbarians after two weeks, even though they have a military base only 30 kilometers away, is telling about the failure of the un mission to stop the violent conflict with strong regional implications. this escalation of atrocities ironically preceded the report of the united nations high commissioner for human rights. since then, however, millions of congolese have been victims of brutal violations of basic rights, and impunity for the perpetrators has continued to be the unshakable rule. i believe that a full investigation is needed to establish responsibility for the mass killings, including by the neighbouring countries involved in the conflict, especially rwanda. there was a genocide in the great lakes region in 1994, and some of the perpetrators are now facing the international criminal tribunal for rwanda. i believe that the establishment of the rule of law is one of the essential premises of stopping conflicts and massacres. without justice, there can be no peace. this is also demonstrated by the experiences of the former yugoslavia, sierra leone and cambodia. that's why i think the un report should be the starting point for the creation of an international criminal tribunal for the people's republic of congo.
margot walström, the united nations special representative on violence against women and children in armed conflict, called the democratic republic of congo the "rape capital of the world". the truth is, however, that if we look at the figures that are made available to us by various organizations, we see nothing but barbarism, horror, unacceptable suffering. 14 women raped per day in the first quarter, several hundred women and children subjected to this torture between july 30 and august 2, 200,000 victims of sexual violence from 1996 to the present. behind all these figures, as i said, is an intolerable suffering, especially as we are 10 years after the adoption of security council resolution 1325. i think we should consider sanctions against the leaders of the democratic forces for the liberation of rwanda.

transatlantic relations are a priority in european foreign policy. mobility is at the heart of the concept of european citizenship as laid down in the charter of fundamental rights and the treaties. free movement within the schengen area and the right to move to third countries are the same for all european citizens and therefore also for the citizens of the new member states. in this context, we continue to express our regret vis-à-vis the unjustified exclusion of millions of european citizens from 4 member states, including romania, from the special mobility partnership between the european union and the united states. the colleagues expressed concern about the promotion of the esta system, which in effect reintroduces a quasi-visa for all european citizens. the fee is not just $14 but it's also collecting personal data from eu citizens. the us department of homeland security is currently assessing the application of this visa fee. the commission must work with the american side to find a solution to eliminate it. i would point out that the maintenance of the decision may have an unforeseen impact on other pending transatlantic security and mobility related issues, such as the future eu-us pnr agreement. if the us administration does not waive the fee, we will support the commission in the necessary steps to apply reciprocity to all us citizens travelling to the european union, in accordance with the fundamental principle of the european union's visa policy.
the conclusions of the last european council state that the transatlantic relationship is based on common values. the reality is this: american citizens can enter the union freely. the european union has accepted the pnr and swift agreements on the personal data of european citizens. some european citizens still need a visa to travel to the united states. in addition, every european citizen is fingerprinted on entry to the united states, whether or not he has a visa. european citizens have to electronically declare their intention to travel and, most recently, pay $14 upon entry into the united states. i don't see where the common values are. i think it is necessary that at the next summit in november the european union should call for the abolition of visas for all european citizens and for identical treatment on both sides of the atlantic.

in writing. – as we mark the world day and the european day against the death penalty, i recall that this parliament stands united in its opposition to the death penalty. this is because capital punishment erodes basic human dignity and contradicts international human rights law. studies show that there is no evidence that the death penalty has a significant deterrent effect on crime, while it does disproportionately affect underprivileged citizens. despite these facts, there are over 20 000 people around the globe on death row; dozens of them are european nationals. from this parliament, we must continue to oppose executions in all circumstances and support an unconditional international moratorium on capital punishment. we also need to encourage states to provide accurate and official statistics on their use of the death penalty. under our treaties, parliament must give its consent to international agreements with third countries. we should keep in mind the stance of these countries on capital punishment when we do so.
