i would like to begin by stressing the urgent need for the european union to adopt a clear and united position on biodiversity at cop10 in nagoya. the lack of such a firm and coherent position would lead to another shameful outcome, like the one at cites in march 2010. i would therefore like the envi recommendations to be accepted without reservation, as they are perhaps the best guide to formulating an official european union position which our representatives can support without hesitation in nagoya this month. beyond these considerations, we must not forget that what is at stake is not only the credibility of the european union as a lucid and responsible partner in international decision-making, but above all the fate of the planet.
ensuring environmental sustainability is one of the millennium development goals, with direct and dramatic implications for people's lives. pollution and the unreasonable exploitation of agricultural land, forests, and water resources are causing climate change that is threatening the earth's natural resources. i would like to talk about one of the most dramatic threats, which is the increasingly difficult access to water resources, with humanity facing the grim prospect that by 2050, about 45 percent of the world's population will be threatened by water scarcity. unfortunately, it was only this year that the un general assembly declared both the right to safe drinking water and the right to sanitation as basic human rights indispensable to the enjoyment of life; but this comes amidst the fact that already more than a quarter of the world's population lacks access to safe drinking water and proper sanitation. the rate of disease and death from improper drinking water remains alarmingly high, especially among children. i therefore believe that the european union must bring about a much more rapid and precise response at the nagoya conference to these problems of the third world, which exacerbate poverty and lack of prospects. i believe that the historical responsibility of developed countries for the material and ecological state of the planet should be an additional argument for policies that counter the current trend of encouraging the unsustainable exploitation of natural resources in developing countries, dependent on the export of raw materials.
if we think about the environmental, social and financial consequences of the destruction of biodiversity, we cannot underestimate the importance of the forthcoming nagoya conference. the ecological disaster in hungary, which killed four people, hit seven towns and affected the ecosystems of several rivers, threatening to affect the danube and danube delta in romania, provides a sad backdrop for today's discussion, but also a serious call for stronger action to protect the environment and biodiversity. it is time to reconsider the ban on the use of hazardous substances in mining, to put an end to these tragedies. the environment committee's resolution on biodiversity contains many important elements, but i would like to highlight a few that i consider essential. first, the main objective of the negotiations should be to adopt ambitious and concrete targets, relevant to a wide range of areas and sectors of activity, from construction and transport to forestry and agriculture.
europe can be divided into nine distinct biogeographical regions based on similarities in climate, topography, geology and vegetation. the danube region is one of the top 20 ecoregions in the world. the biodiversity in this region is extremely rich. it is home to 2,000 plant species and 5,000 animal species. since 1991, the danube delta has been a unesco world heritage site, and the danube area comprises several special protection areas and special conservation areas under natura 2000. as the danube and danube delta constitute a unique and fragile ecosystem, which harbours rare plant species threatened by pollution, we believe it is important that the european commission sometimes improves its capacity to predict and respond to floods, severe drought and accidental pollution. the european union has taken several measures to protect diversity, biodiversity. nature is not only an important part of europe's heritage, not only bringing economic benefits, but also providing many valuable services such as water purification, flood control, soil erosion prevention, crop pollination and recreational activities. land exploitation, accelerated urbanisation and transport infrastructure development have seriously damaged natural habitats and, for example, large-scale drainage schemes have reduced a significant proportion of naturally flooded areas.
in writing. in the context of this debate, i would like to highlight the important role of the teeb project, funded by several european countries, which calculates the financial value of nature and the costs of biodiversity loss. teeb allows us to recognise the scale of the challenges and prepare for future decisions in this area. i would like to mention just a few figures recently presented by teeb: the cost of deforestation is about $4.5 trillion a year; according to other, equally recent estimates, over a quarter of the world's original biodiversity has disappeared by the year 2000, and by 2050 a further loss of over 10% is expected. the examples go on and on. under these circumstances, the nagoya summit is more than timely. i also believe that this parliamentary debate is particularly appropriate to enable us at european level to coordinate our position at the forthcoming summit.
in writing. this year is a crucial moment to strengthen international efforts and commitments to halt biodiversity loss. we must seize this moment to set clear vision and targets for biodiversity and its sustainable conservation beyond 2010. we need to define a strong common position and have the european union actively involved in the future international negotiations. a long-term global vision must take into account the links between biodiversity, ecosystem services, climate change, desertification, economic prosperity, and the health and well-being of citizens. the achievement of the proposed biodiversity objectives and targets is conditional on the mobilisation of the resources necessary for the proper implementation of measures for the conservation and sustainable use of natural resources. in this respect, romania supports greater involvement of the private and public sectors in finding innovative solutions and mechanisms for biodiversity financing.

in writing. the european commission is increasingly imposing fines on cartels and companies that abuse their market position. the fines imposed by it in 2009 exceeded eur 2 billion. the promptness of the european executive's reaction is welcome. at the same time, we must ask whether the current system of sanctions is sufficiently comprehensive. the commission plays the dual role of prosecutor and judge. in addition, the negative effects of the fines imposed include the loss of jobs of the employees of the companies subject to the fines. thus, people who have not broken the law become collateral victims. i therefore believe that it is necessary to develop a more refined set of measures in the area of antitrust infringements aimed both at greater transparency of proceedings through the appointment of an independent judge and at introducing the possibility of individual punishment of directors responsible for the unlawful conduct of companies.

in writing. health in sub-saharan africa is one of the most difficult challenges for eu humanitarian and development policy. i think the drama of the situation is best summed up by the fact that the people in this region have a life expectancy that is about half that of a european citizen. the report gives a good overview of the causes and highlights the remedies needed, including our share of responsibility. international funds for health care are set at half of those for education. without in any way underestimating education, i believe that this disproportion reflects a neglect that needs to be corrected in the future. also, the encouragement by developed countries of the exodus of doctors and nurses from african countries perpetuates the current disaster. i believe that more discernment, especially by eu countries, in recruiting specialists in such key areas would foster substantial progress in improving africa's health system.
social inclusion is a particularly important and well-integrated theme in regional policy and, as we all know, involves much more than just job creation. the resolution on the european social fund underlines its role in achieving the objectives of the union 2020 strategy, which without the instruments of regional policy has no chance of being successfully implemented at national, regional or local level. so as long as regional and social policy are interlinked policies that work together successfully, i do not think we should accept the separation of the european social fund from the structural funds in any way. such a decision would open the door to the sectoralisation of funds, thus setting an undesirable precedent in this respect. the european social fund must remain within the framework of the structural funds, all the more so since it has proved its effectiveness in all european regions, and is a key element in the fight against the economic crisis alongside the european regional development fund. to achieve social, economic and territorial cohesion, we need a strong and well-funded community regional policy. i therefore believe that the regional dimension must continue to have its rightful place both in the revised union budget and in the future budget. we must reject any attempt at renationalization. regional policy is not a charity policy, but a community policy for all regions, which brings economic growth, innovation and competitiveness, an instrument that is within the reach of all member states. if we want solutions to meet the needs and realities we will face in the future, we must maintain the same framework - and i am referring to both the basic principles and the amounts allocated.
cohesion policy has so far been a successful tool for reducing disparities between member states and for demonstrating solidarity - yes, solidarity, a fundamental value of our union. but reducing imbalances is essential not only for the european union, but for each citizen and for each region, and it requires human resources as well as adequate financial resources. the current cohesion policy requires improvements, but not dramatic changes, and above all we must reject, refuse to renationalize and under-finance it. at a time when rich and less rich member states are suffering from the effects of the economic crisis, cutting the budget allocated to cohesion policy would jeopardise all the gains made in recent years and reduce the disparities we have tried to combat so far. that is why i agree with president josé manuel durão barroso's position that the budget allocated to cohesion policy in the future must be at least equal to the current one. otherwise, we will be left with nothing but talk and we will undermine the european project itself.
the achievements of the european union's cohesion policy and the added value it can bring to the eu 2020 strategy are undeniable. the role of this policy in ensuring the competitiveness of regions and facilitating their adaptability should also be emphasised. i believe that while cohesion policy priorities should be aligned with the eu 2020 objectives, there should be enough flexibility to take account of regional specificities and to support weaker regions with greater needs so that they overcome socio-economic difficulties, natural handicaps and reduce disparities. a strong and well-funded european union regional policy, benefiting all eu regions, is a necessary condition for achieving our future objectives.
in my view, the european commission should explain in detail and clearly how the synergy between the cohesion funds and the funds for the common agricultural policy will be achieved, since their concerted operation would add value to community action and would also lead to greater efficiency in achieving our objectives. last but not least, i join those who today called for the simplification of the rules for all types of funds, both at european and member state level, and those who said that gross domestic product must remain the main criterion for determining eligibility for assistance.
i ask the european commission that the future economic, social and territorial cohesion policy of the european union allocate significant amounts to the transport sector, in particular to intermodality and also to the energy efficiency of housing. i believe that these investments will ensure, on the one hand, job creation at local and regional level and also create economic welfare and the development of small and medium-sized enterprises in these sectors. last but not least, commissioner hahn, i hope that after 2013 we will have a separate funding line for the european union strategy for the danube region. i would mention that the european union strategy for the baltic region has, for 2011 alone, 20 million euros. the european union strategy for the danube region can become one of the most successful projects of the european union.
today's debate on cohesion policy beyond 2013 is timely, also taking into account the 'open days' in brussels. the fact that many participants from most european regions have come here to present their initiatives, efforts, results and dissatisfaction in various areas of regional development, strengthens my conviction that the union's cohesion policy is delivering concrete results. a particular aspect of the current programming period is the efficient use of existing funds. we will have to concentrate on measures to increase the absorption of the funds allocated, especially in those regions which are experiencing difficulties in this respect. therefore, the simplification of the implementation of cohesion policy must continue at european, national and regional level. of course, the right balance must be struck between simplification of procedures, efficiency and sound financial management in order to have an easy-to-implement policy with increased visibility.
the european union's cohesion and regional policy is of paramount importance not only for the sake of increasing economic competitiveness but also for the sake of the ideal of european unity. i think we can all agree that a truly united europe can only be built in the medium and long term if it is based on a balanced level of economic development. the eu 2020 strategy is therefore essential for its effective implementation and achievement of its objectives, so that the different regions at different levels of development are both beneficiaries of the process. it is therefore crucial for the less economically developed regions to maintain the current level of funding for cohesion policy. we must avoid europe being divided into two by the slowdown in the catch-up of the member states that joined after 2004.

in writing. − in recent years, there has been encouraging progress towards the abolition of the death penalty. the number of countries that have permanently abandoned the death penalty has increased to 95 and its regular application has been restricted to two regions of the world, asia and north africa. un resolutions on the implementation of a global moratorium have contributed significantly to these results. the eu also continues to be the most important source of funding for organisations campaigning against the death penalty. however, i believe that the concrete initiatives of these organisations must find the necessary political support. as the european parliament's motion for a resolution is an important support in this respect, my vote was in favour. however, despite the positive developments, 58 countries retain the death penalty and the statistics on the number of convicts are worrying. last year, more than 700 people were executed, in addition to the thousands of allegedly condemned in china. i would therefore like to draw attention to the need to step up efforts to influence international public opinion. even in some eu member states, a significant proportion of citizens would support the introduction of the death penalty.
in writing. − the european union is committed to its priority human rights objective the complete abolition of the death penalty worldwide and the declaration adopted by the european parliament's plenary on the world day against the death penalty confirms this. the fact that many states still apply the death penalty, the most cruel, inhuman and degrading of all, and even more so to women and even minors, is beyond comprehension. and it becomes all the more incomprehensible since there is no evidence whatsoever that the death penalty discourages crime any more than other punishments do. it is important that the european union continues its efforts to cooperate between states because only in this way, through collaboration, education, awareness-raising, will it be able to fulfil your desire to abolish the death penalty worldwide. key to achieving the number one human rights goal for the european union is also the work of the non-governmental sector, which has reported cases of unfair trials that have resulted in brutal sentences such as the one handed down in iran against a boy who was only 16 years old at the time of the alleged crime.
in writing. − one of the first measures taken by the provisional government in bucharest, after the collapse of the ceausescu regime, following the popular uprisings in timisoara and bucharest, was the abolition of the death penalty. it was a reparative gesture, first of all towards the political victims of the totalitarianisms that dominated romania since the 1930s. i recall this episode in recent european history because the european parliament's resolution on the world day against the death penalty responds to an anachronistic reality for the 21st century: the death penalty is still present in the legislation of many countries, including some that are active promoters of civil rights and freedoms globally. not only does the death penalty not deter crime, it does not reduce crime, but it also raises the very real problem of possible miscarriages of justice, which would send innocent people to their deaths. the invitation by the member states of the european union to the countries still applying this penalty to adopt a moratorium on the execution of sentences seems to me to be one of the main advantages of this resolution, and this is what led me to vote in favour of it.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the eu strategic objectives for the 10th conference of the parties to the nagoya convention on biological diversity, primarily because i am convinced that the preservation of biological diversity is a factor in sustainable development for developing countries. and the fact that neither the global biodiversity target for 2010 to significantly reduce the rate of biodiversity loss, nor the eu target to halt biodiversity loss, has been met, makes further action to achieve them all the more urgent. another worrying phenomenon is the illegal use of genetic resources, which often leads to negative effects on the target countries of such practices. i agree that biodiversity conservation issues are only sporadically present in public debate, and therefore support the motion in the body of the resolution for a more sustained and applied effort to promote biodiversity conservation measures among citizens. we need their understanding and support. just as important, i think, is the effort to make biodiversity conservation part of civic education in our countries.
in writing. − given that halting biodiversity loss is not an urgent priority on the european and international political calendar, i welcome the implementation and adoption of a set of concrete, science-based indicators to measure progress on biodiversity towards the european union's strategic objectives and targets.
in writing. − the international community has not remained indifferent and has undertaken numerous solidarity actions to support the people of the african continent. however, the level of development of this sector is still far below that of the west. if we consider that the life expectancy of an african may be as much as thirty or forty years shorter than that of a european, we can say that the problem remains, even at this hour, a major one. ladies and gentlemen, i support the solutions proposed in mrs de keyser's report and draw attention to the fact that the real solution to the problem on the african continent depends as much on building the foundations of the health system as on providing aid on time. to paraphrase a famous saying, i believe that if you give a patient a medicine, you have helped him for a day. if you give him the basics of a health system, you're helping him for his whole life; him and his children. that's why i'm advocating a balanced funding policy!
in writing. − in my view, the main merit of the resolution on health systems in sub-saharan africa and global health is that it addresses the issue from the specificities of the area under discussion. it is about the objective difficulty of grafting a model of the organization of social protection systems, specific to western civilization, into a completely different context. the failure of many projects for developing countries in the developing world has its origin in the absolutization of the western-centric approach, whether it was europe or the united states. this has led to a waste of resources and created additional problems for the countries concerned. the specific situation of the area makes it even more apparent that we cannot treat health as a commodity, so we need to identify non-profit health insurance based on the values of solidarity and democracy. progress made over time, including through contributions from eu member states, can be undone by a hasty approach from a mercantilist perspective. it seems to me that the resolution addresses the problem correctly and coherently, which is why i voted in favour of it.
in writing. − cohesion policy is the most effective instrument for implementing european policies at regional level. the resolution adopted today contains important elements for achieving a close link with the objectives of strategy 2020. the 2014-2021 budgetary framework should support an ambitious cohesion policy in terms of resources allocated. also, given the impact of the economic crisis on the less developed regions, the convergence objective must continue to dominate. for romania, the implementation of this policy allows for real convergence with the other states of the union, especially since all 8 development regions of my country can benefit from structural funds. the attraction and optimal use of these would have resulted in a 15% increase in gdp over the next 5 years. the limited administrative capacity of the management units within ministries, however, meant that the absorption rate remained one of the lowest in europe. for this reason, i believe that it would be useful to reorganise these existing management structures at the level of ministries and apply strict criteria of competence in the selection of staff. in addition, i believe that macro-regional strategies such as the danube strategy should be maintained as a priority axis of this policy.
in writing. − i believe that the european social fund should remain within the framework of the regulation on general provisions relating to cohesion policy funds, but i believe that it needs to operate on the basis of its own rules.
in writing. − the european social fund is a key instrument that contributes to strengthening economic and social cohesion in the eu countries. optimal financial support for the fund would strengthen the sense of solidarity among european citizens, especially in the new member states. for the period 2007-2013, the european union has allocated approximately €3.5 million to romania for the european social fund. operational programmes focus on two areas. the first is aimed at developing human capital and the second aims at improving the service and public policy infrastructure through the 'administrative capacity building' programme. in this context, the potential of the structural funds needs to be strengthened by simplifying and improving procedures. the main objective is to help member states optimise employment and the active participation of citizens in society. in the future, the european social fund will have to play an important role in supporting the europe 2020 strategy. this will certainly require action at both european and national level.
in writing. − as the structural funds remain to a large extent the main funding instrument for social objectives, i believe that economic, social and territorial cohesion must be strengthened by improving employability and employment opportunities, encouraging a high level of employment and ensuring more and better quality jobs.
mr president, there will be no successfully united europe without a far-sighted vision of how our common interests must be promoted outside the borders of the union at global level. such a vision will not last without an ambitious, accountable, efficient and ‘communautarian’ external action service. such a service will not function effectively without staff recruited on the basis of merit. i believe most of us can agree on these principles. the devil is, however, in the detail. and it is precisely these details, which have transformed a report that was meant to be technical into a source of passionate political debate which risks dividing us deeply. there is no dilemma between ‘communautarianism’ and intergovernmentalism, between merits or quotas, between old and new member states. nevertheless the triumph of ‘communautarianism’ requires that each and every national of each and every member state feels fairly treated on the basis of their merits. the triumph of the merit criterion must be tested by the equilibrium of the results of the selection, since god, i believe, distributed merits and sins in a balanced way to men and women, old and young, small and big, weak and powerful, westerners and easterners etc. the fact of the matter is that some in our union – mainly but not only among the new members – feel they are discriminated against. even if this perception were wrong, we should still treat it with respect and care since our unity is of the utmost importance. it is not the criteria which are being questioned, but the insufficiency of guarantees that they will be properly enhanced, and of corrective measures to be applied when imbalances are obvious. i can only hope that the high representative will correct the imbalances in the process which apparently fuelled these perceptions, and i also hope that a future european diplomatic academy, or something similar, will help us to create a corps of european diplomats who are competent and loyal to our common interest and to the european institutions.
in writing. the vote shows that there is neither equality between member states nor solidarity within a political group. the adoption of the socialist amendment introducing the 'merit' criterion in the selection of eu heads of delegation (diplomats who will represent the union in third countries) will demonstrate to us, once it is applied by the external action service of the socialist catherine ashton, that romania and other new member states will be left with dust on the drum. i regret that, once again, we were unable to adopt a united position in favour of romania's interests at the level of romanian representatives in the european parliament. i would have expected adrian severin, as a former foreign minister (even for a few months), to support introducing clear criteria in the allocation of the posts of heads of delegation (number of inhabitants, number of seats in the european parliament and share of votes in the council) instead of a very subjective and ambiguous criterion of 'merit'. especially since, as far as i know, intelligence is evenly distributed across the eu and not all the smart ones have been clustered in the west and only the stupid ones have been left in the east. but in diplomacy, romania has representatives who deserve to be heads of delegation.
in writing. the european external action service should contribute to the achievement of the objective of the treaty of lisbon, namely the achievement of effective and coherent external action by the union. the current staff selection procedure is a long and complex process and the filling of posts is gradual until the numbers corresponding to the full operationalisation of the service are reached. a number of new eu countries, particularly the last two of the last wave of enlargement, are underrepresented in the external relations department of dg relex. mrs catherine ashton has already expressed her wish that the eeas should be composed of the best officials selected on professional grounds, rather than on the basis of their countries of origin. we remind mrs ashton that eu states have all the same rights and as such there is a need for adequate representation in the structures of the new european diplomatic service, both at the brussels headquarters and in the eu delegations. we therefore call on mrs ashton to take account of the fact that the european union has 27 member states. they must be able to contribute, through their representatives in the eeas, to the achievement of the union's foreign policy objectives and to the credibility of that institution before all european citizens.
in writing. we are in the final stages of the decisions that will enable the launch of the european external action service. i support a compromise on the staff regulations and the financial regulation which would allow the high representative to have a functioning service by december this year. however, this support is not a blank check. the high representative must fulfil his commitment already undertaken on several occasions to ensure fair representation in the european external action service of member states, such as romania, which are under-represented in the external relations structures of the commission and the council to be transferred to the eeas. it is not a question of national control of the eeas, but of the interest in having staff recruited also on the basis of the criterion of geographical balance. this criterion is not incompatible with the criterion of competence.
in writing. – the final steps in creating the eeas have been discussed today and will be voted tomorrow. there were tough negotiations between the three pillars of the union: the council, the commission and the parliament, so each, even if not completely satisfied, saw its main interests safeguarded. during the entire process, emphasis was placed inevitably on the national representation of the member states in the staffing process. things were not helped when, in spite of the ongoing negotiations to set its rules, the process continued unabated and, as a consequence, only some countries have seen their representatives getting the positions they were seeking. however, i think that the main challenge to the new service lies less in composition than in substance: if we want the members of the eeas to be truly european, then we will have to provide them with a truly european foreign policy to implement. in that respect, both the multi-polar structure of the international system and the current crisis are important obstacles to be dealt with vigorously. otherwise, the eeas will only pursue the national objectives of the individual members.
in 1992, the united nations declared october 17 to be the world day against poverty. in 2000, the world body committed itself to halving the proportion of people living in extreme poverty within 15 years. we're two-thirds of the way through the deadline. the numbers are alarming, we're falling behind the markers. but the demand is high, the expectations are high. in the eu, 73% of the population consider the increasing poverty in their country to be the main problem. 89% of citizens want immediate action to tackle poverty and 74% expect the eu to play an important role in eradicating poverty. in contrast, 6 million eu citizens have lost their jobs in the last two years and child poverty has increased. although we recognise and refer to employment as the most effective tool in the fight against poverty, the social europe model proposed by jean monnet has been overshadowed by economic interests. the aim of economic development is to ensure the well-being of citizens, but without effective social measures, without drastically reducing the current level of poverty, this is of no use. social policy is, of course, primarily the task and responsibility of the member states, but i believe that we must find answers to the most pressing questions together by making greater use of the open method of coordination and by promoting the exchange of good practice.
the lisbon targets of creating more jobs and eradicating poverty by 2010 have not been met, and europe must continue to work towards them. i believe that the union and the member states must pay particular attention to lifelong learning programmes. they are a way of combating poverty and social exclusion and help to strengthen the capacity for integration into the labour market and the workplace. on the other hand, i believe that the european executive should analyse the areas where the shortage of qualified staff is increasing, in order to be able to subsequently promote measures to cover this shortage. one possible measure would be to extend the erasmus programme, currently aimed at students, to other socio-professional categories, for example young people without university studies or unemployed people in vocational retraining programmes.
member of the commission. − madam president, poverty is a tragedy for individuals as well as for society. poverty leads to violence, crime and conflict. i would like to thank the european parliament for putting the fight against poverty so high on the agenda and today’s debate demonstrates european determination to address this challenge. the europe 2020 strategy, ms figueiredo’s report, activities in the member states – these are all steps in the right direction. i would like to emphasise that as long as global poverty exists – with 1.4 billion people living on less than one dollar a day – we cannot expect to also solve this issue inside the european union. that means the millennium development goals policy is a policy that also matters to us. i believe that we are trying to find the right solution and it is inclusive economic growth -of our partner countries and also in the european union. i know inclusive economic growth sounds rather simple, but that is exactly what we are trying to address in changing our development policies. the eu 2020 strategy also goes in this direction.
president of the council. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, in my first speech i had deliberately confined myself to the development aspect of the fight against poverty. a few words, of course, on the union. the belgian presidency has focused on developing instruments in the field of combating poverty and social exclusion, in particular through the implementation of the flagship initiatives of the europe 2020 strategy. the objectives of the strategy approved by the council on 7 june 2010 include the promotion of social inclusion, with a particular focus on poverty reduction. this objective is to remove at least 20 million people from the risk of poverty or exclusion by 2020 on the basis of three indicators proposed by the social protection committee, namely the risk of poverty, material deprivation and living in households without a job. the european year for combating poverty and social exclusion also aims to raise public awareness of the problem and to convey the message that poverty and exclusion undermine social and economic developments. it also aims to challenge the view that poverty reduction is a cost to society and to reaffirm the importance of collective responsibility involving not only policy makers but also public and private sector actors. the belgian presidency has been keen to take part in this year of the fight against poverty and social exclusion. let me mention some of the initiatives and events organised on this occasion. a conference on child poverty was held in september. the aim of this conference was to give momentum to the european debate on the adoption of a recommendation on child poverty to break the vicious cycle of the reproduction of poverty from generation to generation. in response specifically to our colleague mr daerden, a round table is being held today in brussels. it focuses on the implementation of the recommendation on active inclusion with its three pillars: minimum income, inclusive labour market and access to quality services. another conference on the social economy will be held on 27 and 28 october and the conference on homelessness will be held on 9 and 10 december. finally, on 17 december, on the sidelines of the european council, the official closing session of the year of combating poverty will take place, with the presentation of best practices and highlights of the year. this, madam president, ladies and gentlemen, is the concrete expression of the belgian presidency's ambition to place social issues at the top of the european agenda.
in writing. in 2009, europe felt the full impact of the global economic crisis, and the effects of this period on the level of poverty at community level were devastating, especially for the 17% of europeans living below the poverty line in 2008. unfortunately, that share has most likely increased. only now, in 2010, are we beginning to see hope that the overall economic situation may improve. our strongest efforts must be directed towards the europeans most affected by the crisis, especially as 2010 is the european year for combating poverty and social exclusion. in view of the objective of eradicating absolute and child poverty by 2015 and the objective of substantially reducing relative poverty, i too draw attention to the need for the european union to urgently introduce national minimum income thresholds that offer protection from the risk of poverty and ensure social inclusion for all european citizens.
in writing. the eu 2020 target of reducing the number of europeans living below the poverty line by 25%, representing more than 20 million people, should contribute to the development of national policies to protect citizens against the risk of poverty. women represent a significant segment of the population threatened with poverty due to unemployment (the unemployment rate rising from 7.4% in 2008 to 9% in 2009), unshared caring responsibilities, precarious and low-paid jobs, wage discrimination and lower pensions. in romania, 25% of women (the european average is 17%) and 33% of children live in poverty. romania is the second poorest country in the european union, with 23% of the population. the minimum wage barely reaches 140 euros, and the average gross wage does not rise above 460 euros. calls on the member states to take concrete measures to create decent and sustainable jobs, to promote adequate income and social protection systems to prevent and reduce poverty, in particular extreme poverty, and to develop long- and medium-term strategies that include a gender perspective and are mainstreamed in all relevant policy areas.
in writing. − the member states of the union should contribute to the establishment of a european database on the monthly sea transport of goods or passengers and the vessels carrying them. the eu's specialised service, eurostat, will thus be able to produce european statistics on all modes of transport in accordance with eu standards. the exploitation of these data will then contribute to the establishment of the european integrated system of statistical data in this field with a view to achieving a maximum level of comparability between modes of transport in european countries.
in writing. − the community of european shipbuilding associations (cesa) estimates that global shipbuilding requirements will decline by 2014 as a result of the global financial crisis, and that the shipbuilding industry will move to low-cost areas, particularly in asia, in the future. in the absence of a european policy to support the shipping sector, it is unlikely that it will return to the production level before the current crisis. in my home town of galati, the damen shipyard is also suffering from the effects of the economic and financial crisis, laying off some 600 workers in 2009 alone, and another 500 are expected to be laid off in 2010. i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) requested by denmark for the co-financing of the support programme for 951 workers made redundant in the region of north jutland between 15 february 2009 and 14 november 2009 with eur 7 521 359. the redundancies occurred in 45 enterprises producing machinery and equipment for the naval sector.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) in respect of the request from nl/nxp semiconductors in the netherlands. on 26 march 2010, the netherlands requested financial assistance from the egf in respect of 512 redundancies out of 590 in nxl semiconductors, which operates in the electronics sector in the nuts ii regions of gelderland and eindhoven. of the total number of persons made redundant, 425 are men, 87 are women, and 7 of the workers (1.3%) have serious health problems or a disability. the netherlands underlines the significant impact of these redundancies, as nxp semiconductors is the largest industrial employer in the area, providing jobs to a significant number of low-skilled workers who have worked for several decades in the company. the lack of job opportunities in similar enterprises in the region will be particularly problematic for workers with specialised experience in semiconductor manufacturing. the mobilisation of the egf is particularly important for the reintegration of workers made redundant into the labour market. however, i would draw the attention of the commission and the member states to the need to develop an eu industrial policy that is sustainable and creates new jobs.
in writing. − in january 2010, spain submitted an application to mobilise the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) in view of the redundancies in 23 companies in the catalan region in the production of road transport vehicles, trailers and semi-trailers. i voted in favour of the european parliament's resolution on the mobilisation of the egf to provide aid for people made redundant. the redundancies occurred in the context of the financial and economic crisis, which caused a sharp decline in demand for vehicles in spain and worldwide, at an unprecedented rate. in the period february-november 2009, in the region of catalonia alone, there were 2 330 redundancies in the automotive sector, 75% of the workers being men and almost 25% of them over 55 years old. i advocate that the people who are laid off receive financial support and training so that they can get a new job for as long as possible.
in writing. - i voted to combat precarious work, one of the phenomena that is proliferating amid the economic crisis. this will help to eradicate job insecurity, low wages, often undeclared, the lack of social protection for casual workers and a work environment lacking minimum standards of health and safety and protection of workers against accidents. at the same time, these measures will more effectively combat gender discrimination, which dominates the precarious workplace, with women being particularly victims of these inhumane working conditions. the abusive treatment of domestic workers, who are mainly women, wage discrimination against women and the exploitation of migrant women who do not know or cannot defend their rights are all reasons to vote in favour of these actions to counter a revolting socio-economic reality.
in writing. − i believe that member states must fight to be able to offer women jobs, the possibility of trade union protection of rights, as well as decent pay, maternity leave, fair and regular work schedules and a non-discriminatory working environment. i believe that member states must sanction the creation of barriers to trade union membership and also provide easily accessible counselling services for women who cannot benefit from the support of a works council, for example women employed in private households and in agriculture.
in writing. − during the economic and financial crisis, precarious work among citizens, especially women, has become even more pronounced. the permanent jobs that were lost during the economic crisis will certainly not be restored, but will be replaced by atypical and very atypical employment contracts, which will lead to a sharp decline in the level of working conditions. at european level, 31.5% of women work part-time (30 hours a week or less), compared with only 8.3% of men. i believe that the sustainability of the pension system, credit facilities for self-help projects and programmes to create jobs and alternative incomes can improve conditions for women in precarious employment. i call on the european commission and the member states to develop viable strategies on precarious work, with a focus on decent and green jobs and gender mainstreaming. calls on each member state to introduce clear measures to reduce the gender pay gap by 10% by 2020, including pension gaps, in order to improve living standards, combat poverty and stimulate economic growth.

in a volatile economy, late payments have negative effects on smes. improving the system in this respect is an ambitious goal and also necessary for the timely payment of employees and suppliers. the new rules on late payment in commercial transactions should facilitate and accelerate the recovery of money owed by companies. i think it's essential that all parties are on an equal footing and that the rules apply to everyone. in the last three years in romania over 30 thousand smes have disappeared as a result of the financial blockade. one cause is the delay in payment by the state for goods and services. finally, i would like to express my support for this proposal for a directive which encourages better monitoring and evaluation of the trading system.
in writing. the late payments directive provides a vital tool for building a fair and equitable relationship between authorities and small and medium-sized enterprises. once in force, this directive will punish insolvent authorities and give businessmen significant leverage to recover their debts. such legislation was needed to balance the market and provide the private sector with guarantees that the authority is an equal player, who can be held accountable when it does not respect the rules of the game. the directive provides for a reasonable period of 30 days for payments and for derogations of up to 60 days only in special cases such as hospitals and for compensation and interest for late payment. although the form adopted is more lenient with the insolvency authorities than the european commission's original proposal, the directive provides sufficient support to both small and medium-sized enterprises and large companies which, in many eu member states, face difficulties in recovering money for services rendered. i am disappointed that the 5% penalty has been removed, but i see this backsliding as a strategic way of winning the support of as many union countries as possible in the council debates.

madam president, this drama reminds us of our responsibility as politicians. it is not an urgent matter to come up with another new law, another legislative package. we already have a full environmental acquis in the european mining waste directive. the problem in europe is not about having a proper legislative framework, but about the proper implementation of these laws by the member states. obviously, companies have had way too much leverage in negotiating with national authorities over what constitutes hazardous waste that should fall under the strictest safety standards. furthermore, i am honestly worried when i hear of the large number of toxic deposits all across the danube region and of over 1 000 contaminated sites in romania alone. i think the first priority in terms of prevention should be to list these sites in europe. we cannot afford to wait until 2012 for this to come into force. member states should voluntarily share this information with the commission as quickly as possible. this case also demonstrates that the commission should be given more means to ensure correct implementation of environmental law, especially in central and eastern europe. it also shows that the commission should also be given more resources to investigate quality control and inspection of these dangerous sites. last but not least, i should like to emphasise that the basic principle should be that polluters pay for the environmental damage they cause. this is why i am unsure that the use of the eu solidarity fund for natural disasters would be appropriate, as it may undermine this principle at the core of the environmental liability directive.

it seems that the effects of the crisis are far from being removed at the moment, and i would therefore like to recall in this context the important role played by economic and social cohesion policy and, not least, the sine qua non condition it represents. this policy has become an essential element of the economic recovery package, generating added value and supporting efforts to modernise and sustain economic growth, while demonstrating european solidarity. i think that we need, first of all, major investment in infrastructure of all kinds, whether it be transport, energy or telecommunications. we need substantial capital investment from multiple sources of both public and private funding, including through public-private partnerships, which in my view are still not being used to their full potential.
in writing. the current economic crisis demonstrates that the existing economic governance model in the eu has not worked well enough, failing to achieve full convergence between member states. in this context, an improved economic framework and the establishment of ambitious monitoring instruments that are clearer and better focused are needed. it is essential that member states comply with the rules and decisions laid down at european level, in particular those of the stability and growth pact. in this connection, i would like to welcome mr feio's initiative, which encourages, among other things, the development of more controls and a closer monitoring of the evolution of public debt and revenue. finally, i would like to add that the romanian government recently adopted the fiscal strategy for 2011-2013 which includes the necessary measures to return to a budget deficit below 3% and to keep the debt below the 60% threshold. this reform process will ensure that the necessary conditions for economic recovery are created.
in writing. the regulatory structures that existed before the economic and monetary crisis in the european union and the united states were inconsistent and relied heavily on dispersed macroeconomic analysis. in the absence of global consistency of these regulatory structures, states have reacted on their own. they have not taken into account that, in a globalised world, monetary policies adopted at national level have a considerable effect on other economies. the creation of the european systemic risk board and the european system of financial supervisors strengthens financial supervision within the eu. however, there is still insufficient regulation at international level on crisis management in the financial sector. at the g20 meeting in november 2010, the union should underline the importance of a supervisory and regulatory system that imposes, inter alia, the obligation to register financial transactions and instruments. we have an economic responsibility and we must first be strong at the level of the european union in order to be able to be leaders at the global level.
in writing. europe has started to recover economically, but the context remains uncertain. the global economic recovery remains fragile, and the pace of the process varies from country to country. the first priority remains the creation of a stable base that regularly generates sustained and balanced economic growth. to this end, we need to create a system that allows for simultaneous crisis response, prevention and cooperation in the medium and long term. the european union must be a strong partner, able to impose its experience in economic and political integration, but also to make a substantial contribution to global economic governance. we need to create credible and viable economic policies in the medium term and coordinate macroeconomic policy based on a framework for sustained and balanced growth developed by the g20. a strategy for the union's economic policies should include: an action plan on the use of structural reforms to strengthen growth and employment; strengthened fiscal reform; and strengthening economic governance of the eu and the euro area. it is necessary to adopt a g20 development agenda with a multiannual action plan to promote growth and flexibility for developing countries.
in writing. the eu, with its 500 million citizens, representing 7% of the world's population, accounts for 30% of global gdp. according to the latest statistics, the eu recorded a trade deficit of eur 17.3 billion in august 2010. in the first half of this year, the eu recorded the largest increases in exports to brazil (+57%), china (+41%) and turkey (+38%), and for imports the largest increases were recorded in relation to russia (+43%), china and india (both +25%). to achieve the objectives of the 'eu 2020 strategy', the eu should reduce its energy dependence on its traditional suppliers. in the first half of this year, the eu27's energy trade deficit increased by eur 34.3 billion compared with the same period last year. the union also needs an eco-efficient industrial policy that links the eu's innovation capacity to its production facilities, thereby creating jobs within the union and maintaining the eu's global competitiveness. the european council should therefore include on its agenda for 28-29 october the future industrial policy and energy security of the eu, as well as proposals on mitigating the effects of climate change and demography.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the regulation. it contains technical, financial and administrative details and clarifies the interinstitutional relations that this european service and its structures must have. we all wanted and we all want the eu to be a strong and recognised actor in foreign policy. for this we also need rules, european regulations adapted to the mission.
in writing. - i believe, as do other colleagues, that the eeas needs autonomy within the european staff regulations. i support the provision that union officials and temporary staff from member states and diplomatic services respectively must have the same rights and be eligible for the new posts. i hope that the widest possible geographical recruitment, and i am talking about the new member states, will become a reality.
in writing. − the results of the vote on the rapkay report show that a considerable number of meps from new member states either abstained or voted against it. i was one of the meps who abstained. my main concern was the lack of ambition of its wording on the principle of geographical balance within the employment policy and staff of the future european external action service (eeas). the report failed to introduce a legally binding commitment to geographical balance in eeas, thus relying only on political promises made by key eu decision- makers on foreign affairs. this is why most new member states do not feel reassured by the proper application of the principle of geographical balance in the future eeas. it is regrettable that the rapporteur chose such a minimalist line, while the reluctance of the council to explicitly accept this binding commitment raises even more concern. i am calling on the council and the commission to examine the voting result on this report closely and deliver on their promises of respecting the geographical balance principle while recruiting the future staff of eeas. it will be one of the meps’ priorities to monitor this process closely in future .
in writing. - i agree with the other members who do not support the budget cuts proposed by the council. the best argument is the situation of the member states which have done so internally. i am referring specifically to romania. the pressure on consumption, the freezing of consumption, did not get us out of the crisis, but it generated unprecedented social pressure. i'm also in favour of increasing the milk fund by 300 million euros. we have had the same attitude of supporting additional financial allocations throughout the european crisis to this product. i strongly support the idea of the european stabilisation mechanism and the need for the two new budget lines to be concrete, covered with figures and not empty as they are now, so that this instrument of european intervention becomes concrete, not just theoretical. i hope that in the conciliation process parliament's view will be respected, that an agreement will be reached with the council and that we will be able to vote in november on the union's 2011 budget.
in writing. − i voted for this report because the european parliament identifies among its most important priorities youth, education and mobility policies. i have in turn argued on several occasions that these are essential and necessary parts of the eu's economic recovery strategy and the europe 2020 strategy. youth, education and mobility require specific cross-sectoral investments in the appropriate policies to foster eu growth and development. i therefore support the need to increase appropriations for all programmes related to these priorities, namely 'lifelong learning', 'people' and 'erasmus mundus'. the commission is also proposing to increase the appropriations for the european employment services network. to this end, i support the launch of the 'your first eures job' preparatory action to help young people enter the labour market or access to specialised jobs in another member state as a first step towards a non-academic youth mobility programme.
in writing. − i agree with extending maternity leave to a minimum of 20 weeks and to be paid 100%, but with some flexibility for countries that already have provisions for this type of leave. women who take maternity leave must receive full pay, 100% of the last month's salary or the average of monthly wages. the amendments adopted will prevent the dismissal of pregnant women from the beginning of their pregnancy until six months after the end of maternity leave. furthermore, women must have the right to return to their position, or to a position with the same remuneration, occupational category and job description as those held before the start of maternity leave.
in writing. − the eu is currently facing demographic difficulties, driven by a falling birth rate and an increasing number of older people. improving work-life balance provisions is one way of responding to this demographic decline. it is clear that gender stereotypes persist in society, representing an obstacle to women's access to jobs, and especially to quality jobs. women are still seen as the main carers of children and other dependants, often facing the need to choose between motherhood and a career. women are often perceived as 'high risk', 'second class' or 'unsuitable' workers, given their high probability of becoming pregnant and their right to maternity leave. it is therefore essential that new forms of leave do not reflect or reinforce existing stereotypes in society. parental involvement in a child's life, from the earliest months of life, is very important for the healthy physical, emotional and psychological development of the child.
in writing. − i voted for an increase in safety and health at work for pregnant workers both on the basis of the principle of gender equality and non-discrimination on the basis of gender and to stimulate a better participation of women in the labour market. one of the effects of this measure is to create a balance between family and professional life for women. women also need this legislative support to protect their health and that of their child. another important aspect, concerning the occupational safety of women, concerns the prohibition of dismissal during the period from the beginning of pregnancy until at least six months after the end of maternity leave. also meeting the need for social security is the establishment of a salary ceiling for maternity leave. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' in the context of the directive.
in writing. − statistics show that the birth rate in the eu is declining. with this low birth rate and with an ageing population, we will face a real problem in the future with pension payments and healthcare payments in europe. families, especially women, should not be penalized if they want to have children. pregnant and breastfeeding workers must not perform work which, following assessments, presents a risk of exposure to certain agents or particularly harmful working conditions, endangering the safety or health of such workers. i therefore support the idea of measures to promote the improvement of the safety and health of workers who have recently given birth or are breastfeeding, measures which must not disadvantage women in the labour market or act to the detriment of the directives on equal treatment between women and men.
in writing. − extending maternity leave to 20 weeks and paying 100% for this period are measures that restore the dignity of mothers. that is why i voted unreservedly in favour of the report, confident that the member states will follow our decision and implement it in their national legislation. in addition to support for mothers, the report recommends that states introduce fully paid parental leave, which recognizes the role of both parents in raising a child. we have sent an important signal through today's vote, which calls for a decent life, transcending national ideological boundaries and social systems.
in writing. − the european parliament today made an investment in the future of the european union by promoting maternity by extending maternity leave to 20 weeks with full pay. progress can be made in terms of both quantity and quality. the simplistic argument of short-term economic benefits did not hold, and the sustainability of european society prevailed, which is impossible to achieve without a healthy demography, and therefore implicitly without greater protection for mothers and children. i drafted the opinion of the empl committee and voted for maternity not to be penalized, to be paid in full, pregnant workers not to be dismissed from the beginning of their pregnancy until six months after the end of maternity leave; to have the right to return to their position or to an equivalent post - a position with the same remuneration, the same occupational category and the same job sheet as those held before the start of maternity leave; taking maternity leave not to affect the pension scheme; workers are not required to work nights and overtime during the 10 weeks before the due date for the remainder of the pregnancy, where this is necessary for the health of the mother or the foetus and throughout the period of breastfeeding.
in writing. − i voted against this resolution because i believe that the remuneration of maternity leave is a matter to be decided at national level, applying the principle of subsidiarity. moreover, i believe that in a time of crisis, the adoption of this measure may have perverse effects, acting as a deterrent for firms wishing to employ women.
in writing. − today i voted to support improved rights and a better work-life balance for working parents. of special importance in this report are the provisions for women who are breastfeeding at work. breaks for breastfeeding allow mothers the time they need to provide the best and most natural form of nutrition for their developing child. nutrition is a key determinant of health throughout life. i am pleased that this report is favourable to those mothers who have gone back to work and still choose to breastfeed their child and provide them with the nutritional benefits.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a directive on the introduction of measures to encourage improvements in the safety and health at work of pregnant workers, workers who have recently given birth or workers who are breastfeeding. i think it is extremely important that women workers on maternity leave are paid their full salary and that the maternity allowance is 100% of their last monthly salary or of their average salary, if the monthly salary is less than that. thus, women will not be penalised for the maternity leave period. in view of demographic developments in the union, it is necessary to stimulate births through specific legislation and measures to contribute to a better reconciliation of work, private and family life. to help workers reconcile their work and family life, it is essential to provide for longer maternity and paternity leave, including for the adoption of children under 12 months of age. the establishment of the legal duration of maternity leave at 20 weeks is in line with the recommendation of the world health organisation of 16 april 2002 on a global strategy for the nutrition of infants and young children.
in writing. − in a volatile economy, late payments can have extremely negative effects on small and medium-sized enterprises, which need money to pay their employees and suppliers. the new rules on late payment in commercial transactions, agreed by parliament and the council on 5 october, should facilitate and speed up the recovery of money owed by companies. small and medium-sized enterprises are what keep the economy running, even in times of crisis. this is happening in all european economies. the european parliament has ensured that all parties are on an equal footing and that the rules apply to all, to the benefit of many european small and medium-sized enterprises. the agreement will also remove the role of smes as banks for public enterprises or large companies. alongside the european parliament's recommendation to collect vat from small and medium-sized enterprises only when invoices are collected, the imposition of a clear deadline for payment of invoices helps those struggling to survive in a time of downturn in the markets.
in writing. − i hope that the entry into force of the directive on combating late payment in commercial transactions will benefit the most small and medium-sized enterprises in the european union, which will thus be better protected and will have liquidity to develop investments and create new jobs. i also hope that the directive will allow the development of debt recovery mechanisms, as late payments by public authorities cause imbalances in the functioning of small and medium-sized enterprises and, consequently, of the market.
in writing. − the international community has repeatedly confirmed its commitment to combating poverty. such a global approach is necessary because poverty is not limited to the underdeveloped countries of sub-saharan africa or asia, but affects 17% of the eu population. i believe that last month's un summit marked an important development, leading to the adoption of a concrete action plan for achieving the millennium development goals. the eu has set itself the goal of reducing the number of people living in poverty by a quarter by 2020 and allocating 0.7% of gross national income to development aid. in addition, by adopting this report, the european parliament is encouraging the active inclusion of disadvantaged groups and ensuring effective economic and social cohesion. i would like to mention romania's important contribution to the un programmes to combat poverty, worth eur 250 million. since development assistance must be reciprocal, my country will continue to honor its commitments. however, i believe that more attention should be paid to groups at high risk of poverty, such as the rural population or the roma minority.
in writing. − almost 300 000 families in romania receive a minimum income guaranteed by the state, through a law that has been in force since 2001, and for which a budgetary effort of almost 300 million euros is made. in the current economic crisis, which is felt particularly by the population of the least economically developed countries, the european parliament's recommendation to introduce a minimum income system in all member states is a natural step. while no one can dispute the necessity of such a guaranteed minimum income system, it is clear that the system can be subject to abuse. good timing and control of the system is necessary because there is a risk that this system will encourage non-work. to prevent this from happening, it is advisable that those who receive this income and are in a position to do so give hours of work to the community. 85 million people across the union were living below the poverty line at the end of 2008. there are figures that confirm that support is needed, especially when we talk about young or old.
in writing. − with around a fifth of the eu population below the poverty line, with increasing rates for children, young people and the elderly, with the growing share of poor workers in parallel with the proliferation of precarious and low-paid jobs, with 10 member states where the rate of material deprivation affects at least a quarter of the inhabitants, exceeding half of the population in the case of romania and bulgaria - the eu is facing a poverty problem aggravated not only by the recession but also by the anti-social policies of right-wing governments. the minimum income can guarantee social protection to large sections of the population who are now living in poverty. the role of this minimum income is extremely important in avoiding dramatic cases of poverty and stopping social exclusion. to fight poverty effectively also requires improving the quality of jobs and wages, the establishment of the right to income, and everything that implies income from social assistance, pensions, allowances. 2010 is a year of the fight against poverty, continuing the campaign for an inclusive society undertaken by the treaty of lisbon. all the more reason to cast my vote in favor of this campaign.

in writing. − the economic and financial crisis has worsened the situation of the labour market throughout the european union. in the last period alone, some five million jobs have been reported lost, generating poverty and social exclusion in the member states. i strongly support this report because i believe that urgent measures are needed to reintegrate the affected people into the labour market and to guarantee a minimum income capable of ensuring a decent standard of living and a life compatible with human dignity. i believe that we need to develop relevant indicators to enable us to introduce minimum income systems in the member states, thus ensuring an adequate standard of living, fostering social integration and promoting social and economic cohesion throughout the union.
in writing. − poverty is a reality that affects people who do not have enough income to provide an acceptable standard of living, and whose numbers are increasing because of the current crisis. in 2008, 17% (almost 85 million people) of the eu population were at risk of poverty. the rate of at-risk-of-poverty was higher among children and young people aged up to 17 years in relation to the total population, at 20% in the eu-27, with the highest values in romania (33%). the at-risk-of-poverty rate among the working population was on average 8% in the eu-27, with the highest rate also in romania (17%). i voted for the need to adopt a system of calculating minimum income (equivalent to at least 60% of the average income in the member state concerned) in all member states, consisting of specific measures to support people with low incomes by means of a financial contribution and by facilitating access to services. this could be one of the most effective ways of combating poverty, ensuring an adequate standard of living and fostering social inclusion.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report for two reasons. the first reason is that its authors have done an extraordinary job, which has resulted in a complex analysis of the causes and consequences of the economic crisis on the global economy on the one hand, and on the european economy on the other. the second reason for my vote is that the report contains a number of important recommendations, in that part of the report which argues that the future is a europe of added value. we must recognize that europe has lost, from a narrow view of short-term profit, a great many jobs in high value-added industries, while creating precariousness and poverty in work. it is time to reverse the trend, to re-industrialize the european union, to rebuild its capacity to innovate and create jobs in sectors linked to research and development and new technologies.

president of the council. - ladies and gentlemen, at its meeting on 14 october the council adopted conclusions on the position of the european union with a view to the cancún climate conference, at which the global framework for climate protection is to be discussed. on the basis of this text, the european council meeting in october next week, on 18 and 19 october, will establish the european union's position for the 16th conference of the parties to the united nations convention on climate change. this position of the european union covers all aspects of importance to this conference: the expected outcomes, the conditions for the continuation of the kyoto protocol beyond 2012, the progress to be made in the various areas set out in the bali roadmap mitigation, adaptation, forest technology aspects and financing. the council has endeavoured to present clear and communicated positions on all these aspects. it is now up to all actors in the european union to use these positions to send a clear and unambiguous message to our international partners. as the council has just indicated, the european union hopes that the cancún meeting will lead to the adoption of a balanced set of decisions contributing to the establishment of an international regime for climate protection after 2012. several bilateral meetings and contacts will take place before cancún and will be an opportunity to explain our positions to our partners. at the conference itself, these positions will be clarified if necessary during the coordination meetings which the european union will hold on a regular basis on the spot. of course, we are counting on all the institutions to help clarify our position by conveying the same message to all external contacts, if possible.
president of the council. - i must tell you and give you as clarification that it is true, progress will be difficult in cancun. three reasons for this relative pessimism. firstly, the economic crisis which obviously affects the european union but also many countries outside the european union, which in any case means that the goodwill and the investment claims in this area are rather downplayed; the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the european union has maintained the positions it took in copenhagen, and i think we must be careful in the way we engage today so as not to override the positions and the guidelines we may take in cancun in a month's time.
