president of the council. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the council would of course like to recall that the free movement of persons is one of the fundamental freedoms guaranteed by the treaty and secondary legislation, and that it includes the right for citizens of the european union to live and work in another member state. as regards the temporary restrictions provided for in the accession treaties, it is for each member state that continues to apply restrictions to assess the impact on its labour market and decide whether to maintain the remaining restrictions or to relax them before the end of the transitional period: april 2011 for countries that acceded in 2004 and december 2013 for countries that acceded in 2007. the council also invited those member states which continued to apply restrictions under the transitional provisions laid down in the accession treaties to lift them during the third phase of the transitional period if it could not be established that their labour market was suffering or was likely to suffer from serious disturbances. since may 2009, when denmark granted free access to its labour market, the transitional provisions applied by the member states have not been changed and while the majority of member states grant free access to workers from member states that acceded after 1 may 2004, ten member states still apply restrictions. the council stressed that the economic and financial crisis should not be invoked as a single and general justification for maintaining the provisions in question and invited the member states to further develop strategies and appropriate tools to identify and analyse obstacles to the geographical and occupational mobility of workers and to contribute effectively to the elimination of existing obstacles, in accordance with the treaty.
i thank you for your reply, mr minister, and i would ask you to continue to ask the council of the european union to ask the member states to lift the barriers and the transitional provisions restricting the free movement of workers from the new member states, in particular romania and bulgaria. and i want to stress that providing equal opportunities in the european labour market for all workers in all member states means equally protecting workers in the countries of destination. that is why i ask you, mr minister, to ask the member states to remove the existing barriers.
in writing. i would like to welcome the progress made in the acta negotiation process. this agreement is essential in order to establish common international standards on the application of intellectual property law. however, i would point out that the measures to punish infringements of intellectual property must respect the principle of proportionality and balance between the seriousness of the acts committed and the penalties imposed. i am referring in particular to cases of infringement of intellectual property in digital media and the internet, where a clear distinction should be made in the treatment of large-scale piracy for commercial purposes and isolated and unsystematic cases of intellectual property fraud. in addition, regardless of the seriousness of the offences committed, the agreement should pay particular attention to the protection of freedom of expression, due process and confidentiality.

the development of an integrated maritime policy is an absolute necessity given the fragmented approach of the past, which has led to inefficiencies and conflicts in this area. the report by mrs meissner reiterates the european parliament's view that an integrated, coherent and common decision-making process should be created for the oceans, seas, coastal regions and maritime sectors. the integrated maritime policy facilitates a pan-sectoral approach to maritime governance by promoting the identification and use of synergies between the european union's policies in this area. the proposal for a regulation provides for a programme which will provide a stable framework for maintaining support for initiatives in this area and will lead to a more coherent use of funds for the seas and coastal areas. the only cost-effective and feasible financing solution in the current economic context was unfortunately the modest financial contribution from the union. i hope that this form of financing will nevertheless enable the objectives of the integrated maritime policy to be achieved in the short and medium term.
the importance of an integrated maritime policy is undeniable in a context where the european union is the world's leading maritime power and around 40% of the union's gross domestic product is produced around the seas and coastal areas. the implementation of these policy objectives must take particular account of the regional specificities of the seas around europe. each maritime region is unique and requires individual attention to sustainably balance its uses. at the same time, we need to ensure that this policy is adequately funded for the next programming period, thus generating a new approach that aims to promote the optimal development of all maritime activities in a sustainable way and covering all sea basins. so we'll get much more benefits with less impact on the environment.
shipping and shipbuilding make a significant contribution to the economic prosperity of the countries of the european union and provide important services to european and global industry and consumers. i congratulate mrs meissner on her report and stress the importance of a barrier-free maritime area, while at the same time calling on the commission and the member states to assess and ensure the conservation of small seaports, to extend the short sea transport network to minimise land transport distances, to support research and innovation in freight transport modes, handling and logistics solutions to reduce transport time and handling costs, and to support the development of port infrastructure and intermodality. underlining the geostrategic importance of the black sea, the european council should ask the european commission to develop a european union strategy for the black sea. unfortunately, little attention has been paid to the black sea, which is of geostrategic importance to the european union.
in writing. – in my capacity as rapporteur on eu strategy for the black sea, i noticed with regret that matters related to the black sea are almost ignored in the union’s integrated maritime policy (imp). though the black sea was included in the imp concept in 2007, concrete eu action on this dimension seems to lag behind. i strongly urge the european commission to redouble efforts to develop the black sea approach of this policy. imp is an important tool for addressing opportunities and challenges in eu sea basins in a coherent manner which is aimed at comprehensive development of the coastal zones. i am deeply convinced that the black sea, as a sea partially within the eu, and its littoral states have an acute need for proper application of this tool. the international dimension of the imp is a crucial aspect for successful implementation in the black sea region, which also encompasses seven non-eu countries. the european parliament is currently preparing a report on establishing an eu strategy for the black sea. i hope that the commission will follow this initiative and will regard the future strategy as an important basis for strengthened imp implementation in the black sea area.

mr president, the current situation in zimbabwe is appalling and unacceptable. nearly 700 people were victims of the 2005 operation murambatsvina forced evictions. now 20 000 citizens face forced evictions from the hatcliffe extension near harare. the government has imposed unaffordable lease renewal fees on the people who were evicted, and has failed to consult with citizens or to inform them of the upcoming regulations. operation garikai intended to assist those who were affected by the 2005 evictions is merely a continuation of the same human rights abuses. i join in insisting that zimbabwe halt these evictions of citizens in the harare region. i urge the government of zimbabwe to immediately amend operation garikai to comply with all obligations under international and human rights law. i ask the commission to raise this issue as a matter of urgency with the government of zimbabwe.

the european parliament, the council and the commission have adopted a joint resolution on the situation in cambodia. after being excluded from the national assembly and having his parliamentary immunity revoked three times so far, after numerous assassination attempts and dozens of his supporters killed, sam rainsy is now being sentenced in absentia for his politically charged protests. the ultimate goal of the september sentence is to prevent the opposition leader from running for re-election in two years, which will ultimately jeopardize cambodia's chances of democratization. the demands made to the cambodian government in this resolution to put an end to the political persecution are accompanied by a request to the high representative of the european union for foreign affairs and security policy to exert the necessary pressure on the authorities to resume the political and institutional reforms necessary to establish a genuine democracy.
it is unfortunate that cambodian courts still use arrest as a tool to intimidate political opponents and dissidents. journalists, human rights activists, and other critical voices promoting freedom of expression are most often targeted. it is clear that the charges against sam rainsy are more political than criminal. he was sentenced to 12 years in prison after a symbolic gesture of protest against the way the border with vietnam was drawn. the real reason for the conviction, however, appears to be to remove the opposition from the electoral race for the 2013 parliamentary elections. i would therefore like to call on the cambodian government to honour its commitments to strengthen the democratic state. mr. sam rainsy, as the main opposition leader, must be allowed to resume his duties in the cambodian parliament as soon as possible. this would stop the evolution towards a one-party system, which is dangerous for the respect of human rights.
it's about, in the case of sam rainsy, as it was said, two convictions. in addition to the oldest, two-year-old, there's a 10-year-old for a misdemeanor count of false reporting and falsification of public records. it is obvious, as my colleagues have said, that this is an attempt to block his participation in the upcoming elections. there is a procedural issue in this whole story, namely that sam rainsy was convicted in absentia in proceedings that took place behind closed doors and which, as has been reported, were marked by numerous irregularities. it's not an isolated case, by the way. there are many more voices critical of the cambodian government who have suffered such treatment with prosecutions and, as has been said, i believe that under the cooperation agreement with the european union, the cambodian authorities must make clear commitments on human rights.

in writing. the eu and the us form the most important trading partnership and account for half of the world economy. on the other hand, the two partners need to cooperate more closely to promote growth and employment in their economies, especially as the economic crisis has destroyed 30 million jobs worldwide in recent years. in this respect, the transatlantic economic council remains the most appropriate mechanism for achieving the objective of a unified transatlantic market by 2015. i believe that the priority issue of visa arrangements for all member states should be discussed at the lisbon summit. as freedom of movement is a highly valued right in the eu, the commission needs to continue the political and technical dialogue on progress made and future lines of action. i would mention that the romanian government recently approved the legislative framework for the creation of a national visa information system, which allows the exchange of data with other member states on visa applications. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a common position on the proposal for a directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the labelling, presentation and advertising of foodstuffs for sale to the ultimate consumer.

the union's population is ageing and the share of the active population in the total population is declining. due to the economic crisis, unemployment has risen to 10%. in this context, the union and the member states should take measures to ensure the sustainability of pension systems. reform of pension systems must provide solutions to guarantee pensioners a minimum income for a decent living. despite the increase in life expectancy, raising the mandatory retirement age is not a solution. older people, who can and want to remain active in the labour market, can continue to contribute to the development of society, but they are not obliged to do so. at the same time, the economic crisis and the relocation of european industry to third countries have reduced the number of jobs and people with the ability to work, unable to find stable employment, are having difficulty meeting the minimum contribution period to public pension schemes. i draw attention to the fact that raising the retirement age will lead to increased unemployment among young people.

in writing. in a europe affected by demographic change, maintaining a balance between respect for rights and social assistance, i.e. the principle of 'a society for all', is a real challenge. i believe that the use of skills by people at the end of their careers is beneficial for society as a whole, and that public authorities, private companies or ngos that develop innovative programmes to involve older people in various activities should be encouraged. the main tools for achieving solidarity between generations remain social dialogue and debate with the affected groups. to this end, programmes can be created in education systems to bring such issues to the attention of young people and to facilitate dialogue with older people. on the other hand, it is beneficial to promote age-blended work teams and to encourage support for companies that implement such initiatives, because generational diversity enhances competitiveness and allows for more harmonious economic growth. the social economy and financial support from the european social fund are ways of creating and developing specific programmes aimed at active ageing and fostering solidarity between generations.
in writing. demography is a key challenge for the european states and regions in the context of the declining and ageing population faced by most member states. demographic risks are a priority of social policies at european level. in the context of continued ageing, low birth rates and demographic disparities, these policies need to identify concrete measures to counter the effects. over the past two decades, the rural population has declined considerably in convergence regions, especially among young people. young people have an important role to play in reducing disparities between urban and rural areas, with the bridging of demographic gaps being an important objective of cohesion policy. we need to put the benefits of rural areas into practice, from investor support to broadband. according to the european statistical institute, the average working age will increase by 7 percent by 2060. member states must have a clear, coherent policy to create solidarity between generations and to involve the population in the labour market at an older age than now.
in writing. i would like to welcome the report by mr thomas mann. the demographic problems facing the european union are becoming increasingly visible and affect rural areas in particular. according to statistics, only 7% of european farmers are under 35 years old, and at the same time, 4.5 million farmers will retire in the next 10 years. we risk seeing a decline in the rural labour force, and these effects will have negative consequences for agricultural productivity in the future. new tools are needed to counter rural demographic problems. one of the key issues is access to education for vocational training of young people in rural areas and their attraction to agriculture. another important aspect would be the implementation of early retirement measures for farmers by all member states, as well as the implementation of measures for the establishment of young farmers. the application of the two measures would lead to a substantial improvement in the management of agricultural holdings through the renewal of the generation of farm managers. last but not least, supporting entrepreneurs in accessing funds for agricultural projects is another key aspect to be taken into account in order to motivate young people in particular to get involved in agriculture.
in writing. europe is ageing faster than other continents and it is worrying that the ratio of the population over 65 to the working age population (aged 15-64) is set to double by 2060 (from 25.4% to 53.5%). in romania, the dynamics of this ratio is worrying, with it set to increase from 21.3% in 2008 to 65.3% in 2060. in view of the scale and speed of population ageing, member states should take into account in their employment policies the gender dimension, new forms of work organisation in enterprises, means of facilitating the transition to retirement through flexible arrangements, improvement of working conditions and promotion of non-discriminatory practices in recruitment and vocational training. i also call on the member states: to promote a culture of ageing management in enterprises and to adapt to its various aspects, in particular by allowing for gradual retirement, taking into account the difficulty of the job, working conditions, health and safety; to continue to maintain early retirement for certain categories of workers, depending on working conditions, and in special situations such as redundancy or restructuring.

first of all, i would like to thank mr victor caldeira for this clear and relevant report on the commission's work and on the implementation of the 2009 budget. secondly, i want to make clear from the outset something that is very important to us: every five years we are elected, sent to the european parliament by european citizens, who pay taxes and who, in the end, make up this budget. from their point of view, because we periodically go home and meet with them, the budget execution for 2009 cannot be a good one. i'll give you just two reasons. firstly, because the national management declarations are not backed by the political factor, they have neither the signature of the minister of finance nor the signature of the prime minister. therefore, we do not know who is responsible for these national management statements and how clear and accurate they are. it basically opens the door to a false and, if not false, incomplete report. secondly, for errors made in the management of european funds, it is the national state itself that has to pay the money back to the commission. in other words, european citizens pay money to the european budget, but they also, as the losers, pay the damage to the national budget. so twice as much money is paid by eu citizens for mistakes, errors or even fraud in the management of eu funds. thirdly, i would like to welcome the commission, welcome the european court of auditors and support, in turn, its better linking up with the national audit institutions in each member state. i think if we want more money in the budget, we have to spend the money we have better first and, to spend the money we have better, we have to know first where the problems are and how we can solve them.
i recall that in 2009, when the european union's economic recovery plan was first discussed, the commission committed to allocating one billion euros to energy efficiency in housing. unfortunately, this was not timely and the 'smart cities' initiative only had a small amount allocated, and subsequently, if there were any unused funds, the commission would allocate this money to the 'smart cities' initiative, which is what is happening with this regulation. i have asked, through an amendment, that the level of management expenditure and the costs associated with the creation and implementation of the instrument should not exceed 5% of the value of each use, so that the bulk of the sum does not go to financial intermediaries but goes to investments for projects related to energy efficiency in housing and the use of renewable energy. we also called for more transparency, the use of the www.buildup.eu website and we also called for the model applied to be made available free of charge to all interested parties whenever this tool is used, so that we can benefit from best practices. i congratulate mrs van brempt on her report and believe that energy efficiency should be at the top of the energy strategy of the european union.
the 'energy 2020' strategy, launched yesterday by the european commission, is an important step towards a secure and competitive energy market in europe. it offers solutions to important problems such as diversifying supply routes and sources, reducing energy consumption or coordinating with third countries. there are, however, visible shortcomings in terms of funding. the european energy recovery programme has as its main objective to facilitate the financing of investments in this area. effective implementation requires that all environmental legislation is complied with and that project promoters meet their funding commitments. i believe that active cooperation between national, regional and local authorities would facilitate the issuing of the necessary authorisations. in conclusion, i would like to stress the importance of public-private partnerships, which are a key element in implementing solutions to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.
in writing. the european energy programme for economic recovery provides a financial package of eur 3,98 billion for 2009 and 2010. the creation of a special financial instrument for the use of the funds from this energy programme that could not be committed by the end of 2010 was imperative in order not to lose the rest of the financial package. a particularly important aspect mentioned in the regulation on the european energy programme is the balanced geographical distribution of projects, which is an essential element in order to ensure the impact of this regulation on economic recovery across the union and which recognises that in certain member states there have been projects that have either not been funded or have been only partially funded. last but not least, i would stress the importance of renewing these types of financial instruments aimed at the union's long-term energy efficiency. i ask the commission to closely assess the effectiveness of renewing these types of instruments and to analyse the potential for using a similar approach in the future for other unspent funds from the eu budget.
i think it should be said at the outset that it is not farmers but consumers who are the main victims of the crisis we are talking about today. it is known that on farms grain prices influence about 80% of the feed price. this in turn influences about 70% of the cost of production. a proportional increase in the selling price of meat to the producer is impossible. the farmers have no contact with the final consumer, but turn to the processors, who always have the option of importing. at the same time, processors transfer the high profit margin they have become accustomed to in the selling price. unfortunately, this period overlaps with a general economic crisis, and the decline in the purchasing power of the population is also affecting livestock production. another aspect: with farmers having difficulty in securing food for their animals during the winter, many will choose to slaughter their animals, which will prolong the crisis for many years to come. in order to keep internal prices at a reasonable level and to meet the need for feed, intervention stocks must be released and i welcome the announcement made today by commissioner ciolos. i share the view of my colleagues who today stressed the importance of cultivating new genetically modified organisms to provide cheap animal feed and reduce dependence on imports. last but not least, today's debate is closely linked to the future of the common agricultural policy. we need a strong, well-funded and well-managed common agricultural policy, which allows for both structural development and modernisation measures and market measures and direct support.
in writing. european livestock farmers have recently been facing increasing difficulties. they have difficulty in coping with competition from third countries, as they do not meet the high standards of domestic producers and are always the victims of the european union's trade negotiations. but i hope we will see a different attitude from the european commission in the future, because it is not normal that european farmers always lose out in trade agreements. increased involvement of the commission in strengthening producer organisations in all livestock subsectors is also needed to enable them to negotiate better prices for their products, taking into account production prices. at the same time, i ask the commission to release cereals from intervention stocks as soon as possible to help this sector hit by the crisis.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament's resolution on the mobilisation of the egf in respect of aid to redundant workers. in october 2009, ireland submitted a request for assistance for the use of the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) in respect of redundancies in sr technics, an air transport company in the dublin region of ireland. the global financial and economic crisis has caused a reduction in air transport activity, leading to massive redundancies in this sector as well. in ireland, 1 135 redundancies were recorded between april and august 2009, 850 of which were at sr technics ireland ltd. recognising the importance of the egf for the reintegration of dismissed workers into the labour market, as evidenced by the approximately 11 applications approved in 2010 alone totalling over eur 30 million, i consider that this instrument is still insufficiently known and used at member state level. i also ask the european commission to analyse the redundancies in the public sector during the economic and financial crisis and to develop a similar egf instrument to support workers made redundant in the public sector in different member states.
in writing. − the adoption by a large majority of the report by mr agustín diaz de mera demonstrates the usefulness of the decision to lift the visa requirement for taiwan. the european parliament thus confirms its confidence in the important process of democratisation undertaken in recent years. i want to highlight the remarkable economic progress that taiwan has made. the volume of trade with the eu is significant, taiwan's economy is ranked 25th in the world and continues to grow by over 13% annually. the continued development reduces the chances of the eu facing an illegal migration flow from taiwan. i therefore believe that facilitating the movement of persons must become one of the main elements of bilateral cooperation. the decision to exempt taiwanese nationals from the visa requirement also takes into account the fulfilment of technical conditions relating to the security of travel documents. the introduction of biometric passports in 2008 is one of the positive measures implemented so far. i hope that the european parliament's decision will be approved by the council and that the new provisions will come into force this year. in conclusion, i consider that the decision of the taiwanese authorities to lift the visa requirement for romania, bulgaria and cyprus is appropriate, given the need to respect the reciprocity criteria.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this new amendment to regulation 539/2001 which includes the us northern mariana islands and taiwan on the so-called white list of countries exempt from the visa requirement for entry into the european union as i believe it contributes to increasing freedom of movement for european citizens. i also hope that taiwan will honour its commitment to remove romania and bulgaria from the list of countries for which visa requirements are maintained.
in writing. − access of local and regional public authorities to investment project financing for renewable energy and energy efficiency projects needs to be improved. i welcome the exchange of experience between local and regional authorities in the member states in developing cost-effective energy efficiency projects and in meeting climate change commitments. however, the union needs to implement the necessary financial mechanisms to achieve the objectives of the eu 2020 strategy.
in writing. − welcomes the adoption of the european parliament resolution on the global approach to the transfer of passenger name record (pnr) data to third countries and the commission recommendations to the council to authorise the opening of negotiations between the european union and australia, canada and the united states, for which i voted in favour; it is an approach that strikes the right balance between the security needs of the eu member states and the strict respect for citizens' rights and freedoms. the passenger name record is a highly sensitive database which must be protected as such, so as not to cause any damage to those whose names appear therein. it seems to me important to ensure that, in the negotiation of agreements with the usa, australia and canada, data cannot be used for profiling by extracting certain data from the register. i agree there's a difference between assessing security risks and creating profiles, which can be proven false by misinterpreting data. i hope that the agreements which the commission will negotiate with the countries concerned will meet the requirements of the resolution.
in writing. − as data protection, the right to information autonomy, individual rights and privacy are values that play a very important role in the current digital age and need to be protected with special attention, i believe that the eu must respect and promote a key principle in data protection policies and that any agreement or policy measure must also pass the test of legal proportionality, demonstrating that it aims to achieve the treaty's objectives.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the european union needs to have a coherent and uniform view on the conclusion of future agreements in the field of pnr. this will help to ensure improved protection of personal data and privacy and at the same time help to use such data for the purpose of combating terrorism and serious cross-border crime.
in writing. − the european parliament resolution on european innovation partnerships under the flagship initiative 'innovation union' is a concrete initiative to achieve an integrated european innovation policy. it is all the more important because we must recognise that we have not achieved all the objectives of the lisbon agenda 2000 and that one of the engines of future economic growth must be innovation, the development of the research and development sector. i welcome the introduction of the innovative concept of european innovation partnerships, which is designed to create synergies between existing innovation initiatives. we will have to watch closely how the first pilot programme in this field develops, because it deals with a subject of concern to the whole of the union: the consequences of an ageing population and the extension of working life. my vote for the adoption of this resolution also takes into account the subsequent issues, which will be addressed after the evaluation of the pilot project, issues which are part of the general interest area.
in writing. − i voted for this resolution because i believe that the principle of public-private innovation partnerships can boost research and innovation and help to re-launch demand in times of crisis. they are also important for achieving the europe 2020 objectives of creating a more competitive economy, a fairer society and a greener society.
in writing. - i voted for the strengthening of the osce, based on the need to achieve a congruence of the three major dimensions underlying the organisation: political-military, economic-environmental and human. this strengthening of the osce must be achieved within a balance in which neither of these dimensions is supported to the detriment of the other. the effective response to security threats and challenges depends on the proper coordination and functioning of the three directorates. the osce must be the key factor in responding mainly to new threats such as organised crime, terrorism, cyber attacks, trafficking in human beings and drugs, and warnings, prevention and conflict resolution activities. a further reason to vote in favour of strengthening the osce is the human rights component, respect for minority rights and fundamental freedoms, which are central elements of the osce's integrated security concept.
in writing. − underlining that a society that respects human dignity is based on the principle of intergenerational equity, i believe this report is important for combating prejudice and discrimination in all its forms and faced by all groups in society. i believe that the migration of citizens, their successful integration, including their economic integration and social inclusion, can be one of the ways to deal with demographic change; and for this reason i agree that an open debate is essential to discuss different immigration policies. the elimination of prejudices against different cultural models is a prerequisite for the successful integration of migrants, complementing solidarity between generations and cultures. the report also proposes new provisions against age discrimination in access to goods and services. that is why i voted in favour of mr thomas mann's report.
in writing. − eu member states have been experiencing a dramatic decline in their birth rates in recent years, as their populations are increasingly ageing. it's good that life expectancy has increased, keeping people physically and mentally active for longer. in these circumstances, it is clear that we are faced with the prospect of a worsening of the situation, with a demographic imbalance that is having an impact on the economies and budgetary resources of the member states, and on the union as a whole. we are therefore faced with the possibility that future generations will bear the financial burden of these demographic developments. in these circumstances, the lisbon target of half of people aged 55 to 64 being employed becomes imperative, even if this year has been missed. to counter this, the involvement of young and older people in the labour market needs to be strengthened rapidly and decisively in a life-cycle approach. the percentage of unemployed people aged 15-24 is significantly higher than that of all other age groups in the eu. the proposal for a european youth guarantee is therefore advisable.
in writing. − as member states have the main tools to promote intergenerational equity and eliminate discrimination, and as the number of people over 60 years old in the european union will increase at an unprecedented rate, with the peak expected between 2015 and 2035, when two million people will join this segment of the population each year, i believe that the eu must have an effective policy to ensure that workers can remain in the labour market and are not discriminated against on grounds of age, and that the involvement of more women of all age groups in lifelong learning programmes must be maximised.
in writing. − age discrimination undermines solidarity between generations, being prohibited by the treaty, but remains widespread, considerably restricting older and younger workers' access to the labour market, social security and certain services. i voted for member states to take firm action against the grey or underground economy maintained by undeclared work, whose victims are mostly women, whose effects on the european labour market are more than disastrous, and not to be content with taking measures to protect their own workers. at the same time, undeclared work must be combated through concrete measures and the application of sanctions to employers and/or intermediaries. i also voted for the member states and the commission to cooperate in the area of care services supervision, cooperation in which member states could envisage, in respect of national care services, a network of contact points, which would allow, both at national and european level, to obtain information on the care services provided and their level of quality, and to make complaints about the quality of these services.
in writing. − research makes a fundamental contribution to economic growth, job creation and clean and sustainable energy. i support improving research funding in the european union, as it is essential to the achievement of a european research area that requires ensuring the highest standards of excellence, effectiveness and efficiency in research in order to attract and retain the best scientists in europe and to promote an innovative european economy based on knowledge and skills. europe must invest in research to develop new products and services that improve the quality of life of its citizens. i voted in favour of this framework programme because i believe it encourages the research communities, academia, civil society organisations, business and industry to participate in research projects.
in writing. − the union is keenly aware that research and innovation are the key to the future as they lead not only to the creation of new products but also to the creation of new jobs, resources and, consequently, economic growth. this will, in turn, lead to an increase in europe's competitiveness and, as a consequence, an increase in the quality of life. in these circumstances, the increase in bureaucracy in access to finance for those running research and innovation programmes only serves to dampen and reduce the enthusiasm of those developing them, who are already showing signs of losing confidence in the process. the current system should be replaced by a system that gives more confidence to applicants. a step forward would be to simplify the monitoring of the financial and administrative aspects of projects, while strengthening the scientific and technological evaluation process. it should be possible, firstly, to simplify bureaucratic control and to give more confidence to the scientific and business communities. a balance between trust and control, between risk-taking and the dangers of risk, is necessary to ensure the proper management of research funds.
in writing. − i voted for the simplification of the implementation of the research framework programmes, considering this as a fundamental aspect of facilitating scientific and educational development, which in turn can contribute to the creation of new jobs and economic growth, increasing the eu's competitiveness and improving the quality of life of its citizens. the current system should be replaced by a system that gives more confidence to applicants. the increase in funding applications has been met by increased control mechanisms in an attempt to ensure the proper use of eu funds. a balance needs to be struck between trust and control, between risk-taking and the dangers that risk entails, to ensure the correct financial management of eu research funds. the european parliament has voted in favour of the new eu funds, which are intended to help the new member states in eastern europe to bring their research up to western standards.
in writing. − i voted for this report because i believe that the implementation of the seventh research framework programme (fp7) suffered from certain weaknesses which prevented it from being put into practice under the best conditions. i believe that this parliament's proposal provides the necessary solutions to simplify grant award procedures, involve small businesses and new entrants more and increase synergies between fp7 funds and other european funds, including structural funds.
in writing. - the positive vote on this report is based on three aspects. the first relates to my previous activities. we've noticed the great attention that citizens have paid to research in the area of early detection and therefore prevention of cancer, and it's become clear that research is essential to improving people's lives, but only if the link is clear. i therefore considered that this report, which aims to simplify the way in which r & d & i funding is allocated through framework programme 7, deserves to be promoted. the second aspect is the importance i attach to smes as central to the economic development and the development of the european union's global competitiveness. the report's provisions on ensuring access to information and facilitating sme participation by developing the one-stop shop system, the open access initiative, and training campaigns made me appreciate the report and give it my vote. last but not least, i appreciated the contributions to the future framework programme 8, which needs to be much more transparent, flexible and easily accessible. the proposals for simplification, clarification, appreciation of the results proposed in the report are commendable.
in writing. − science, education and innovation are the pillars of economic growth and job creation. europe must invest in innovation if it is to develop new products and services. research and innovation are at the heart of the europe 2020 strategy, but it is particularly difficult for smaller organisations, smes, high-tech start-ups and smaller institutes, universities and research centres to cope with the complexity of the procedures for accessing funds for this sector. the scientific community is urgently calling for harmonisation of rules and procedures and a general simplification of financial responsibility requirements. recently, 13 000 researchers signed a petition calling for greater simplification and trust in eu research funding. it is, of course, necessary to simplify the mechanisms involved in the community framework programmes for research, technological development and demonstration activities, fp7 and fp8, and in all the european commission's innovation and science programmes. i believe that much more research is needed to measure the impact of environmental and climate policies on employment, and i call on the commission to give priority to this area in the eighth framework programme.

in writing. - the food market has developed in recent years in a paradoxical way. one is that, despite rising food prices, farmers, including livestock farmers in the eu, are facing an income crisis that threatens the existence of their farms and impoverishes them. we must be aware that the high quality standards imposed on livestock farmers come at a cost, and if competition from imports from third countries which do not impose the same high standards, not to mention the case of chinese milk powder infected with melamine, is not kept under control, these costs will lead to a reduction in community production in this field. the commission's intention to release a quantity of fodder cereals is only one step towards helping the sector, and others must follow. that is why i believe that the recommendations contained in the resolution, if they are taken up by the commission and implemented, will meet the demands of the farmers, which is why i voted in favour of it.

president of the ecb. mr president, mr rapporteur, honourable members of parliament, mr balz, ladies and gentlemen, members of the european parliament, the committee on the environment, public health and consumer protection, the committee on the environment, public health and consumer protection, the committee on the environment, public health and consumer protection, the committee on the environment, public health and consumer protection, the committee on the environment, public health and consumer protection, the committee on the environment, public health and consumer protection, the committee on the environment, have all made a very good report. i have the honour to present to you, as required by the treaty, the 2009 annual report of the european central bank. because of the slightly upset timetable, particularly with the european elections, i spoke to you last march on the previous annual report. this is the second time this year that i have spoken before parliament. first of all, let me welcome the support once again expressed in the european parliament's motion for a resolution for regular hearings before the committee on economic and monetary affairs and, more generally, for maintaining close relations with the european central bank. i am particularly pleased that this year the european parliament has shown very strongly its willingness and ability to put the european interest first, particularly in the financial supervision package. i shall first give you a brief overview of the monetary policy measures taken by the ecb during the financial and economic crisis. i would also like to look back at the ecb during its first twelve years. finally, i would like to address the most urgent challenges that await us in 2011. mr president, let me first mention the action taken during the crisis. 2009 was a most challenging year for the ecb's monetary policy. it started with a severe economic downturn worldwide following the outbreak of the financial crisis in autumn 2008. in this environment of subdued inflationary pressures, we continued with our policy of lowering our key rates further. overall, within a period of only seven months between october 2008 and may 2009 we lowered our main refinancing rate by 325 basis points. this brought our main refinancing rate to 1%. to ensure that households and firms in the euro area would benefit from these most favourable financing conditions, in 2009 we also continued with and even extended our enhanced credit support to euro area banks. we did this in response to dysfunctional money markets that had weakened the ability of monetary policy to influence the outlook for price stability by means of interest rate decisions alone. among those non-standard measures as we used to call them the most prominent is the full allotment liquidity provision through our refinancing operations with euro area banks against good collateral and at the main refinancing rate prevailing at the time for several maturities extending well beyond the weekly operations . in 2009 we also extended the maturity of our longer-term refinancing operation to one year. these were, of course, decisions of extreme importance. as rightly emphasised in your draft resolution on the ecb's annual report, this enhanced credit support has been successful in avoiding what would have been if additional dysfunctional tensions had been observed a depression or a much deeper recession. let me emphasise that all our action was fully in line with our mandate to deliver price stability in the medium term for the euro area as a whole. that we have been able to credibly deliver on our mandate is reflected in a favourable inflation outlook and well-anchored inflation expectations in the euro area. following some improvements in financial market conditions in the course of 2009, renewed market tensions erupted in a number of segments of the euro area bond market. since the smooth functioning of the bond market is essential to the transmission of the ecb's key interest rates, we decided to intervene in the euro area debt securities markets with the aim of helping to restore a more normal transmission of monetary policy to the economy. to this end, we introduced our securities markets programme. to ensure that this program does not impact our monetary policy stance, we re-absorb all the liquidity injected. to sum up, let me emphasize that all the non-standard measures we have adopted during the period of acute financial stress are temporary in nature and were designed with exit considerations in mind. some of the non-standard measures initiated in 2009 and early 2010 have already been phased out in view of improvements in conditions in some financial markets and taking the ongoing recovery of the euro area economy into account. let me share with you for a moment a few thoughts on the track record of the euro. in my view, three elements are fundamental. first, the ecb has delivered what it was expected to deliver according to its treaty mandate, namely price stability. indeed, euro area average inflation over the past almost 12 years stands at 1.97%. this fully reflects our definition of price stability, namely our aim to keep annual inflation rates in the euro area below 2% and close to 2% in the medium term. in this sense, the euro system over the past 12 years has operated as an anchor of stability and confidence and has done so during the most recent times, despite the challenging environment created by the global financial crisis. secondly and reflecting favourably on the credibility of the ecb's monetary policy inflation expectations have, as i have said, remained solidly anchored at levels in line with price stability. thirdly, this success is based, we trust, on the ecb's full independence from political influence, on its primary mandate to maintain price stability and on its transparent communication, particularly concerning the definition of price stability. the ecb's two-pillar monetary strategy allows for a forward-looking and medium-term-oriented course of action that is underpinned by a solid analytical framework. that framework includes a thorough analysis of monetary and credit developments, taking the monetary nature of inflation over the medium to longer term into account. we consider that this comprehensive approach allows for well-informed and consistent decision-making, whilst being steady and looking beyond short-term volatility. as regards the external dimension of the euro, let me just say that our currency has established itself internationally. in 2009 the euro represented around 30% of the stock of international debt securities and the stock of global foreign exchange reserves. speaking of the external dimension of the euro, i will say a word on the present foreign exchange rate issues, domains where i would call for great prudence. there are two major topics. one is the relationship between the major floating convertible currencies of the industrialized countries, such as the dollar, the euro, the yen, the pound sterling and the canadian dollar. these currencies have been floating since the collapse of the bretton woods system at the beginning of the 1970s. i should underline the strong view of the international community that excessive volatility and disorderly movements in exchange rates have adverse implications for economic and financial stability. let me say that the ecb appreciates the recent statements by the us authorities, namely the us secretary of the treasury and the chairman of the federal reserve, reiterating that a strong dollar vis-à-vis the other major convertible currencies is in the interests of the united states. i share this view entirely. a dollar that is credible among the major currencies of the advanced economies is in the interests of the united states, of europe and of the entire international community. the second topic concerns the currencies of emerging market economies which have current account surpluses and exchange rates that are not sufficiently flexible. on this issue, the international community agrees and this was reiterated in korea last week, as well as by the commission that moving towards more market-determined exchange rate systems, enhancing exchange rate stability to reflect underlying fundamentals and refraining from competitive devaluation of currencies are in the interest of the emerging economies concerned and of the international community. the ecb used to say that this is no time for complacency. this is truer now than ever. the challenges lying ahead of us are manifold. all relevant authorities as well as the private sector must assume their responsibilities fully, and this is true for executive branches, central banks, regulators, supervisors, the private sector and the financial industry. in particular, the current crisis has clearly demonstrated that implementing ambitious reforms in economic governance is in the interest of both the euro area countries and the euro area as a whole. the proposals put forward by president van rompuy on the reform of the eu's economic governance and approved by the european council meeting of october 2010 represent an improvement to the current surveillance framework at eu level and seem broadly appropriate for the eu countries not participating in monetary union. however, as regards the specific requirements of the euro area, in our opinion they fall short of what we view as necessary to ensure the best possible functioning of the single currency economy. i am convinced that, over the coming months, the european parliament will help europe make the necessary quantum leap in economic governance a reality. with its legislative role concerning financial supervision and the esrb, parliament has shown its determination when it comes to major issues. i would like to take this opportunity to thank you for this, and to reiterate my conviction that the influence of parliament will be decisive in the economic governance debate. another important challenge relates to financial regulation. we should take full advantage of the lessons of the crisis and maintain the momentum for financial reform. as advocated in your draft resolution, a speedy implementation of basel iii is of crucial importance. the commission's legislative proposals on short selling and over-the-counter derivatives are also indispensable to making the financial system more transparent and resilient. we are facing a decisive year. 2011 should see the adoption of the revised governance framework, in-depth discussions on the crisis management framework and possibly the launch of the procedure for a treaty change. we need to get all these reforms right, so as to ensure that europe as a whole and the euro area can meet future challenges with even greater capacity and conviction. 2011 will also be the first year of the european systemic risk board. as is called for in your draft resolution, we are doing our utmost to support the new body. at the same time, of course, the complete independence and primary mandate of the ecb, enshrined in the maastricht treaty, are unchanged, and i have already stressed this point before parliament. we will continue to deliver on our mandate. this is what the treaty requires from us. you can trust that we will deliver what our fellow citizens expect.
member of the commission. − mr president, let me first thank the rapporteur, burkhard balz, for the solid and comprehensive report on the ecb annual report 2009. the commission welcomes the report, which reflects the key issues appropriately. the report recognises and praises the work done by the ecb in managing the crisis. the commission shares this view; the ecb, under the leadership of president jean-claude trichet, has navigated in this difficult situation skilfully and with a steady hand. i want to use this opportunity to thank jean-claude trichet for an excellent cooperation and especially for his crucial role during these turbulent times. the ecb has, both through its monitoring stance and its non-standard measures, been instrumental in the fire-fighting to overcome the crisis and thus in laying the foundations for sustainable growth and job creation. your report rightly stresses that the financial crisis has exposed the need for reinforced economic surveillance in the euro area. the commission agrees with this, which is precisely why we have put forward several legislative proposals to reinforce economic governance in the eu, especially in the euro area. we have also taken on board several suggestions presented in the feio report to strengthen and broaden economic governance in the union. the committee on economic and monetary affairs has received the commission’s proposals and is currently working towards achieving the ambitious deadline of june next year, which i appreciate and welcome. let me now turn to the second part of the debate, which is the latest developments in the international exchange rates. it is correct that volatility in foreign exchange markets has increased in recent weeks, with significant shifts in the value of major bilateral exchange rates. the euro appreciated against the dollar since june this year due to stronger data for the euro area economy and due to further expansion of the us monetary policy. more recently, however, the euro has somewhat weakened against most currencies, as increased worries about the member states’ public finances – above all in ireland – have affected the euro. in real effective terms, the euro is currently close to its long-term average following an overall depreciation this year from an overvalued level at the end of last year. compared to the beginning of the year, the euro depreciation in real effective terms amounts to around 7%. in the context of a slow recovery in advanced economies and large capital flows to emerging economies, many countries have aimed at weakening their currency or at least resorting to competitive non-appreciation. it is therefore important that leaders in the g20 seoul summit last week very clearly and strongly committed themselves to abstain from competitive devaluations of their currencies. the g20 summit also agreed to work further on the rebalancing of global growth. an agreement had been reached to work on indicative guidelines. it is clear that exchange rate flexibility must play a role in the necessary rebalancing so that exchange rates reflect economic fundamentals, as was underlined by president trichet. the commission will continue to support this important strand of g20 work, which will also be one of the key focuses of the french g20 presidency next year. finally, i need to inform you about an important development concerning the euro area. yesterday when the ecofin council welcomed the request of the irish government for financial assistance from the eu, ministers concurred with the commission and the ecb that providing assistance to ireland is warranted to safeguard financial stability in europe. eu financial support can be provided under a programme with a rigorous policy conditionality which is being negotiated currently with the irish authorities by the commission and the imf, in liaison with the ecb. the programme will address the fiscal challenges of the irish economy in a decisive manner and the programme will also include a fund for potential future capital needs of the banking sector. to redress stress in the banking sector, a comprehensive range of measures including deleveraging and restructuring will need to be taken to contribute to ensuring that the irish banking system performs its role properly in the functioning of the overall economy. the technical talks on an eu-imf programme are now well underway and the negotiations can be concluded by the end of november. apart from eu and imf financing, i can inform you that the united kingdom and sweden have indicated that they stand ready to contribute to the programme through bilateral loans, which is welcome. all in all, yesterday’s decisions are a critical step forward in the joint efforts to stabilise the irish economy and thus safeguard financial stability in europe.
on behalf of the s&d group. first of all, i would like to thank the rapporteur, mr balz, for his cooperation and to welcome the conferral of european institution status on the european central bank with the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon. secondly, i would point out the existence of substantial macroeconomic disparities between the euro area economies, which demonstrates the need for closer coordination of economic and monetary policies. the stability and growth pact is not a sufficient instrument to address the existing economic imbalances. one solution to this impasse could be the release of government bonds at the european level. this solidarity mechanism would ensure stable funding for member states in difficulty, increase the efficiency of budgetary surveillance and have a significant liquidity effect. the common currency must be supplemented by fiscal austerity and a unified long-term debt. the risk-taking behaviour of financial actors contributed to the outbreak of the economic and financial crisis. in addition, recent speculative attacks on certain member states have contributed to the latter's difficulty in borrowing money on international financial markets, affecting virtually the stability of the euro area as a whole. i therefore believe that a permanent mechanism is needed to defend the euro area against speculative attacks and that it is the duty of the european commission to monitor the work of the current credit rating agencies and to think about the architecture of a european credit rating agency. we also need to bear in mind that austerity measures by national governments could significantly reduce the chances of a european economic recovery, which is why a model of economic governance at european level is needed that combines fiscal consolidation with job creation. the commission must also propose specific targets to reduce the competitiveness gap between european economies and, not least, aim to invest in green energy.
in writing. i would like to congratulate mr balz for his work on this report. the austerity packages proposed for the exit from the crisis should not lead to measures that could jeopardise the economic recovery. considers it necessary to ensure a balance between the process of economic consolidation and the protection of investments through jobs and sustainable development. the lesson of the countries that entered the euro area unprepared should make us think seriously about setting realistic deadlines. in this context, a one- or two-year delay may be accepted. the enlargement must continue subject to the fulfilment of the maastricht criteria. in this respect, i believe that the adoption of the euro should not be seen as a one-off solution but should be part of a broad medium-term political strategy.
on behalf of the s&d group. as the council's proposal for a directive shows, the minimum vat rate ensured that the system operated at an acceptable level. i believe that we should consider common regulation, which includes the lessons learned from the experience of budgetary imbalances highlighted by the financial crisis. a new european vat strategy is needed, focusing on reducing bureaucracy and tax obstacles to business, especially small and medium-sized enterprises. we also have to take into account the need to prevent and combat fraud, but until this strategy is finalised, i believe that the extension of the transitional provision on the minimum vat rate until 31 december 2015 is a decision designed to ensure certainty for the business environment, to prevent structural imbalances in the european union and to encourage the harmonisation of tax legislation. while awaiting the commission's green paper on the revision of the value added tax system, i would like to draw attention to the tendency of some governments facing recession to raise vat to 24-25%, as has happened in romania and hungary. so far the relative commitment to keep the maximum vat rate within 10 percentage points above the 15% threshold has been respected, but i believe that in order to prevent any breaches of the 25% threshold we need an imperative ban on this. let us not forget that beyond these figures are citizens whose living standards are increasingly affected by austerity policies and excessive taxation. in conclusion, i want to say that overtaxation is not a solution to a sick economy, it only prolongs its agony.
the new vat strategy should aim to reduce administrative burdens, remove tax obstacles and improve the business environment, especially for smes. there is a lack of balance in relation to the development of the internal market. this puts european companies at a disadvantage. moreover, the vat system as currently designed and applied in the member states has shortcomings, which are exploited by tax evaders. i would like to call on the commission to present the results of its analysis. it will also have to organise consultations on the new vat strategy with all stakeholders. in this context, common issues such as reduced vat rates, derogations from the system, the appropriateness of setting a maximum rate and, not least, the place of taxation for intra-eu supplies will have to be addressed.

member of the commission. − mr president, during my hearing as commissioner-designate i made it clear that information to patients is a very important topic for me. patients are highly interested in their own health and wellbeing. but today the availability of information on medicines in europe is very diverse: you could even say very unfair. whether patients obtain the relevant information depends on languages, it skills and often even social class and networks. for a europe that strives to overcome today’s health and inequalities, this is not sustainable. the key ambition of the commission’s initial proposal therefore remains justified, and i applaud parliament and in particular your rapporteur, mr fjellner, on taking this important proposal forward. however, i strongly believe – as i also stressed during my hearing – that we have to address this file from a patient’s angle. we have to ask what information patients need, not what information industry may wish to provide. we have to ensure that we do not drift into direct-to-consumer advertising, which patients clearly do not want. again i applaud parliament for taking exactly this stance. this will allow the commission to accept many of your key amendments when we present our modified proposals. this concerns, in particular, the obligation to publish information, the question of what information is covered, the information distribution channels and the control mechanisms. firstly, i support the amendment stating that industry must have the obligation and not just the right to make certain information on medicinal products available. this is a very important change. secondly, as regards what information is published, i generally agree that information should not cover comparisons between medicinal products, as this could be seen as promotional. of course this information is highly relevant for patients and healthcare professionals but, due to its potential abuse for promotion, it needs a strict framework. we are cooperating with member states on such a framework in the area of health technology assessments. i also share the view that the proposals should concern the information made available by industry and not by third parties such as journalists and scientists. however, we know that there is a grey zone which leaves room for abuse. i therefore believe that such parties should be obliged to declare whether they have received financial or other benefits from industry. thirdly, as regards the information channels, i partially agree with your amendments. however, not everybody uses the internet; we must avoid corroborating inequalities by excluding those who do not use digital communication tools from access to medical information. i consider, therefore, that it should be possible for industry to draft printed material on its own initiative and not only by request. this draft information could be used on request by the public or via healthcare professionals. fourthly, on the control of information, i agree that information which has not already been approved during the marketing authorisation process must be pre-approved by competent authorities as a matter of principle. however, i believe that europe should play close attention to the constitutional concerns that some member states raise as regards the compatibility of pre-vetting with freedom of expression. it should be possible for these member states to provide for exposed control, irrespective of whether they already have such exposed control in place. several of parliament’s amendments concern information from sources other than industry sources. in this context, let me stress that i fully agree with the political ambition to place the proposals on industry-generated information on medicines, which we are discussing today, in a broader and more comprehensive agenda on patient information. yes, there are other very important sources which have to be exploited as fully as possible, but the proposals are not the right place to address them. the commission is already obliged to draft a report on the readability of the package leaflet. therefore, any changes regarding this issue would be premature. nor is it feasible to introduce, for each clinical study mentioned in the summary of the european public assessment report, a link to the eurydice database on clinical trials. a general link between databases would suffice. the public summary of the assessment report should not be annexed to the european marketing authorisation, as it is already publicly available through the ema website. i recognise that, in addition to information provided by industry, there are already a number of european and national databases and portals providing information on medicinal products. what we lack is interlinkage between them. i propose that the future european medicinal web portal recently created by the pharmacovigilance directive be used as a central point to access information. in this context i fully recognise the need for broader information about diseases and their prevention. patients are interested in all different treatment options, not just learning about medicines. however, this cannot be addressed through the present proposals, which focus on medicines. nevertheless, the commission is well placed to serve as a european information switchboard. i see our role as connecting other reliable information providers such as member states or patient organisations. european action can add value, and many information tools such as the eu health portal are already in place. honourable members, you will not be surprised that there are some amendments that the commission, after careful reflection, cannot support. the right of citizens to lodge complaints, for example, is a fundamental eu principle. it is neither appropriate nor necessary to restate this. the level of penalties should be determined at national level and not at european legislative level. a list of the commission’s positions on all the proposed amendments has been made available to parliament. let me conclude by again thanking parliament and mr fjellner and the shadow rapporteurs for your important contribution. i hope this week’s vote will help strengthen patients’ access to information and convince the council of the need to start in-depth discussions of the proposals.
rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on the internal market and consumer protection. − mr president, i would like to congratulate the rapporteur and the other colleagues who have contributed to this dossier. i would also like to congratulate commissioner dalli. i think we have reached a good outcome, and now the report is much more patient-oriented than the initial proposal. nowadays, patients increasingly tend to seek health-related information so that they can be actively involved in the decisions concerning their health. patients also tend to seek information online. this information is not easy to control on the internet, but sooner or later we have to deal with that problem, which will not disappear if we simply do not do anything because it is too complicated. i therefore support imposing strict rules for the registration and monitoring of websites, as well as making available a list of registered websites so that patients can be sure of the reliability of their source. safeguards are also needed, and the report provides them, namely by limiting the information that can be made available to information that is approved by the competent authorities. to this end, we in the committee on the internal market and consumer protection have adopted number of amendments covering advertising, concentrating on changing the wording from ‘disseminate’ to ‘make available’ in the context of non-promotional information according to the ‘pull principle’, whereby patients have access to information if they need it.
in writing. – the environment committee has made some important improvements to the commission's proposal which, in its original form, would not have prevented all forms of advertising of prescription drugs directly to patients. prescription medicines are not like ordinary consumer goods. they should be supplied by clinical experts, not marketed like cars or cosmetics. so i welcome the continued ban on advertising of prescription medicines on television, radio, and in the print media. healthcare professionals remain the most trusted source of information about medicines. so i cannot support the rapporteur's amendment which would allow healthcare professionals to distribute additional, unapproved material from the pharmaceutical companies directly to patients. this would represent a clear opportunity to advertise, something which we want to avoid and which would be inconsistent with our position against direct advertising to patients. it is especially inappropriate because the material directly from the pharmaceutical company would, in the patient's eyes, carry the legitimacy of the doctor distributing it. on the whole, the report represents improvements for patients compared to the commission proposal, and we should not undermine these improvements by allowing pharmaceutical companies to advertise directly to patients in the doctor’s surgery.

i believe that both the proposal to close the mines and the suggestion to reduce subsidies would be premature and would have undesirable socioeconomic and regional consequences. we must not forget that the mining sector in europe employs some 100 000 people, 42 000 in the coal sector and 55 000 in related sectors, and that certain regions in europe are completely dependent on this sector economically. a large number of people in these areas work in mines or have occupations related to the sector. the consequences of such measures could be disastrous, even impoverishing entire communities. a strategy for the retraining of workers affected by mine closure plans must therefore be developed rapidly. special support from the european union's structural funds is also needed to rebuild the regions that will suffer from these measures. in addition, miners and their families can lose confidence in the political process through which such decisions are made, which directly affect them, if they are made at the wrong time. we must also look at the less populated regions, which will suffer the most socioeconomically. i don't think 2014 is a realistic time frame for mine closures. on the other hand, the 2020 deadline proposal, which was put forward by the itre commission, did not have enough positive feedback and therefore i believe that we can find a common denominator in 2018. i would also like to mention that the coal industry is an integral part of european policy and is a source of its own, thus guaranteeing security of supply. a transitional period is needed to enable these mines and those which could become competitive to become competitive in order to ensure access to european coal and to avoid adverse socioeconomic effects.
coal is an important part of the european union's energy mix. in the european union, the coal mining sector provides 280 000 jobs, mainly in mono-industrial areas. it is therefore important that the union should secure as much of its coal needs from domestic production as possible, obviously at a competitive price, based on the efficiency of the coal extraction and processing process. without the state aid, production will fall by 20% and 100,000 jobs will be lost. state aid to the oil industry is very necessary for non-competitive mines. they are uncompetitive because of their outdated technical equipment and the state aid would allow them to retrofit these facilities to ensure job security. we support the commission's proposal to delay the closure of the mines. the itre committee voted for 2020 and we will support the compromise reached by rapporteur rapkay and his colleagues from the other political groups. we support the abolition of article 3 (1) (h) and in particular the abolition of the percentage prescribed for the phasing out of aid granted, so that member states which will grant state aid to uncompetitive coal mines have as much flexibility as possible. i believe, however, that the member states should also present plans for the economic and social development of mining regions, which are often mono-industrialised regions. these development plans should aim at job creation and investments in energy efficiency and renewable energy production. i congratulate the rapporteur, mr rapkay, on his report and on the work he has done.
