the union's energy strategy should focus on energy efficiency, reducing primary energy consumption and energy poverty, promoting renewable energy and the union's energy security. however, it is essential that the union's energy strategy is also linked to industrial policy, transport policy, research and innovation policy and climate change policy. we call on the commission and the member states to develop the necessary financial and fiscal instruments for energy efficiency, in particular in the building sector, and to give priority to energy efficiency and smart energy infrastructure in the future multiannual financial framework. the union must attach greater importance to the eastern partnership and in particular to the black sea region, a region of particular geostrategic importance for the union's energy security and for the diversification of its energy supply routes. we invite the commission and the member states to continue the implementation of the european southern gas corridor project, in particular the nabucco project, which could significantly improve the security of energy supply.
energy is a major priority that cannot be delayed and it is important that the future action plan 2011-2020 makes a significant contribution to strengthening the common policy of the european union. we need close cooperation, particularly in the field of energy infrastructure, and adequate european funding. i believe that, in addition to public and community funding, in order to develop a strategic infrastructure at union level, which will drive the expansion and integration of all local, regional and european energy markets, we must pay greater attention to the private sector and investments from here. in my view, a good way is to promote public-private partnerships by providing the necessary political and administrative support, a certain level of funding and public guarantees. this will help us to secure the much-needed funding for the future of any energy policy.
in my view, improving the eu's renewable energy potential is one of the most important elements of the report. that's why i remind you that the dobrogea region in southeastern romania will become the largest wind farm in europe in a few years. construction of the 522 turbines will be completed in 2011. dobrogea will thus be able to supply 50% of national consumption. infrastructure is another key element for a functioning energy market. the eu must choose between those projects that prove to be efficient and economically viable. the agri interconnector, one of romania's first contributions to the development of energy infrastructure, is low cost and offers an alternative. diversification of sources of supply is also required in the oil sector. the p8 pipeline is a good example of this. romania and serbia have recently resumed feasibility studies for the construction of the first constanţa-pancevo tronson.
diversification of sources, a new energy infrastructure, increasing the share of renewable sources are important for the union's energy future. but at the same time we must not abandon the use of old energy sources, of course, improved by innovative technologies, according to the possibilities and needs of each member state. the most important thing for me, for the citizens i represent here, is that we must keep the price affordable for all consumers, and maintain and even create new jobs in this area. we must not have a situation where there is a surplus of energy on the european energy market because it cannot be bought because of high prices.
in writing. it is time to talk about a real european energy strategy. currently, there is a lack of implementation of eu energy legislation. through the provisions of the lisbon treaty, the european union has a firm legal framework for developing a functioning single market, guaranteeing security of supply, sustainability, network interconnection and solidarity. in this context, the new member states, which are much more vulnerable to external disruptions to energy supply, need the support of the european union to face these challenges. i also want to advocate that member states should be able to continue to subsidize coal mines at least until 2018. in a capitalist world, the term noncompetitive is synonymous with social plague. we have to take into account the human factor, think about the negative socioeconomic consequences of closing coal mines, which are a major source of jobs, before labelling a mine as noncompetitive.
in writing. the proposed energy strategy should promote a diversified combination of energy sources, namely renewable energy and nuclear energy, in the long term. however, this strategy cannot be viable unless the transmission network is strengthened to support market integration and the development of large-scale sustainable energy production. strengthening interconnections and links with third countries is also of paramount importance. there is an urgent need to develop and modernise distribution networks to accommodate the increasingly common cases of distributed production. market integration also requires, of course, better use of existing functional networks, based on cross-border harmonisation of market structures and the development of common european models for managing interconnections. and, last but not least, the establishment of an eu-wide 'smart grid' capable of managing, distributing and measuring, in real time, all the different production and consumption patterns to ensure the safe and efficient operation of the future electricity system is of the utmost importance.
in writing. i would like to welcome this report and in particular the references to the development of the potential in the field of bioenergy. the european potential in this area is under-exploited, and the situation in some member states is relevant, where there are huge areas of agricultural land that remain uncultivated every year. these abandoned lands could also be exploited for renewable energy. the example of romania, which is the one i am most familiar with, is instructive: some three million hectares remain unused, and the energy lost on this area is about 187 terawatts per hour. i think that this issue should be taken into account in the debate on the future of the common agricultural policy. the call to the commission to propose a policy framework and support the continued promotion of the use of sustainable second generation biofuels in europe is timely and i hope it will be taken up by the ec.
mr president, being an optimistic person, i consider that a step forward is now possible at cancún in the form of a balanced package that will allow countries to take faster, stronger actions across all areas of climate change. it is therefore of high importance to re-establish europe’s leading position within the international climate negotiations by introducing the climate diplomacy principle, and for the european union and its member states to define and implement a principle of climate justice, advocating therefore an equity clause in future international climate negotiations. i stress the importance of establishing the mechanism that regulates the funding of the financial aspects of climate change. new innovative sources of revenue, such as a financial transaction tax, green funds or private sources will be necessary to raise the money required in order to implement climate change adaptation and mitigation projects and to achieve green growth, which contributes to a good life for citizens, and fair growth. let us also not forget the gender dimension in climate change policies.
climate change is certainly the greatest challenge facing humanity today. unfortunately, expectations for the cancun conference are somewhat shy, due to the failure of copenhagen. at copenhagen, developed countries were expected to support developing countries' action plans to combat the effects of climate change through various means. however, the effects of the economic crisis, which are felt mainly at eu level, are forcing us to focus on other priorities. the importance of an international agreement to reduce carbon emissions is essential. at cancun, the eu must express a common position on the objectives it has to achieve and take into account that the success of the 2020 strategy is conditional on meeting the climate change objective. in this context, i would stress the role of partnerships aimed at developing the potential of sustainable energy at regional level and encouraging regions to use renewable energy.
the eu-africa summit in tripoli next week offers us the opportunity to reflect on the direction we want to take the partnership that links us to africa. in my view, the european commission's 11 november communication is welcome and i would particularly like to welcome the emphasis in this document on the need to complement development cooperation with concrete measures that could trigger sustainable and inclusive growth in this region. indeed, if we want the countries of the african continent to become true partners of the union and to assume their own destiny, there is no other way than to promote economic growth. i would like to stress three points which i believe are particularly important for our future relationship with africa: firstly, if we want the union's voice to be heard on the african continent, we must ensure that we have a partner who can hear our message. strengthening the african union in institutional and operational terms is a priority in this regard; secondly, i believe that the partnership on peace and security is the area of cooperation with africa which, in the commission's and the experts' analysis, is currently working best. but i think we can do more than that. we need, in my view, to strengthen the dimension of conflict prevention and policy-enhancement mechanisms because it is clear that both conflict and the fragility of some states in the region influence the achievement of the millennium development goals; finally, i would like to stress the essential nature of democratisation and respect for human rights. on these issues, the union and africa are often not in unison. the political dialogue must therefore be strengthened and the democratisation of the region must be a priority subject, to be tackled systematically in relation to africa.
the next africa-eu summit is a good opportunity to develop a realistic cooperation strategy. i believe that the proposals put forward by the european commission to strengthen relations between the two continents will facilitate the adoption of a concrete action plan at the summit. the decisions of the heads of state and government who will meet on this occasion will affect one and a half billion people in 80 countries. eradicating poverty, human rights and economic governance are common challenges that require a common approach. this is why it is important that the eu-africa partnership does not remain a donor-recipient partnership but becomes an equal partnership. as i have done in the debate on poverty reduction, i would like to stress the importance of achieving the millennium development goals. i believe that what is needed in particular is a good articulation of the four priority areas of action: financing, security, food, health and education.
madam president, i would first like to say that it is true that we could have discussed this much longer and come to a different text, but at the same time, this is about the time that is usually spent on emergency resolutions. we must therefore tell our moroccan partners that this is where the consensus of the various political groups actually ended. i believe that this is a step in that dialogue. i support the proposal made - i believe for the first time - by mr panzeri to continue the dialogue on certain subjects within the parliamentary committee which bind us to our moroccan colleagues. it is a recently created commission which could, why not, be supported by a group of friends of morocco because there are many of them here. i also look forward to the dialogue with the moroccan minister for foreign affairs. he's announced his presence next week before the foreign affairs committee. this is another opportunity to continue this dialogue.
on behalf of the s&d group. – mr president, my group’s philosophy on ukraine-european union relations today could be expressed by the following paraphrase of a famous speech: do not ask what ukraine could do for the european union, but ask what the european could do for ukraine, in order to have in ukraine a reliable pillar of the european union project. to this end, the european union approach on ukraine should be balanced, fair, fact-based and strategic. i believe that these criteria were met by the results of the recent summit, and i would like to thank the commissioner for expressing our approach in this way. ‘balanced’ means asking for improvements and at the same time offering assistance. ‘fair’ means avoiding taking sides in internal political controversies and using the same standards when evaluating the actions of parties wearing the colour we like and those wearing the colour we do not like. ‘fact-based’ means deciding to trust in evidence and not mere allegations, rumours and prejudices. ‘strategic’ means promoting policies which could allow ukraine to become organically integrated in the european union project and not policies which are meant to use ukraine in our confrontation with its neighbours. the compromise resolution we are supposed to be adopting following today’s debate is not a perfect but a decent example of such an approach. i have to deplore a few mistakes in the printing of the text. we must ask all political players in ukraine to avoid presenting this resolution as a victory of one against another. in fact, this resolution is meant to send to all ukrainian political forces the message that it is high time for them to unite behind a minimum national agenda and to deliver the long-awaited reforms, policies and political results which would assure a better life for the people and a better opportunity for the country, with the aim of european integration. there is no need for internationalisation of the internal controversies in ukraine. let us all accomplish our duties both here and there, and the future will reward all of us.
on behalf of the alde group. – mr president, it is interesting to see that ukraine is so often on our agenda. i hope this signifies progress in our relationship. i tend to believe that, with pragmatism and respect on both sides, understanding differences but finding common interests, we can build on common projects and achieve an honest partnership. i appreciate the recent statements of the ukrainian leadership, which i hope now are putting aside some fears that ukraine is moving away from a european future. on the other hand, any debate on ukraine has a tendency to become a war between the european political families of the opposition and government political parties of ukraine. i think this does not help, because it is not about who is better – government or opposition – or who is better supported by the europeans, it is about ukrainian citizens’ democratic future, and about ukrainians having a strong, democratic and prosperous country. the summit that took place this week achieved good results in fostering access to eu programmes and in the negotiations on the association agreement. i am particularly happy to see long-awaited progress towards a free trade area. of course, much remains to be done, in terms both of economic and institutional reforms, and the steps taken should be consolidated. no exemptions should be allowed to be made under the public procurement law, which was adopted earlier this year – not even for the european football championship. while a new tax code is a good step towards improving the fiscal environment, this should not become a burden, especially on smes, which play such an important role in any healthy economy. but let me be clear. this is not about us telling ukraine what to do, and it is not about what ukraine needs to do for us. it is primarily about what ukraine needs to do for itself, because both institutional and economic reforms are a prerequisite for a prosperous democratic future, and this is in the ukrainian citizens’ best interest.
an important aspect of today's debate was the criticism of the transparency and fairness of the local elections on 31 october. these have rightly concerned the government's increased influence over the media, the political role of the secret services and the adoption of the new electoral law, which disadvantages opposition parties. ukraine remains a key partner for the eu. in this regard, i welcome the eu's commitment to the process of reform and democratisation, reaffirmed at the summit on monday. the partnership with ukraine is also a natural one for romania, given its important role in the black sea region and the common challenges in the field of energy security. as already the case for the republic of moldova, it is envisaged to conclude a border traffic agreement with ukraine in line with eu rules. my country also expressed its support for the launch of the eu action plan on visa liberalisation for ukrainian citizens.
in writing. i would like to remind you that every country has the right to become a member of the eu, as provided for in article 49 of the union treaties. it is precisely because ukraine wants to become, one day, a member of the eu that i am deeply concerned about the way the recent local elections in this country have been conducted. the elections were neither free, fair nor democratic. the change in legislation shortly before the elections, the fact that the party of regions was 'pushed' to the top of the electoral lists in 85% of cases, the late registration of opposition parties, and other obstacles to fair representation of opposition parties call into question the character of the political system. as the us government has pointed out, the local elections were clearly below the level of the presidential elections in january. in order to demonstrate their commitment to democratic values, ukrainian leaders must adopt electoral legislation in line with international norms.
i would like to congratulate yannick jadot on the ambitious proposals put forward in this report and, above all, on his willingness to find a compromise with all the political groups which tabled amendments. we must recognize that there have been key moments when the european union has had the opportunity to speak with one voice. copenhagen was one of them, and the whole planet was waiting for the european union to take the lead in the fight against climate change and to lead reluctant states in the same direction. expectations, unfortunately, have not materialized, and disappointment has been directly proportional to it. the conclusion that can be drawn is that there is no consensus within the union. there are national governments that are not really ready to make strong commitments to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, and one sure explanation could be the economic and financial crisis that has slowed their momentum to engage in developing an ambitious climate policy. however, tackling climate change at both local and global levels must be a continuing concern for the world's states. it's not just the future of future generations that is at stake, but global justice. it is not right that developing countries should be left to pay the costs of global warming while the industrialized countries are pursuing a pragmatic and individualistic approach. what is needed is real north-south solidarity. that's why i'm looking at the cancun summit as an opportunity to go beyond an operational agreement. cancun must be a legally binding global operational agreement to help keep global warming below 2 degrees celsius. a more defined verification procedure than that established in copenhagen is also required. nor can the european union's singular effort to combat climate change guarantee the success of an agreement for the period after 2012. we need to convince other parties to make more ambitious commitments to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. last but not least, i want to focus on the relationship between international trade and climate change. trade is an important tool in the transfer of technology to developing countries. this requires the removal of barriers to green trade. this could take the form of eliminating, at least at the wto level, tariffs on green products. we must also be aware of the global disruption that the current trading system is producing in transport-based labour and production. that is why i end by advocating the encouragement of local production in the european union.
on behalf of the epp group. i wish to speak as the epp group's alternative rapporteur for the european ombudsman's special report. i would first like to stress that the achievement of consensus among all the political groups facilitated the preparation of the report. i would point out that there was no amendment tabled and i would also like to congratulate mrs paliadeli on this result. it is worrying that the commission's non-cooperative practices towards the ombudsman can generate a pronounced lack of trust of citizens in the european institutions. the lack of good cooperation jeopardises the ombudsman's and the european parliament's ability to supervise the commission effectively. i also recall the principle of sincere cooperation enshrined in the treaty on the functioning of the european union. it involves strengthening good faith relations between the eu institutions. unfortunately, the ombudsman very often encounters delays in the commission's deadlines for public access to documents. another concern is that the ombudsman had to draw up a special report as a last resort to persuade the commission to be more cooperative. such cases should not be encountered in the future. in this regard, i would like to ask the european commission to make further efforts to cooperate more effectively with the ombudsman. it should not be overlooked that, if the commission does not make such a commitment, parliament will be able to apply sanctions. the situation described in the report creates a systemic problem. it deprives citizens of one of the key benefits they expect to derive from the fundamental right to complain.
the european ombudsman is the democratic conscience of the european union. it contributes year by year to strengthening the trust of citizens with complaints in the institutions. it is a particular pleasure to note that, with the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, it is now also monitoring compliance with the charter of fundamental rights, in particular by ensuring that the right to good administration is respected. i find the european network of ombudsmen extremely useful, as the level of awareness among citizens and the quality of public services in some member states, including romania, where i come from, are below the european average. this is also reflected in the ombudsman's report on its activities. i therefore ask the ombudsman to try in future to collect complaints to national ombudsmen concerning the application of european law by member states, since citizens are most often brought into contact with european law through their own authorities.
in writing. the application of european law is vital if eu citizens are to enjoy the full benefits of the internal market, as even the best-performing legislation becomes useless if it is not applied. as regards internal market legislation, there is a lot of progress to be made, particularly with regard to the services directive or the directive on the recognition of professional qualifications. it is true that this legislation is technical in nature, which complicates the implementation process. for this reason, cooperation between the european institutions and national administrations is essential. the internal market information system, used for services, has proved particularly useful and i believe we could benefit from extending it to other sectors. i would stress, however, the need for member states to take transposition seriously and to avoid as far as possible the delays that cause the internal market to operate at suboptimal parameters. finally, i stress the need for citizens to be able to solve their problems with the application of european law quickly and at minimum cost. this requires the replenishment of solvit resources as well as the intensive promotion of this informal problem-solving tool. last but not least, priority should be given to the development of alternative dispute resolution.
first of all, i too would like to welcome the european commission's proposals for the revision of the rules on horizontal cooperation in the field of competition. they aim to clarify the conditions for obtaining exemptions, readjust restrictions and provide information on intellectual property rights. the economic and financial crisis has highlighted the need for closer cooperation on these plans and for common economic regulation at global level. we also need to assess the possibility of more frequent international exchange of information in the field of competition and the possibility of global governance in this area. making cooperation agreements between competitors more efficient promotes innovation and contributes to the competitiveness of european companies. i therefore consider that there is also a need to examine the possibilities of introducing block exemption regulations for other types of horizontal agreements at times.
in writing. − the european parliament must not give in to pressure from the european commission to accept the 2011 budget. it would mean that the changes to the treaty on which the union is founded would be violated by the most democratic forum of the european community, the only one directly elected. the reactions of the european commission leaders suggest that the eu executive is living with the impression that parliament does not agree with the budget, which is designed to show who really holds power. but it is clear that parliament, which has spoken out in its entirety against the 2011 budget from the commission, has more important things to do than to fight unnecessary power struggles. the reality is that the budget does not take account of the union's new competences and does not provide funding for the eu 2020 strategy, which is unanimously agreed. we cannot be inconsistent with our own decisions, we cannot think and approve generous strategies without also securing the financial side of their implementation. it is parliament's right to set the course for the union next year, as given by the treaty of lisbon. the unity with which all the parliamentary groups in the european legislature have acted only demonstrates that the budget must be reconsidered on a much more flexible basis.
in writing. − through its policies, and in particular its trade policy, the union must defend its trade interests, respecting its own rules and values and ensuring that others respect them. this perspective must help the various european institutions to launch and lead a new trade policy, an ambitious policy based on firmness and dialogue. it should be borne in mind that in europe, european industrial and commercial companies are subject to strict compliance with social and environmental standards. if the european union complies with binding standards, it must be able to demand the same from its trading partners, in particular emerging countries, and to promote quality and sustainability requirements, especially for food products entering its territory, in order to maintain fair and equitable trade. in this respect, the high standards of the european single market in health, safety, environment, worker and consumer protection constitute a specific european model, which should serve as a source of inspiration at international level and in multilateral contexts and should be reflected in the ongoing negotiations on bilateral trade agreements.

in writing. − the main message we wanted to convey through this report is the need to maintain an independent public service broadcasting. i insisted on the additions to the draft report on board appointments, which must be made on the basis of competence alone and not on political partisanship. we also tried to make clear our desire to have attractive, high-quality content for public broadcasters, but also to incorporate new platforms, taking into account new technologies. one point i stressed was the investment in public broadcasting services, without which high standards of operation are impossible.
in writing. − unfortunately, declarative efforts, national and international resolutions and plans to improve the protection of women in theatres of conflict have not resulted in the eradication of this barbaric weapon frequently used in modern warfare: sexual violence. on the contrary, impunity provides the conditions for proliferation in this direction, which is completely contrary to our values. i am among those who have repeatedly denounced the mass rapes in congo, liberia and other conflict zones, especially in africa. the worst problem is that there have been cases where atrocities have been committed within walking distance of un bases. thousands of women who fall victim to sexual abuse and violence are also condemned to later endure the social stigma and the burden of terrible diseases such as hiv infection. the european union must step up its action to combat these grave human rights violations so that un resolutions do not remain a dead letter. the international day for the elimination of violence against women, which we celebrate on 25 november, should also remind us that women are victims of domestic violence, which is alarmingly common, of marital rape, sexual harassment and human trafficking.
in writing. − security council resolution 1325, adopted on 31 october 2000, recognises that women have historically been excluded from the peace and stabilisation process of a nation, calling for women's equal participation at all levels from conflict prevention to post-conflict reconstruction, peacekeeping and security. the 10th anniversary of the adoption of the resolution should mark the beginning of a new agenda, which is being implemented and which cannot be implemented without political support at the highest level and without the necessary resources. the eu must actively promote the employment of as many women as possible in senior management positions in order to coordinate and ensure the coherence of european policies and actions and to monitor the implementation of commitments. the ec must appoint at least five women to senior posts in the european external action service and ensure gender balance in the experts it employs. in addition, there is a need for an organisational unit within the eeas responsible for gender issues and in each geographical department and eu delegation at least one full-time position dedicated to the gender dimension with responsibilities for women, peace and security.

in writing. − the new energy strategy for europe aims to implement the lisbon treaty on a single energy market, security of supply, energy efficiency, reducing import dependence and increasing domestic energy production. i support this resolution because the european union needs the swift implementation of energy legislation and overall energy strategies. we need a long-term vision of energy policy to ensure the proper functioning of this market, supporting modern integrated networks, improving the exploitation of the union's energy efficiency potential, promoting research and development and innovation in the field and placing the benefits for consumers at the heart of european energy policy. i therefore voted in favour of this report, which is a first step towards a comprehensive community energy policy in the context of the eu 2020 strategy.
in writing. − the eu's energy security policy should enable it to anticipate, not just react to, gas crises such as the one in 2009. this must be done in parallel with the achievement of the stated targets of a 20% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions and a 20% reduction in consumption by 2020. the task is not easy, especially since the financial effort for environmental objectives alone will amount to €58 billion. add to this the financial effort to reduce the eu's growing dependence on external energy resources. internal and external aspects must be combined to make the eu energy-vulnerable and its policies must be adapted accordingly. all measures to ensure the proper functioning of the internal energy market should be accompanied by dynamic diplomacy aimed at strengthening cooperation with the main producing, transit and consuming countries. national plans with preventive and emergency measures are urgently needed and their coordination at community level would ensure their effectiveness.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the new energy strategy for europe 2011-2020. under this resolution, the main objectives are to move to a low-carbon energy system and to guarantee the security of energy supply for all member states. these two objectives must ensure both the eu's competitiveness and the distribution of energy at affordable prices, with secure supplies. i believe that extending the rules of the eu's internal energy market to neighbouring countries and efforts to diversify energy sources and transport routes for energy imports are essential to guarantee energy security.
in writing. − the european union has set itself a series of very ambitious targets for the next decade, one of which is to increase energy efficiency by 2020. it is an objective that will allow for increased investment in the field and, by implication, create new jobs in both rural and urban areas. in this context, i believe that it is useful to provide financial incentives for such projects, but also to launch campaigns to inform citizens about energy efficiency and the use of resources that consumer products and products with an energy impact can offer.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution of 25 november 2010 on the un climate change conference in cancun to meet the global target of limiting the increase in annual average surface temperature to 2°c (the '2°c target'). the consequences of not meeting the 2°c target can be particularly serious. up to 40% of species will disappear, millions of people will be displaced by rising sea levels and increased frequency of extreme weather events, crop yields will decline, food prices will rise, and global economic output will decline by at least 3%. the scientific case for climate change and its effects is more than clear, so it is crucial to create a legislative framework to ensure that these measures are implemented.
in writing. − i believe that the european union and the member states must define and implement the principle of climate equity and therefore the introduction of an equity clause in future international climate negotiations. i think the biggest injustice would be if the world were unable to limit climate change, because especially the poor people in poor countries would suffer.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution with the conviction that we will achieve a great result in cancun this year. learning from the positive outcome of nagoya in october 2010 and the negative experience of copenhagen in 2009, i believe that the eu will speak with one voice and, on the basis of the mandate, the eu and the member states must continue to play a constructive role at international level in order to achieve a legally binding post-kyoto agreement. for its proper implementation and for more transparency, ngos and civil society must be fully involved. i therefore welcome the signing of the 5,000 civil society representatives to take part in the work of cop 16.
in writing. − trade in goods and services generates around 20% of global greenhouse gas emissions. support the continuation of trade policies aimed at differentiating products and services according to their climate impact. i voted in favour of this resolution because it identifies further steps that will allow the european union to continue on this path, reinforce the positive interaction between trade and climate protection, the instruments that ensure trade-climate coherence and encourage fair prices in international trade while avoiding carbon emissions. i want to stress that the european union cannot take a leading role in the fight against climate change unless it strengthens the competitiveness of its economy through energy saving and the development of renewable energy sources. these are two sectors with high potential for industrial development, innovation, spatial planning, job creation and can improve european energy security.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that the rapporteur's text is moving towards bold commitments by the european union to combat climate change. the resolution proposes to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by up to 30% at eu level. i support this ambitious proposal and at the same time believe that this eu effort must be matched internationally by the efforts of the major industrialised countries. so we have to find a way to train the more reluctant international state actors to follow suit. in my capacity as virtual rapporteur for the s&d political group, i also stressed, by submitting amendments to the original text, the need to create a world environment organisation and to introduce environmental criteria into the gsp reform.
in writing. − to play a leading role in the fight against climate change, the european union needs to strengthen the competitiveness of its economy through energy saving and the use of renewable energy sources, two sectors that can improve its energy security and have high potential in terms of industrial development, innovation, spatial planning and job creation. at the same time, the eu needs to change its trade policies, whether bilateral, regional or multilateral. this is because trade in goods and services is responsible for about 20% of global greenhouse gas emissions. this is a difficult project. but the eu has already taken the first steps in the right direction with regard to illegal imports of wood, biofuels, and aviation emissions. the report, which is the result of numerous discussions with businesses, associations, trade union representatives and the commission, aims to identify further steps that would allow the eu to continue in this direction.
in writing. − the eu has a key role to play in efforts to create new governance and, to this end, it must promote policy coherence in international institutions. it is becoming clear that the eu needs to reflect on the trade policy it wishes to adopt as part of its review of its trade strategy. if it wants to send a clear message against protectionism, it must ensure the fairness of international trade. the union must defend its commercial interests by respecting its own rules and values and ensuring that others respect them. it should be borne in mind that in europe companies are subject to strict social and environmental standards. the eu must be able to demand the same from its trading partners, especially emerging countries, and promote quality and sustainability requirements, especially for food products entering its territory, in order to maintain fair and equitable trade. the union must engage in dialogue with its partners and find a common space for transmitting its values. through this effort to be transparent and to engage in dialogue on the new powers conferred on it, the european parliament plays a key role, with the duty to give the negotiations a political and moral mandate.
in writing. − the economic and social effects of trade liberalisation vary from country to country and need to be controlled in most cases. the common commercial policy must be in line with the general objectives of the european union and must not serve only the short-term interests of some important economic operators. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that integrating the principles of corporate social responsibility into international trade rules will give the union the possibility to put certain pressure on companies and on the states that are signatories to trade agreements with the european union to ensure that labour standards are respected. in doing so, we will ensure that the foreign policies we put in place effectively contribute to sustainable social and economic development and that businesses abide by our internationally agreed norms and values.
member of the commission. − madam president, the european commission shares the deep concerns of this parliament – so explicitly and clearly expressed by the honourable members – as regards the human rights situation in iraq. the foreign affairs council on monday expressed its outright condemnation of the recent terrorist attacks, notably those which targeted places where civilians congregate, including christian and muslim places of worship. the council, adopting conclusions put forward by high representative / vice-president ashton, also stressed that the new government in iraq will need to dedicate itself to the pursuit of national reconciliation. this means it should represent the interests and needs of all iraqis, regardless of creed and ethnicity. the protection and promotion of human rights, including those of persons belonging to minorities, must be a top priority. in its dialogue with iraq, the european union frequently voices its human rights concerns, including not only the freedom of religion or belief but also on the death penalty. ten days ago the eu made an urgent and direct call on the authorities in reaction to the decision by the iraqi high tribunal to sentence to death five representatives of the former regime, including tariq aziz. the eu recalled its firm opposition to the use of capital punishment under all circumstances, seeking a global moratorium on the death penalty as a first step. human rights have a prominent place in the partnership and cooperation agreement which we hope to sign with iraq soon. that is the direct answer to mrs de lange. since 2003, an important part of eu cooperation with iraq has focused on strengthening the rule of law and promoting human rights and fundamental freedoms, for example, through eujust lex and community assistance. substantial funds have also been dedicated to providing protection and relief to the most vulnerable iraqis. many of them are, for obvious reasons, internally displaced and now live in areas with dense minoritiy group populations. our work has ranged from promoting awareness and enforcement of human rights among vulnerable groups to the rehabilitation of schools in areas already mentioned in the discussions, such as nineveh, which has a large christian population. humanitarian assistance also continues to reach the most vulnerable inside and outside iraq. eu aid cannot directly target specific ethnic or religious communities, but it should and it can, help the most vulnerable iraqis, wherever they live. we do not underestimate the challenges facing the iraqi government. it is no easy task to root out the extremists who seek to create sectarian tensions through acts of barbarity. security, development and the preservation of human rights are closely linked. the eu remains committed to helping iraq as best as it can to secure progress on all three issues. the iraqi people deserve no less.
in writing. – i join my colleagues in this parliament in the condemnation of the ongoing murders, executions and human rights violations occurring in iraq. the situation for iraq’s christian minority is one of life and death: nearly 50 iraqi christians were killed in a ruthless massacre in our lady of salvation church on 31 october 2010. human rights watch estimates that, since 2003, almost half of the christian population of iraq, hundreds of thousands of people, have had to flee the country. we must continue to fight for them to stay alive and be free. we must stand for minority rights and continue to oppose murder, violence, segregation, and any discrimination based on ethnicity or religious belief. i call on the commission and the council to raise the issue of christians’ safety in iraq as a matter of urgency, as the eu continues to move toward closer cooperation with the iraqi government.

on behalf of the epp group. first of all, i would like to welcome the release of aung san suu kyi, the leader of the opposition in burma, after many years of house arrest. i also want to express the hope that this release will be followed by the release of the more than 2 000 political prisoners, because, as mr posselt said, otherwise we will understand that this is just a cosmetic gesture. i also have to tell you that i want to support aung san suu kyi in rebuilding her party, the national league for democracy, which was abused and disbanded in may. of course, there is a huge amount of work to be done, and that is why i believe that international pressure must continue because the military junta has not engaged in a process of democratization, but the exact opposite of such a process, the elections held in november being neither fair nor free. so i think we should not lose sight of the importance of this space.
as early as february 2010, the european parliament called for the release of aung san suu kyi, who has been in detention since 1990. the fact that the burmese authorities have decided to release her a few months after this imperative request by meps is a first step in the right direction. however, we cannot regard this particular situation as a human rights restoration in burma, given that there are still many pro-democracy activists who remain in captivity. the treaty of lisbon states that the european union aims to promote peace, its values and the well-being of its peoples. by common values we mean respect for human dignity, freedom, democracy and human rights. the european union has a duty to do more than promote these values within itself, and i therefore call for a message of solidarity to be sent to the burmese people, who are suffering from repression by the government and who are fighting a daily battle for respect for fundamental rights.
mr. president, i have to go. i am pleased that the romanian winner of the european commission's 2010 european journalist of the year competition has been selected from the ranks of the hungarian national community in romania. the winner of the prize was recognised by the commission for a report written in hungarian, her mother tongue. hungarian is not an official language in romania. for the one and a half million hungarian community, it is the language in which they learn about the world around them. i am grateful to the commission for its understanding that it is not possible to exclude the possibility of competing publications written in a language other than the official language of the state concerned. however, i feel that there is a lack of awareness because national communities that do not have an official language of the eu - catalans, basques, corsicans and many others - have not been given the opportunity to inform their community in their mother tongue and to participate in the competition. it is time for them to take the european reality, multilingualism and the coexistence of cultures into account in all their decisions.
the european commission published a report last week on the implementation of the 2007 strategy on nutrition and obesity. this report highlighted some concrete actions in the fight against unhealthy eating and obesity in the european union, but also the fact that many of the objectives set out in the strategy were not achieved. the strategy included commitments to expand and support nutrition education among children, but little has been done at european level to meet these commitments. for example, the european 'fruit in schools' programme contains educational elements but is only addressed to a limited number of children and, although its positive impact is nonetheless, we find it rather limited. another major problem is the advertising of food products to children. in 2007, the commission drew up codes of conduct to regulate the marketing of baby food, but unfortunately, today in some member states there is still direct advertising of unhealthy foods to children, as well as very different interpretations of the guidelines on the code of conduct.
during romania's pre-accession to the european union, the european commission closely monitored the situation of international adoptions and recommended that they be stopped, following reports of abuses in adoption practices; however, in 2009, in the context of the european commission and council of europe conference on the challenges of adoption procedures in europe, i wrote a letter to mr jacques barrot, in which i wanted to draw attention to the consequences of the reopening of the market for international adoptions and called for consistency on the part of the european commission. following an investigation by a romanian newspaper, we are faced with the hypothesis of an abuse of power by the european commission, manifested by the imposition of the conclusion of the official report of the conference, which recommends the establishment of a european agency for adoption. i believe that the image of the european union suffers from the association of the guardian of the european treaty with the falsification of an official act. i therefore expect a clear, reasoned reply from the european commission to remove this question mark on its verticality.
fundamental rights are the basic principles of the european union. ensuring that they are respected is the primary duty of all the european institutions. in romania, a member state of the european union, we are witnessing serious violations of fundamental rights. the current government of romania, after having brought the country to economic and social bankruptcy, is now implementing aberrant measures that seriously violate the fundamental rights recognized in the european union - the right to pension, trade union rights, the right to wages, the rights of young mothers - and, moreover, i would like to draw attention to the fact that romania is also preparing to amend the law on the protection and promotion of the rights of persons with disabilities. the adoption of the draft law proposed by the romanian government, instead of strengthening the protection of persons with disabilities and promoting their social inclusion, will only make their lives more difficult, making them dependent on the state. the interests and dignity of persons with disabilities will be profoundly violated.
the accession of bulgaria and romania to the schengen area is very important for the stability of the european union on its eastern border. secondly, and perhaps just as importantly, it is a natural step, as both countries were granted full membership of the european union in 2007. however, this decision must be a technical one, not a sentimental or passionate one. there are some parties in the european union that are in government that think they can win some electoral points by opposing this decision and blaming romania and bulgaria for the fact that there are problems with roma integration at the european level. on the other hand, if the report is finalised in a favourable way and the checks carried out these days in the two member states show that the two countries are ready to join the schengen area, i say that it is very important that we continue to support them, especially as we gave a favourable opinion not long ago.
the latest amendments to the romanian labour code will further worsen the situation of employees, already badly affected by the recession. the notice period and the probationary period for the terminating employee will be extended, and the employment contract may be terminated without notice during or at the end of this period, in which more than three persons may be successively employed for the same post. the most abusive measure, however, in flagrant contradiction to basic human rights, is the legal suspension of the individual employment contract for the period of participation in the strike. i just want to protest against this attempt to turn employees into slaves of the bosses and i would like to ask the political forces and european institutions to intervene to stop the degradation of the status of employees in romania.
on behalf of the ppe group. – mr president, the epp group is in favour of the two proposals for eu-georgia agreements: the readmission agreement and the visa facilitation agreement. i would like to refer to the last one, the visa facilitation agreement. it simplifies the visa application for georgians. member states will apply uniform and simplified procedures. a visa will cost eur 35, less than at present, and will allow a stay of up to 90 days every six months. visa applications will be processed in 10 days, or in three days for some categories, or less in cases of emergencies. no visas will be required on diplomatic passports. free movement is one road to learning democracy and seeing it at work. the people-to-people direct contact means sharing values and realities. it creates trust. this is why i hope that more eu citizens will travel to georgia and more georgians will travel to the european union.
thank you, commissioner, for the information you have given us on visa facilitation arrangements, particularly with regard to georgia, the republic of moldova and the countries of the former yugoslavia. moreover, our debate coincides with the abolition of visas for citizens of bosnia, herzegovina and albania, with the possibility of swiftly suspending the agreement in the event of problems such as the avalanche of asylum applications. i think any attempt to turn back the clock on the european union's policy towards the western balkans would be a mistake. removing barriers to free movement can play an important role in closing the wounds of the past. i also believe that closer cooperation between the european union and these countries is needed to discourage the influx of asylum seekers, to strengthen border controls, to provide the local population with the right information, and to combat organised criminal networks involved in the trafficking of human beings and the export of crime and prostitution. all of these can help to reduce this phenomenon.
a fundamental condition for the complete abolition of visas between the russian federation and the european union is the fulfilment of the commitments undertaken under the 2007 agreement. the russian authorities have repeatedly called for lifting the requirement for short-stay visas, but the eu has preferred a gradual approach, translated into a list of common steps. i consider it important that all technical conditions are met before implementing a liberalisation decision - for example, improving standards in border management, document security or the fight against corruption. it is also necessary for russia to confirm by deeds its intention to achieve tangible results in the settlement of frozen conflicts in the region. it has a substantial responsibility in this regard. resolving the conflict in transnistria is a political priority for my country. we support the continuation of formal talks within the 5+2 negotiations with a view to identifying a lasting solution. it shall fully respect international law and the sovereignty of the republic of moldova. i would also like to refer to the case of the eastern partnership countries, including georgia and the republic of moldova. they have long been waiting for visa liberalisation and have implemented numerous reforms in this regard and i would point out that the republic of moldova is the champion in this area within the eastern partnership. i would stress that russia's achievement of a relaxed visa regime before the countries in its immediate neighbourhood would be a disincentive for the latter. it would thus prove that the status of eastern partnership countries matters very little when strategic concessions from the union are at stake.
in writing. i believe that serbia has so far made great efforts to meet eu expectations and continue on the path towards integration. during 2009 and 2010, it obtained: visa liberalisation, the launch of the ratification process of the stabilisation and association agreement, and the european commission's acceptance of the preparation of the opinion on serbia's eu accession application. it is regrettable, however, that the serbian authorities have not adequately publicized and explained what constitutes the granting of the visa-free travel regime introduced in 2009 so that citizens do not abuse this regime. i hope that this worrying increase in asylum applications to the eu from serbian citizens will not be to the detriment of serbia's integration process. i am confident that the serbian authorities will react without delay and would like to remind that the path to accession depends on serbia's individual efforts to comply with the copenhagen criteria and the stabilisation and association agreement.
in writing. the western balkan countries have seen such positive developments in recent years that it seems that the region was a war zone in europe a decade and a half ago. the eu's exemplary support for the democratization process in the western balkans and its open accession perspective for the region's states have undoubtedly contributed to these developments. the decision to liberalize visas a year ago brought the european practice of free movement to macedonia, montenegro and serbia, a clear sign of european concern. there is no doubt that in some member states immigration is again emerging as a serious domestic policy issue and is becoming more pronounced as a consequence of the economic crisis, but i believe that european solidarity must prevail despite the crisis if we are to avoid a resurgence of nationalism and protectionism. the western balkans are not yet part of the eu, but stability in south-eastern europe can only be achieved through the enlargement of the union to the balkans. the union should strictly monitor compliance with technical requirements for border protection, but at the same time provide support to make the citizens of the western balkan states feel that there is a real possibility of improving their lot and that eu accession is within their reach. we need to support the region with effective information, more solidarity and additional financial means on the path of social and economic development so that citizens can find their own prosperity in their own country.
we all know that economic immigration is a real phenomenon in the member states of the european union. however, the presence of third-country workers must be assessed from at least two points of view. the issue is primarily seen as an economic necessity, as demographic and labour market trends show that european societies need the work of immigrants. we are interested in immigration taking place legally and in regulated circumstances, in the possibility for member states to control the process and in immigrants feeling secure in their rights, that is, not having to evade legal procedures. i consider very important the part of the directive that concerns common rights, i.e. the same rights for immigrants and workers who are nationals of a member state. i would also like to draw attention to the second cultural aspect of this question. in many member states, the presence of immigrants with different cultural customs and traditions is a source of tension. i am convinced that the guarantee of equal rights cannot be erased by the prohibition of discrimination in the labour market. in my opinion, the question requires a more nuanced approach. legally immigrant workers bring not only their labour to europe, they want not only to work here, but to study, to start a family, to raise children, to live a full life. so if europe decides that economic immigration is the solution to the imbalances caused by demographics, it cannot ignore the cultural dimension of the issue. the success of multiculturalism presupposes tolerance, mutual respect and solidarity.
the single permit will facilitate administrative procedures, improve the control and management of economic migration and the exchange of data on labour market demand. the present legislative proposal, however, only half solves the problem, because it deals with the rights of persons who have already been admitted to the territory of the union and to the labour market of a member state. two other aspects are not covered: the criteria for granting the right to work and the exclusion of seasonal workers and persons transferred within their undertaking. i would also like to remind you that we are regulating the rights of workers from third countries, but we do not yet have a fully open labour market for all european citizens.
first of all, i would like to congratulate my colleague claude moraes on his report and thank him for the excellent work he is doing as coordinator of the libe committee. i think it is very good that this new directive finally fills a legal vacuum in the area of residence rights for beneficiaries of international protection within the european union. these persons established in one of the member states are currently in a precarious legal situation, as they cannot, under the current conditions, obtain a long-term residence permit in the same way as other third-country nationals. the granting of long-term residence to them must be made on a non-discriminatory basis and be conditional only on prior legal residence, as is the case for other third-country nationals. i believe that it would have been better to take into account in this calculation the entire period of legal residence in the territory of the union from the moment of lodging the application for international protection. at the same time, i believe that account must be taken of the fact that these persons remain permanently vulnerable outside the territory of the union, so that any withdrawal of international protection or of the right of residence must be made in strict compliance with fundamental rights and the principle of non-refoulement. this directive provides the necessary complementary information on the procedures applicable in cases of expulsion or withdrawal of international protection. i think we should vote in favour of the report by mr claude moraes as part of the overall package of regulations on asylum and migration in the european union.
the reporter. − this report aims to answer the question in the title, namely whether achieving economic, social and territorial cohesion is a sine qua non of global competitiveness in the european union, focusing in particular on the role played by cohesion policy in this regard. it is alarming that the disparities between the 271 regions of the union are so great. if the most developed region has a gdp per capita of 334% of the eu27 average, the poorest region has only 26%, 13 times less. another negative element is the european union's economic growth rate, which is slower than that of our international competitors. it is therefore necessary, as the eu 2020 strategy also states, to develop strategic areas and look beyond the european union to become stronger. europe faces a difficult task because, alongside the effects of the current crisis, it will also have to face other major challenges, such as adaptation to globalisation, demographic change, climate change and energy security issues. the role of cohesion policy in the eu 2020 strategy is unquestionable. i believe that the priorities of this policy should be aligned with the objectives of the future strategy, but that it should remain an independent policy. the objectives of the strategy can be more easily achieved by increasing synergies between the r & d and innovation programmes on the one hand and the cohesion programmes on the other. we need to support large, high-impact projects at european level that will generate growth, create jobs and ensure sustainable development of regions. economic competitiveness and job creation should not be overlooked. they should have increased access to community financing, financial engineering instruments and other sources of credit. maximising their flexibility, to maintain gross domestic product as the main criterion for determining the eligibility of regions under cohesion policy and the need for a concrete proposal from the commission on the use of public-private partnership. to make the european union more globally competitive, i believe that part of the funds allocated through cohesion policy must be used to achieve and maintain on behalf of the alde group. – mr president, tomorrow afternoon we will be able to share our thoughts on the human rights situation in the world, but this morning we are focusing on the state of play as regards these rights in the european union. discussing the european union first and the rest of the world afterwards is the right order, in my view because, before criticising others, we should put our own house in order. if we really want to be taken seriously we must not turn a blind eye to human rights violations on our own soil. this resolution, for which i want to congratulate our rapporteur, ms gál, focuses on the way forward for eu policy in the field of human rights protection and advancement after the entry into force of the lisbon treaty. it deals not only with who bears responsibility for what, but also focuses on the topics that should be at the centre of our concern in the future. i would just like to emphasise two aspects. i was happy with the support given in the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs to the idea of a kind of freezing mechanism, by which national contested policies or decisions can be frozen by the commission until it has taken a formal decision as to whether to start the infringement procedure. i believe such a mechanism will bring added value in creating a more credible fundamental rights policy within the european union. i hope, therefore, that the entire house will lend its support to this mechanism when we vote tomorrow. the other aspect relates to the right and the duty of this parliament continually to analyse the human rights situation in the member states and to be critical in expressing its views, including naming and shaming when necessary.
first of all, congratulations to mrs. kinga gál on her report. we now have a community of values and principles, reflected in a complex system of human rights protection, which includes the charter of fundamental rights, the most modern codification of fundamental rights at the regional level. member states must comply with the provisions of the charter when applying union law. the provisions of the charter are directly applicable to national courts, which thus also acquire a great deal of responsibility. secondly, we have the european convention and the case law of the strasbourg court. they are a guarantee of individual rights in the member states, and the union's accession to the convention will ensure the application of the european convention on human rights in relation to and in relation to the actions of the union institution or of a member state applying union law. of course, we must look at the reform of the court in strasbourg and its effects on the shortening of procedures. at national level, the third level, member states have the obligation and the opportunity to directly implement the provisions guaranteeing fundamental rights, to apply them at home, through the decisions of their own institutions. so legal and institutional mechanisms are in place. the key word is swift and effective implementation for the victim. and another key word is coordinating the institutions that decide violations and grant reparations.
in writing. the european union, as a community of states that ensure a high level of protection of human rights, always raises its voice forcefully against serious violations in other parts of the world. the european parliament is normally exemplary in its condemnation of practices that flout the universal principles of human rights, wherever they occur in the world. but it is less common to respond decisively to violations of human rights in the union, even though this is the most effective message to be sent to states that do not respect human rights around the world. the greatest impact of joint action by the union would be achieved if we did not express our dissatisfaction with the application of human rights and fundamental freedoms with the same harshness and tolerance for contradiction in our own territory. very rarely do we take account of the principles that are an integral part of the european idea and that have been legally binding for a year now through the charter of fundamental rights. if this happens, we will appear weak and helpless in the absence of appropriate sanctions. this inevitably affects the strength and credibility of our judgments vis-à-vis third countries and our foreign policy efforts to promote human rights and democracy, i think that europe cannot afford to give up these things in the future either.

payments on credit rating agencies that fail to comply with the regulation. of course, this regulation also guarantees the rights of defence of credit rating agencies, including the right to be heard, and provisions of european union law, including the principle of proportionality. the new cra regulation will also ensure a single point of contact for all cras, a harmonised regulatory framework in the european union, with equal treatment, a more consistent application of the rules for agencies across the european union. so i think that's a huge gain in efficiency, transparency and security in the overall architecture that we build week after week for smart oversight and effective regulation. i would perhaps like, mr president, to continue mr chastel's remarks without taking up too much of his time, and to talk about the next step, since i myself have said that we must go further in order to regulate credit rating agencies properly, while noting that it is not the agencies that are creating the problem and the turbulence in the financial markets. it is not the thermometer that causes the fever, but the thermometer must function properly, which was not the case in the past, and which we are curing, if i may say so, by means of these successive regulations. the commission already has the next step in mind, a public consultation was launched on 5 november 2010 to broaden this debate, to gather the views of all the parties concerned and as you know, in all these regulations, these debates are not artificial. i would very much like to hear, ladies and gentlemen, all the contributions, criticisms and ideas that have been put forward in these consultations. we are already thinking about, first, the consequences of the issuer-pays model among rating agencies, second, the reliance of banks and other institutional investors on credit ratings, third, the rating of sovereign debt - not an easy issue - fourth, the increase in transparency to better manage conflicts of interest and finally, to create more competition, more diversity in this market of rating agencies, which is currently concentrated in too few hands. this consultation is open until next january and, on the basis of all the replies we receive and wolf klinz's own initiative report, we will take a decision in the course of 2011, but not too late, on the measures we want to implement to complete, in a third stage, these two regulations which are now virtually implemented in relation to the rating agencies.
rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on legal affairs. − mr president, as a vice-chair of the committee on legal affairs, i would like to present some important aspects that were the subject of the debates and amendments tabled in this committee. firstly, at the present time payment for the structured instruments evaluated by the agencies is made by the issuing company. there can be conflicts of interest because the rated companies are interested in having a good rating. alternatively, it might be the users of ratings who pay. the users’ interests are more diverse and therefore there is not a single interest that can lead to a conflict of interest. there are users who prefer a good rating, for instance when they want to sell shares, and those who prefer a bad rating, for instance when they want to buy shares. secondly, the regime for the rating agencies could profit from the rules that have been established for the auditors. the rating agencies and auditors have a lot of responsibility for the good reputation of companies and the proper functioning of the market. auditors, however, seem to be subject to far stricter rules than the rating agencies. thirdly, the european securities and markets authority, esma, should have supervisory competence over the credit rating agencies in order to verify possible material discrepancies between the ratings given by different agencies for the same structured financial instrument. esma should also have greater power of enforcement. fourthly, the directive introduces a new principle, taken from the latest us legislation. when an agency other than the one contracted to make the valuation can do its valuation for the same instrument, it is subject to the contracted valuation. for this, the first agency must disclose certain information regarding the valuated instrument. in such a way, two beneficial effects are obtained – firstly, there is a second opinion and, secondly, the liability that falls on the contracted agency is reduced. finally, i want to underline the fact that the provisions of this directive, which represents a new regulatory frame, should only apply to the structured financial instruments, credit rating agencies themselves being an important part of structured finance. the remainder of the financial instruments, 150-year-old common shares or plain bonds which do not pose a systemic risk should not be part of this directive if you want to be tight but not to over-regulate, if you want to be competitive but not expensive in administrative costs, and if you want to hold capital in europe and not drive it away to the emerging markets abroad.
the amendments introduced by mr gauzès' report are intended to provide further details on the new esma's powers in relation to national bodies. i think the scope of the powers should be very clearly defined. in addition, financial market participants should be able to identify the competent authority in the field of activity of the agencies. i believe that the new european authority should be solely responsible for the registration and supervision of existing credit rating agencies. they should be able to consult information on financial instruments rated by competitors. access to websites should also be granted only if the confidentiality of the information requested can be guaranteed. finally, i would like to stress the importance of the registration of a credit rating agency by a competent authority and its validity throughout the eu.
