in writing. energy efficiency measures are essential if the eu is to achieve its climate change targets. we have a target of reducing energy consumption by 20%, but whereas for the other two targets we have directives that clearly state how the target will be achieved, for energy efficiency there is no such instrument. that is why i insist on the need for an energy efficiency directive. in addition, to achieve the desired results, energy efficiency needs to be promoted at all levels, in all national and european policies. innovation is one of the keys to success in this perspective, which is why i believe that the future research framework programme should make energy efficiency a priority. last but not least, i believe that public authorities need to set an example in this regard and transform the buildings they own into energy efficient buildings. moreover, member states may promote energy efficiency through requirements imposed in public procurement procedures. therefore, priority should be given to undertakings using less polluting technologies. finally, member states may stimulate demand for green products by tax measures or subsidies compatible with the internal market.
in writing. the european union must act to secure its energy future and protect its key energy interests. to this end, the role of energy efficiency measures is critical in ensuring that the climate and energy targets are achieved at the lowest cost. i believe that there is a need to launch broad consultations with local and regional representatives to set out well-defined directions in the field of energy efficiency and to provide support for the development of projects and access to the 9 billion euro made available by the commission through cohesion policy. by using these funds wisely, we will be able to achieve the 20% energy efficiency target, which will greatly contribute to the sustainability and competitiveness objectives in the european union. in addition, reducing consumption through energy efficiency is the most sustainable way to reduce dependence on fossil fuels and will generate a significant reduction in imports (approximately 25-26%).
in writing. – the benefits of reducing energy consumption and dependence in europe would be at once economic, environmental and political. the energy efficiency action plan therefore has far-reaching implications. i was rapporteur for the opinion of the environment committee on the contribution of ict to energy efficiency, and i know that one of the most important tasks here is to facilitate the integration of renewable energy sources into the power supply. smart grids can help to achieve this, whilst smart metering in households can make us conscious of when we can save energy and so help us to reduce consumption. the commission needs to focus properly on these two elements in the action plan, and the member states need to give their full support to installing the infrastructure needed to make it happen, if necessary through public procurement contracts.
on behalf of the alde group. – mr president, i would like to congratulate the rapporteur and the other colleagues who have contributed to this dossier. although it had initially appeared to be a very technical dossier, in the end it was very clear that the political decision would find a solution for this report. there is a need to simplify the acqis communautaire by repealing those directives which contain provisions on means of measurement that are no longer used as a result of technical progress and the use of international standards. the commission’s approach is reasonable. if the mutual recognition principle ensures free movement and no specific barrier exists, then no further additions are needed and the technical specifications should be adopted by the member states. however, the repeal of the directive should not lead to any new barriers to free movement or to additional administrative burdens. we also need to ensure that there will be no gaps between the old directives being repealed and the 2004 directive on measuring instruments. furthermore, the first reading report adopted in the committee on the internal market and consumer protection enabled the inclusion of provisions on the measuring instruments covered by the directives being repealed in the general measurements instruments directive. the member states have been given more time to investigate whether the repealing of the directives will lead to legal uncertainty. the report includes a provision that the commission shall evaluate whether the measuring instruments falling within the scope of the repealed directives need to be included in the scope of the measurements instruments directive. taking account of the fact that a horizontal decision has been also taken regarding correlation tables, together with other shadow rapporteurs i propose to support the text agreed at the first reading with the council.

are still a large number of toys entering the eu market that pose a high risk to the most vulnerable consumers. there are clear signals that the revised toy safety directive needs to be strengthened in order to assure the highest level of protection for our children. we consider that these issues need to be addressed as soon as possible, making sure that there are no loopholes following the implementation of the revised directive. we need to remain focused on toy safety, market surveillance and the prevention of the use of hazardous substances in products specifically designed for in writing. the establishment of the european citizens' initiative proves that bringing the european union closer to its citizens, which was one of the major objectives of the treaty revision process leading to the adoption of the treaty of lisbon, is not just an abstraction. the european citizens' initiative will make a significant contribution to the democratisation of the european political regime by directly connecting citizens of the member states to the european institutions. the parliament's text responds to the need to provide citizens with a simple and easily accessible tool, and the possibility of collecting signatures online shows the adaptation to the reality of today's societies. the initiative will provide european political parties with the opportunity to transform themselves from structures of association of national parties into organisations that mobilise the will of citizens in common projects. the impact of the european citizens' initiative needs to be measured, however, not only at european level but also at national level. indeed, the fact that from now on a minimum of 24 750 romanian citizens will be able to be associated for such an initiative with other citizens from at least one quarter of the member states cannot be separated from another fact, namely that according to the constitution of romania, a minimum of 100 000 romanian citizens are needed for a legislative initiative in a strictly national framework.

in writing. − the citizens' initiative, introduced by the treaty of lisbon, is designed to give citizens the right to participate in the democratic life of the union. its objective is to give citizens a means of making their voices heard by giving them the opportunity to raise a range of issues of interest to the european institutions the difficulties they face in their daily lives and for which they feel they do not receive sufficient attention and support from trade unions, political institutions or other usual interlocutors of the institutions. the initiative will truly create a direct link between citizens and institutions, getting the eu institutions to tackle the concrete issues that matter to citizens. the citizens' initiative is subject to the need to meet certain administrative requirements, but also to respect the eu's fundamental values, among others, ensuring its reliability and efficiency, which are essential for success. the process must be compliant with eu data protection requirements and fully transparent. any organisation, association or even political party will be able to support the citizens' initiatives of their choice, provided that there is full transparency of the support provided, so that signatories know who is behind an initiative they choose to support or not.
in writing. - i voted for the report on the citizens' initiative. the new provisions introduced by the treaty of lisbon enhance participatory democracy and are an important step towards developing civic spirit. european citizens have a 42% trust in the european institutions. one reason could be that few of the european initiatives and policies addressed to european citizens are known by them. this is why the citizens' initiative not only enables european citizens to participate directly in the decision-making process, but also empowers them to contribute to the european agenda. the citizens' initiative will thus bring the major concerns and demands of european citizens to the table of european legislation. the idea is not new. in 2007 we set out to collect 1 million signatures to ask the commission to propose a directive on the integration of people with disabilities into society. at that time, only about 700 000 signatures had been collected, but the legislative proposals were submitted to the european commission. therefore, in order to deliver on our commitment to european citizens, it will be essential to ensure that the demands made through the citizens' initiative are translated into legislation that improves the situation of european citizens.

in writing. − advertising involves unfair practices, invades public and private spaces and makes more target audiences vulnerable. internet advertising has expanded significantly in recent years, currently worth over eur 14 billion in the european market alone. it is important to strengthen european cooperation in combating unfair practices in internet advertising, given the success of the 'sweep' actions (systematic and simultaneous checks of websites by member states), which have so far been limited to three sectors (airline tickets, mobile phone ringers and electronic equipment). these checks should be much more frequent and extended in scope. self-regulation in national markets responds to rapid developments in the advertising sector by focusing on empowering actors and disseminating good practice. self-regulation needs to be encouraged at union level in order to establish a tradition of self-discipline and responsible communication. the european unfair commercial practices directive, which covers aspects of internet advertising in business-to-consumer relationships, has become insufficient, because the field of internet advertising is growing every day. social networks have reached a scale that would have been unthinkable just a few years ago.
in writing. − the report deals with unfair commercial practices in advertising as defined in the unfair commercial practices directive, focusing on issues related to the development of new practices and technologies in advertising, not addressing business-to-business relationships, which are particularly covered by directive 2006/114/ec. advertising is a tool that serves both the internal market, acting as a 'lubricant' of economic activity (stimulating competition, competitiveness, innovation and creativity) and consumers (diversity of choice, lower prices). this is an important economic sector, with internet advertising alone worth over eur 14 billion on the european market. given the lack of information on consumer rights in advertising, there is a need to facilitate access to information and improve transparency. due to the fact that the general public is neither aware of the problems related to the use of personal data nor of the tools available to them to combat them, it is often necessary to launch awareness-raising campaigns on consumer rights in the field of advertising, in particular with regard to the use of personal data, whether voluntarily provided or automatically collected, and to develop educational tools for internet users (e.g. trace management technologies and privacy tools).

madam president, our commitment to a stable self-governing afghanistan, capable of preventing the re-establishment of a terrorist sanctuary there, is strong and long-term, having been reasserted by both the eu and nato. however, precisely because our commitment is a long-term one, i would foresee at least three major challenges. the first is that the kind of state model we provide for afghanistan does not fit the afghan tradition. as the afghans have to adjust, so too do we, helping them to get an achievable state model combining modernity with the afghan tradition. the second challenge is that the security situation might well continue to require our international military involvement beyond 2014, when the afghans will take over. we should be ready seriously to contemplate either extending the deadline or facing the consequences. finally, the third challenge will be provided by the running-out of our public’s patience, which might force us to speed up our present timetable to avoid the alternative of simply declaring victory and going home. that would ruin our credibility.
in writing. the strategy presented and endorsed in lisbon means the gradual transfer, region by region, of control of the area from isaf responsibility to the afghan armed forces. its success depends on how pakistan acts, which is part of the problem and will inevitably be part of the solution. i also don't think we can ignore iran's increasingly obvious involvement in afghanistan. recent events regarding this involvement are disturbing. i believe that this strategy must be accompanied by more important and visible civilian projects that help the development of these regions, where poverty is pervasive and where the presence of isaf and us forces has not produced fundamental changes. we cannot leave behind, after the withdrawal, the same problems that led to the taliban's rise to power in the last decade. i hope this new strategy will work and allow afghanistan to find its peace and balance.
on behalf of the s&d group. – madam president, the nato summit in lisbon has acknowledged the new realities, challenges and non-conventional threats of the post-cold war world. on that basis it has tried to establish a new balance between the alliance’s regional and global involvement. a global nato, or a nato with a global role, is a must. certain consequences are implied. firstly, the european union must prepare itself to assume more responsilities as far as european security and defence are concerned. this means not only developing and updating our european security and defence concept but also developing our military capabilities. secondly, the european union has a duty to prepare itself to face global challenges and to behave like a truly global player. this means that we have to redefine our global interest and targets, and increase our military capacities to an extent which will allow us properly to share the burdens of global defence with our american allies. thirdly, we have a duty to include in our strategies concerning relations with other global players ideas which will lead towards a system of partnership for defence, with capacity for aggregation within a global defensive pact. in coping with all these duties, the european union should not only preserve its strategic connection with nato but should also be able to make its intellectual and political contribution with regard to maintaining nato’s ability to deter, and its ability to defend member states against any aggression, in a context different from the one which determined the birth of the alliance.
on behalf of the alde group. i believe that the lisbon summit is the first summit since 1999 to add to the common good in terms of the alliance's strategic vision. i think what's more important is that in this century, the existing threats, the security interests, but especially the ability of defense budgets to provide effective military solutions are challenging the question of the bipolarity of the world. it was time to make a broad analysis of the direction in which the alliance is heading, and certainly if compatibility with russia is an issue, i would stress that for nato, in my view, compatibility with the european security project is also essential. it seems that the afghan issue has motivated the alliance enough and i'm glad to see that russia has agreed to join nato's efforts in afghanistan. i hope that this complex issue of afghanistan is not one of the reasons for concern for the effective future of this alliance. i also welcome the fact that the european union has raised the question of missile defence technology. i think at the union level we'll have to have a discussion about the effectiveness of this missile shield.
madam president, indeed both the new strategy concept and the summit declaration recognise loudly and clearly that the eu is a major, and therefore indispensible, partner of the alliance. the current international challenges confronting nato and the eu, their simultaneous presence in a number of theatres of action and, moreover, the increasing complementarity between their respective roles require that the relations between the two organisations be strengthened. in that regard, and taking into account the necessary collaboration in theatres of action and – inevitably – the revision of the berlin plus agreements, both organisations expect more concrete results from the discussions between the vice-president of the commission/high representative and the secretary-general, in accordance with their respective mandates and, in that respect, the time has come to be imaginative in finding the right political compromise to allow for an unblocking of the current mechanical deadlock and permit both organisations to achieve their truly collaborative potential.
the lisbon summit has brought a new perspective to the alliance's security strategy. in practice, the three major objectives have been achieved: adoption of the new strategic concept, formulation of a new approach to afghanistan, and relaunching relations with the russian federation. i think the most important result was the integration of the missile shield into the new strategic concept. romania has promoted the placement of the shield since the 2008 bucharest summit. this shows that my country has had the right vision and will contribute significantly to the implementation of the defense system. at the same time, romania supported the open door policy, aimed in particular at strengthening nato relations with georgia and ukraine. i also welcome the fact that nato has reaffirmed the strategic importance of the black sea region, given the security risks that dominate this area. they consist mainly of the existence of frozen conflicts in transnistria and georgia. in this regard, i consider it necessary to maintain the unity of the alliance in our messages to russia. the russian federation must prove its good intentions by taking a substantial responsibility for romania's eastern border and nato. i would like to stress that, through the adopted political declaration, nato has committed itself to the territorial integrity of the republic of moldova and georgia.

on behalf of the ppe group. madam president, madam high representative, i was in côte d'ivoire to lead this eu election observation mission. i would like to start by talking about the courage and commitment of the observers from 26 countries, over 100 people, 120 observers, who were on the ground and did an admirable job. they found, first of all, that ivorian citizens were saying, from all sides: "we are tired". that was the key word, the refrain to say, in fact, that the elections were seen as the end of a political crisis. everyone wanted it to end with this election. there is one exception, the incumbent president, mr gbagbo, who refused to relinquish power and who took the means to prevent the end of this crisis by setting up a partisan constitutional council which simply annulled the results favourable to his opponent. the situation is now that instead of calm, instead of an exit from the crisis, we have an even more complicated crisis, with an equilibrium that was already very fragile and which now leads to the beginning of a confrontation. i would say that it is very, very difficult to avoid confrontation now. we have to look at what happened in the voting in the barracks, in the first round and in the second round. unfortunately, we are faced with a very delicate situation. i would not like to end without expressing my appreciation for the determination of the high representative, for her commitment to the settlement of this matter. i would like to ask him a question - as i have seen that the council has announced that restrictive measures will be adopted shortly - can he say when these restrictive measures will be adopted?
the elections in ivory coast have created an unprecedented situation, with both presidential candidates claiming victory and each appointing a prime minister. there is only one legitimate president, ouattarra. i believe that all political forces must respect the will of the people, as reflected in the election results of november 28. especially since the un, the electoral commission and many european states have recognized the opposition leader as the legitimate winner. it is also regrettable that acts of intimidation were committed against eu observers, which led to the termination of the mission. political instability is already having significant consequences. the african union recently decided to suspend the country from all activities of the organization. in addition, there is a risk of a repeat of the 2002 civil war. the ivory coast can therefore choose between two paths: one of preserving democracy and continuing progress, and the other of isolation from the african community.
today, 16 december, we are celebrating the 240th anniversary of the birth of ludwig van beethoven, the composer of the anthem of a united europe. in virtue of this excellent report of the commission for culture and education, as a romanian historian and writer, i propose as a mark of european heritage an exceptional place, unique in the world st. andrew's cave, located near the danube's outflow into the black sea. as one of the fathers of the christian church, origen, who learned from his father, who in turn learned from the disciples of andrew, says, there, in that little cave in the province of scythia minor, came and spread the light of the gospel the one who had been first called by jesus christ. without a doubt, that is the first christian church in europe. in the first months of 2011 i will take the necessary steps to find community support for a grandiose project. i intend to erect an imposing statue of the savior jesus christ in transylvania, romania, specifically in the brasov area. it will be taller than similar ones in brazil, portugal, and poland, at 130 feet [40 m], and at its base will be a church for weddings, baptisms, and religious services for christendom's great festivals. in the darkness of the future, we will fight and win only under the bright sign of the christian cross.
first of all, i would also like to thank the rapporteur for the very good report she has managed to produce, for the negotiations she has had with the commission and the council. even if it has not succeeded in getting the european union cultural heritage label, the european heritage label is still very good, and the project itself is very good. i am convinced that if it follows the path of the european capital of culture project, it will be a very successful one. it is a very good initiative, especially since it brings together transnational projects. several states are working together to share the same values and the same traditions that they've had for hundreds of years together. i come from a city on the eastern border of the european union, perhaps the largest cultural city on the eastern border, just 10 km from the border, but i've also been to santiago de compostela, practically on the western border of the european union two cultural centers that have a lot in common but also a lot of things that differentiate them. one is an orthodox pilgrimage center, the other a catholic pilgrimage center. we see the values we share best when we go beyond the borders of the european union, when we go to other continents. then we have a very clear picture of the values that we have shared for hundreds of years, that we have a common culture, that we have certain features that differentiate us from other peoples, and the european union cultural heritage label, the european union cultural heritage label, makes sense when we go outside the borders of the european union. i congratulate you once again on this report and i am confident that it will be a successful project.
i welcome the fact that we are voting on the second proposal during this part-session, which aims to bridge the gap between the european union and its citizens. the introduction of the european heritage title, by turning it from an intergovernmental programme in several european countries into an official eu action, strengthens the sense of belonging to the eu, consolidates the recognition of differences and the dialogue between cultures. it raises awareness among citizens, especially young people, of the importance of the role played by the union in european history and in the european symbol system. it can bring our common cultural heritage to the fore. the award will make it easier for young people in particular to visit sites and to make better use of objects that represent our common history. personally, i am particularly pleased with the organisational aspects of the measure. the selection and supervision procedures will be based on common, clear and transparent criteria and the exchange of professional experience will be increased. as an elected representative of a national minority community, i am pleased to note that, for example, in the case of romania, it will be possible to list, on the basis of objective international experts, sites next to the four objects already holding the title, both the teleki tek library in marosvásárhely, which is considered one of the strongholds of hungarian culture, and the black church in brasov, which is considered a reference for the excellence of saxon gothic architecture.
i welcome the transformation of the intergovernmental project on the european heritage label into a formal european union initiative, as the original project did not enjoy the visibility and prestige it deserved. through this project, we also open a door to countries that enrich the culture of our continent without being part of the union. a key point is the revalidation of sites already designated under the intergovernmental agreement, as well as ensuring fairness with regard to states with a different number of sites registered initially. also, where sites are not directly revalidated, it is important that they have the possibility to reapply to give them a better chance. the granting of the heritage label on an indefinite basis, without a periodic reassessment, would help to make more effective use of the reduced budget allocated to the project. the european heritage label will raise public awareness of the diversity of our common cultural heritage and cultural tourism.
creating a european identity and increasing interest in the eu are major challenges. they have the capacity to generate a broad cohesion and solidarity. the european heritage label could fulfil its objectives more effectively if it were managed as a european initiative. it must be based on the same criteria and accompanied by a very well defined monitoring system. this will, among other things, stimulate cultural tourism. as with the unesco world heritage sites, the marche will increase tourist numbers and provide a new impetus to local economies. i welcome the commission's intention to use the european heritage label alongside other instruments designed to create a stronger link between the eu and european citizens. finally, i would like to stress the importance of encouraging intercultural dialogue.

on behalf of the epp group. i'd like to start by quoting some data from an amnesty international study this month, from december 2010. at least 10 000 prisoners and at least 6 000 refugees are flogged every year in malaysia; there is widespread flogging in prisons and mr tannock said that unfortunately malaysia is not the only country where such an anachronistic punishment is applied; indeed singapore is. what is problematic about malaysia, however, is that there is a much higher number of crimes and offenses that are punishable by flogging, to be precise, 66 in malaysia, compared to 30 in singapore. this is not just about violent or sexual crimes but also about drug abuse and, above all, immigration violations. i was concerned, on the other hand, with the perspective that my colleague posselt has embraced, saying that this is torture and that in international law there is this absolute prohibition of torture.
mr president, inflicting physical pain is against human dignity. caning is a gross violation of human rights. it is against the right not to be tortured, but also against the right not to be subject to inhuman and degrading treatment or punishment. in malaysia, over 10 000 people suffer from this form of corporal punishment every year. accounts show that the pain is so great that victims often lose consciousness. reports show that a number of officers carrying out the punishment are eager to accept bribes to spare the victims. therefore, in addition to gross human rights violations, we have government officials committing a crime by taking advantage of people’s suffering. i call upon the commission and the council, as well as on the malay government, to urgently work for an immediate moratorium on the practice of caning, followed by its elimination from the law. beating up people and whipping people on behalf of the government must stop.
i find it regrettable that the practice of flogging has reached such high proportions in malaysia and is on the rise. instead of restricting the practice, the malaysian government encourages it. the authorities make an unfounded argument that flogging is legal and has a considerable effect in curbing criminal activity. furthermore, prison officers receive financial rewards for flogging inmates. estimates confirm a worrying situation: over 6 000 refugees and 10 000 prisoners are victims of this practice every year. i think it's very important that victims who come from outside malaysia have the right to a fair trial. they are currently denied basic services such as interpretation or counselling.
over 10,000 citizens are flogged or whipped annually in malaysia, where the law officially provides for this punishment for 66 offences, the list of which has been expanded in recent years, indicating a worrying trend. in addition to the local victims, foreigners are subjected to numerous and serious abuses, ranging from lack of information and an interpreter to medical ethics violations and the lack of legal assistance. i also call on the european institutions to step up their efforts to abolish this punishment, which is equivalent to torture under international law, and to exert pressure to ensure that the right to an objective and impartial trial is respected in malaysia and that the ill-treatment of migrants and asylum seekers is brought to an end.
on behalf of the ppe group. – mr president, i am alarmed by the use of criminal law against consenting same-sex relations taking place in private. this is already part of ugandan law and the punishment can be life imprisonment. however, the bahati bill would make things even worse. the death penalty could be used, while association and expression of lgbt issues would be effectively banned. the new bill will increase the climate of fear and hostility in a country where persecution of lgbt people is already under way. people would be required to report on each other on privacy matters. the lives of these people will be endangered. human dignity will have no meaning in uganda if such a law is adopted. we must not let this happen.
